嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄕試錄序
國家誕昭文德斂才徵言無遠
邇舉敦化率敎以奉揚
休命歲甲午寔賓興之期巡按
雲南監察御史董珊矢心在
公遵度維寅飭事維預總兵
官黔國公沐紹勛巡撫副都
===
御史胡訓靖綏崇獎士類聿
興巡撫貴州副都御史戴書
都督僉事楊仁巡按御史王
杏皆秉精合德以觀厥成而
行人席大賓以宣
詔適亦駐玆先是前巡按御史楊
東聘考官于列省皆奉愼簡
punctuated:
雲貴鄕試錄序

國家誕昭文德，斂才徵言，無遠邇，舉敦化率敎，以奉揚休命。歲甲午，寔賓興之期。巡按雲南監察御史董珊矢心在公，遵度維寅，飭事維預。總兵官黔國公沐紹勛、巡撫副都御史胡訓靖綏崇獎，士類聿興。巡撫貴州副都御史戴書、都督僉事楊仁、巡按御史王杏，皆秉精合德，以觀厥成。而行人席大賓以宣詔適亦駐玆。先是，前巡按御史楊東聘考官于列省，皆奉愼簡
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination

The state grandly manifests its civil virtue, gathers talent, and solicits counsel. Far and near alike, all strengthen moral transformation and follow its teachings, thereby reverently carrying forth the august commands. The year jiawu [1534] was indeed the appointed time for honoring and advancing worthy men through the examination. Dong Shan, Investigating Censor inspecting Yunnan, devoted himself wholeheartedly to public duty, observing regulations with reverence and making preparations well in advance. Mu Shaoxun, Regional Commander and Duke of Qianguo, and Hu Xun, Grand Coordinator and Vice Censor-in-chief, brought peace and stability and bestowed esteem and encouragement, so that the scholars flourished. Dai Shu, Grand Coordinator of Guizhou and Vice Censor-in-chief; Yang Ren, Assistant Commissioner-in-chief; and Wang Xing, Regional Inspector, all maintained single-minded dedication and united in virtuous purpose to see the undertaking through to completion. Xi Dabin, a Messenger charged with proclaiming an imperial edict, also happened to be staying here. Earlier, Yang Dong, the former Regional Inspector, had sought examiners from the various provinces, where all undertook their selection with care…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以至〔珠〕與教諭張〔澤〕充考試
官尹〔一仁〕趙〔琬〕李〔綽〕文〔大才〕
充同考試官提調則左布政
使張〔峨〕左叅政黃〔祺〕監試則
按察使衞〔道〕僉事辛〔東山〕綜
理防範則右布政使袁〔擯〕右
叅政馬〔侖〕左叅議劉〔彭年〕按
===
察副使鄒〔覯〕車〔純〕僉事劉〔道〕
都指揮僉事馮〔立〕馮〔鳴鳳〕貴
州左布政使周〔忠〕左叅政曾
〔鵬〕按察副使林〔茂竹〕馮〔裕〕陳
〔則清〕僉事康〔世隆〕都指揮僉
事田〔茂〕狄〔遠〕逮百執事則罔
不夙夜肅慎以恊于成右叅
punctuated: 以至〔珠〕與教諭張〔澤〕充考試官，尹〔一仁〕、趙〔琬〕、李〔綽〕、文〔大才〕充同考試官。提調則左布政使張〔峨〕、左叅政黃〔祺〕；監試則按察使衞〔道〕、僉事辛〔東山〕；綜理防範則右布政使袁〔擯〕、右叅政馬〔侖〕、左叅議劉〔彭年〕、按察副使鄒〔覯〕、車〔純〕、僉事劉〔道〕、都指揮僉事馮〔立〕、馮〔鳴鳳〕、貴州左布政使周〔忠〕、左叅政曾〔鵬〕、按察副使林〔茂竹〕、馮〔裕〕、陳〔則清〕、僉事康〔世隆〕、都指揮僉事田〔茂〕、狄〔遠〕。逮百執事，則罔不夙夜肅慎，以恊于成。右叅
translation_en:
…thus Zhu [?] and Zhang Ze, Instructor, served as Examiners. Yin Yiren, Zhao Wan, Li Chuo, and Wen Dacai served as Associate Examiners.

The Proctors were Zhang E, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Huang Qi, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner. Oversight of the examination was entrusted to Wei Dao, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Xin Dongshan, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner.

General management and security were entrusted to Yuan Bin [?], Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Ma Lun, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Liu Pengnian, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zou Gou and Che Chun, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Liu Dao, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; and Feng Li and Feng Mingfeng, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. From Guizhou, these duties were entrusted to Zhou Zhong, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zeng Peng, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Lin Maozhu, Feng Yu, and Chen Zeqing, Provincial Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Kang Shilong, Assistant Provincial Surveillance Commissioner; and Tian Mao and Di Yuan, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners.

Down to all the functionaries, none failed to exercise respectful care morning and night, cooperating to bring the undertaking to completion. The Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
政初〔杲〕右參議華〔金〕副使王
〔閣〕僉事杜〔朝紳〕都指揮僉事
蕭〔嘉〕貴州左參議張〔楠〕則先
期入
賀均與賛襄焉廼合提學副使
陳〔煥〕暨貴州按察使韓〔士英〕
僉事戴〔亢〕所選士一千五百
===
有奇三試之取中式者五十
有五幷錄其名氏與文之優
者以
獻〔珠〕乃進諸士告之曰夫文渾
渾噩噩瀚以充矣衍衍繹繹
翕以布矣煒燁焃爛渙諸物
矣高朗宣融萃諸人矣是故
punctuated:
政初〔杲〕、右參議華〔金〕、副使王〔閣〕、僉事杜〔朝紳〕、都指揮僉事蕭〔嘉〕、貴州左參議張〔楠〕，則先期入賀，均與賛襄焉。廼合提學副使陳〔煥〕暨貴州按察使韓〔士英〕、僉事戴〔亢〕所選士一千五百有奇，三試之，取中式者五十有五，幷錄其名氏與文之優者以獻。
〔珠〕乃進諸士，告之曰：「夫文，渾渾噩噩，瀚以充矣；衍衍繹繹，翕以布矣；煒燁焃爛，渙諸物矣；高朗宣融，萃諸人矣。是故」
translation_en:
…Right Vice Administration Commissioner Chu Gao, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Hua Jin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Ge, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Du Chaoshen, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Xiao Jia, and Guizhou’s Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhang Nan had gone to court ahead of time to offer congratulations; all also contributed their assistance to this undertaking. We then assembled the more than fifteen hundred candidates selected by Education Intendant Chen Huan, who held the rank of Surveillance Vice Commissioner, together with Guizhou Surveillance Commissioner Han Shiying and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Dai Kang. They were examined in three sessions, and fifty-five were selected as successful candidates. Their names, together with the finest of their compositions, were recorded for presentation to the throne.
Zhu then summoned the candidates before him and addressed them: “Cultural patterning, in its primordial wholeness and simplicity, fills the world in its vastness. Unfolding and developing, it spreads in harmonious unity. Brilliant and radiant, it is diffused among the myriad things. Lofty, luminous, expansive, and harmonious, it gathers in human beings. Therefore…”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
上世會道中世昭文汙世狥
物隆世命人文之變也夫雲
貴古泰黔之徼也前世無文
焉然山川物采固有可紀而
薦者矣窿崇蜿蜒山喬而穎
矣澒洞淵澄水順而靜矣齒
角金貝羽罽文石之屬利用
===
於天下者物珍而富矣人皆
曰此泰黔之文而西南之煥
如者也孰知山川之靈運之
氣機物采之華發之寶藏精
秘所積終當應之人文而後
已耳亦何貴於物之文也
皇上光裕大德作新善類
punctuated:
上世會道，中世昭文，汙世狥物，隆世命人，文之變也。夫雲貴，古泰黔之徼也。前世無文焉，然山川物采，固有可紀而薦者矣。窿崇蜿蜒，山喬而穎矣；澒洞淵澄，水順而靜矣；齒角金貝羽罽文石之屬，利用於天下者，物珍而富矣。人皆曰：「此泰黔之文，而西南之煥如者也。」孰知山川之靈，運之氣機；物采之華，發之寶藏。精秘所積，終當應之人文而後已耳。亦何貴於物之文也？
皇上光裕大德，作新善類，
translation_en:
…in highest antiquity, cultural refinement accorded with the Way; in the middle age, it shone forth in patterned expression; in a debased age, it pursued material things; in a flourishing age, it charged men with their calling. These are the transformations of cultural refinement. Yunnan and Guizhou were the ancient borderlands of Tai and Qian [?]. In former ages they possessed no literary culture, yet their mountains, rivers, and splendid natural products certainly offered things worthy of being recorded and presented. Lofty and winding, their mountains rise high with outstanding peaks; vast and deep and clear, their waters flow smoothly and calmly. Ivory, horn, gold, cowries, feathers, woolen fabrics, patterned stones, and the like, useful throughout the realm, are precious and abundant products. Everyone says: “These are the patterned beauties of Tai and Qian [?], the splendors of the southwest.” Who realizes that the spiritual potency of the mountains and rivers is set in motion through the workings of vital energy, and that the brilliance of their natural products emerges from their treasured stores? The accumulated subtle and hidden essences must ultimately find their answering expression in human culture before their work is done. Why, then, prize the patterned beauty of material things alone?
His Majesty has gloriously enlarged his great virtue and renewed men of goodness, …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鴻恩麗澤滂洽海內者十有三
年矣于是兩省逢掖之士咸
祓除振響以揚靈効才於方
嶽之下故茲今日之所薦者
莫非嚮往思奮承休順則之
文渢渢乎可誦可式者矣是
故精深之謂賾鬯達之謂明
===
渾璞之謂醇雋雅之謂則參
伍以變錯綜而通之之謂文
淵乎備矣豈非近被
棫樸菁莪之化遠孕山川物采
之靈毓精會元以闡今日之
郁郁者乎昔者成周三年之
比合六鄉之士考其德行道
punctuated: 鴻恩麗澤滂洽海內者十有三年矣。于是兩省逢掖之士，咸祓除振響，以揚靈効才於方嶽之下。故茲今日之所薦者，莫非嚮往思奮、承休順則之文，渢渢乎可誦可式者矣。是故精深之謂賾，鬯達之謂明，渾璞之謂醇，雋雅之謂則，參伍以變、錯綜而通之之謂文。淵乎備矣！豈非近被棫樸菁莪之化，遠孕山川物采之靈，毓精會元，以闡今日之郁郁者乎？昔者成周三年之比，合六鄉之士，考其德行、道
translation_en:
…His vast favor and beneficent bounty have spread abundantly throughout the realm for thirteen years. Thus the scholars in their broad-sleeved robes throughout the two provinces have all purified themselves and raised their voices, displaying their spirit and offering their talents before the regional authorities. Hence the writings recommended today all express aspiration and determination, acceptance of imperial blessings, and adherence to proper standards. Rich and resonant, they merit both recitation and imitation.

What is profound and penetrating is called abstruse; what is freely expressive is called lucid; what is whole and unhewn is called pure; what is refined and elegant is called exemplary. To vary these through comparison and bring them into coherence through interweaving is called literary accomplishment. How profound and complete it is! Surely this luxuriant flowering today comes from the immediate influence of the transforming instruction celebrated in “The Oak Trees” (Yupu) and “Luxuriant Mugwort” (Jing E), together with the long-nurtured spiritual potency of mountains, rivers, and the splendid products of the land—fostering their essence and gathering their primal energies.

Formerly, under the Zhou, at the triennial assessment, the scholars of the six townships were assembled and examined in their virtue, conduct, and the Way…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
藝者升之天府是以至德薦
士也今胡以文辭爲哉夫文
莫精於德行莫通於道藝君
子擬之後言議之後動脩辭
立誠而天下之理得矣是謂
天下之至文夫至文無聲至
德無文神而明之存乎其人
===
諸士其知所以自勵者詩曰
辭之輯矣民之洽矣辭之懌
矣民之莫矣諸士脩辭以呈
身而敷辭以安民其何事之
弗濟迺若曲學阿世媚辭售
妍怵聲勢而狥人視民如草
菅而莫之恤者是文之厲也
punctuated: 藝者，升之天府，是以至德薦士也。今胡以文辭爲哉？夫文莫精於德行，莫通於道藝。君子擬之後言，議之後動，脩辭立誠，而天下之理得矣。是謂天下之至文。夫至文無聲，至德無文，神而明之，存乎其人。諸士其知所以自勵者！詩曰：「辭之輯矣，民之洽矣；辭之懌矣，民之莫矣。」諸士脩辭以呈身，而敷辭以安民，其何事之弗濟？迺若曲學阿世，媚辭售妍，怵聲勢而狥人，視民如草菅而莫之恤者，是文之厲也。
translation_en: …those examined in the arts of the Way were presented to the imperial repository: this was to recommend men of outstanding virtue for service. Why, then, do we now employ literary composition? Nothing in writing is more refined than moral conduct, and nothing more comprehensive than the arts of the Way. The gentleman considers before speaking and deliberates before acting; he cultivates his language to establish sincerity, and thereby grasps the principles of all under Heaven. This is called the highest literary accomplishment in the world. Yet the highest literary accomplishment has no sound, and the highest virtue has no ornament. To comprehend these with spiritual insight depends upon the person. You scholars should recognize how to spur yourselves onward! The Book of Odes says: “When words are harmonious, the people are united; when words are pleasing, the people are settled.” If you scholars cultivate your language to present yourselves for service and employ it to bring peace to the people, what undertaking could you fail to accomplish? But those who distort learning to flatter the age, use ingratiating words to peddle their elegance, bow in fear before prestige and power and comply with others, and regard the people as mere grass and weeds, showing them no compassion—these are the scourge of literary accomplishment.…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
顧齒角金貝羽罽文石之弗
如矣諸士慎毋忘其初也哉
江西南康府儒學教授黃珠
謹序
punctuated:
顧齒角金貝羽罽文石之弗如矣。諸士慎毋忘其初也哉！

江西南康府儒學教授黃珠謹序。
translation_en:
…would indeed be inferior even to ivory, horn, metal, shells, feathers, woolen fabrics, and patterned stones. You scholars, take care never to forget your original aspirations!

Preface respectfully written by Huang Zhu, Professor of the Prefectural Confucian School of Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi.

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試
監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史董珊〔邦奇陝西膚施縣人丙戌進士〕
提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使張峨〔蜀望四川成都前衛人甲戌進士〕
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參政黃祺〔允吉江西安義縣人甲戌進士〕
監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司按察使衛道〔正夫河南葉縣人甲戌進士〕
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事辛東山〔魯堂河南洛陽縣人舊隷裕州甲戌進士〕
===
考試官
江西南康府儒學教授黃珠〔珎卿福建莆田縣人庚午貢士〕
河南開封府陳州商水縣儒學教諭張澤〔汝厚湖廣黃岡縣人乙酉貢士〕
同考試官
浙江紹興府諸暨縣儒學教諭尹一仁〔任之江西安福縣人戊子貢士〕
河南衛輝府新鄉縣儒學教諭趙珫〔文瑞山西鎮西衛人乙酉貢士〕
浙江金華府永康縣儒學教諭李綽〔汝達廣東南海縣人辛卯貢士〕
江西吉安府泰和縣儒學教諭文大才〔希周湖廣廣濟縣人辛卯貢士〕
印卷官
punctuated:
嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試

監臨官
巡按雲南監察御史董珊〔邦奇，陝西膚施縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官
雲南等處承宣布政使司左布政使張峨〔蜀望，四川成都前衛人，甲戌進士〕。
雲南等處承宣布政使司左參政黃祺〔允吉，江西安義縣人，甲戌進士〕。

監試官
雲南等處提刑按察司按察使衛道〔正夫，河南葉縣人，甲戌進士〕。
雲南等處提刑按察司僉事辛東山〔魯堂，河南洛陽縣人，舊隷裕州，甲戌進士〕。

考試官
江西南康府儒學教授黃珠〔珎卿，福建莆田縣人，庚午貢士〕。
河南開封府陳州商水縣儒學教諭張澤〔汝厚，湖廣黃岡縣人，乙酉貢士〕。

同考試官
浙江紹興府諸暨縣儒學教諭尹一仁〔任之，江西安福縣人，戊子貢士〕。
河南衛輝府新鄉縣儒學教諭趙珫〔文瑞，山西鎮西衛人，乙酉貢士〕。
浙江金華府永康縣儒學教諭李綽〔汝達，廣東南海縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
江西吉安府泰和縣儒學教諭文大才〔希周，湖廣廣濟縣人，辛卯貢士〕。

印卷官
translation_en:
Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination, thirteenth year of Jiajing (1534)

Supervising Official
Dong Shan, Investigating Censor on inspection duty in Yunnan. His courtesy name was Bangqi; he was from Fushi County, Shaanxi, and was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.

Proctors
Zhang E, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Shuwang; he was from Chengdu Front Guard, Sichuan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.
Huang Qi, Left Administration Vice Commissioner of the Yunnan Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Yunji; he was from Anyi County, Jiangxi, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Examination Overseers
Wei Dao, Surveillance Commissioner of the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Zhengfu; he was from Ye County, Henan, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.
Xin Dongshan, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Yunnan Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was LUTang [Lutang]; he was from Luoyang County, Henan, formerly registered in Yuzhou, and was a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.

Examiners
Huang Zhu, Professor in the Confucian School of Nankang Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Zhenqing; he was from Putian County, Fujian, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the gengwu year.
Zhang Ze, Instructor in the Confucian School of Shangshui County, Chenzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Ruhou; he was from Huanggang County, Huguang, and was a tribute student of the yiyou year.

Associate Examiners
Yin Yiren, Instructor in the Confucian School of Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Renzhi; he was from Anfu County, Jiangxi, and was a tribute student of the wuzi year.
Zhao Chong, Instructor in the Confucian School of Xinxiang County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Wenrui; he was from Zhenxi Guard, Shanxi, and was a tribute student of the yiyou year.
Li Chuo, Instructor in the Confucian School of Yongkang County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Ruda; he was from Nanhai County, Guangdong, and was a tribute student of the xinmao year.
Wen Dacai, Instructor in the Confucian School of Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. His courtesy name was Xizhou; he was from Guangji County, Huguang, and was a tribute student of the xinmao year.

也中孚以利貞乃應乎天也
極天下之賾者存乎卦鼓天下之動者存
乎辭化而裁之存乎變推而行之存乎
通神而明之存乎其人默而成之不言
而信存乎德行
天地之道貞觀者也
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝
以義制事以禮制心
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子曰：「君子道者三，我無能焉：仁者不憂，知者不惑，勇者不懼。」子貢曰：「夫子自道也。」

尊賢則不惑。

友也者，友其德也，不可以有挾也。

易

大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。

豚魚吉，信及豚魚也。利涉大川，乘木舟虛也。中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。

極天下之賾者存乎卦，鼓天下之動者存乎辭，化而裁之存乎變，推而行之存乎通，神而明之存乎其人，默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。

天地之道，貞觀者也。

書

文命敷于四海，祗承于帝。

以義制事，以禮制心。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Confucius said: “There are three aspects to the way of the gentleman, none of which I can attain: the benevolent are free from anxiety, the wise from confusion, and the courageous from fear.” Zigong said: “The Master is describing himself.”

“Honor the worthy, and you will not be confused.”

“To befriend someone is to befriend his virtue; one must not rely on advantages of one's own.”

Book of Changes

“Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure and unalloyed, it is the essence of excellence.”

“‘Good fortune with piglets and fish’: sincerity reaches even piglets and fish. ‘It is beneficial to cross the great river’: one rides in a wooden boat with a hollow interior. In Zhongfu (Inner Sincerity), benefit comes through steadfast correctness; thus it accords with Heaven.”

“To fathom the intricacies of all under Heaven depends on the hexagrams; to stir all movements under Heaven depends on the statements. Transformation and its proper regulation depend on change; extension and practical application depend on free passage. To comprehend these things with spirit-like insight depends on the right person; to accomplish them silently and command trust without speaking depends on virtuous conduct.”

“The way of Heaven and Earth is displayed through constancy.”

Book of Documents

“His civilizing teachings spread throughout the Four Seas, and he reverently served the emperor.”

“Regulate affairs by righteousness; regulate the heart by ritual propriety.”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
王拜手稽首曰公不敢不敬天之休來相
宅其作周匹休公旣定宅伻來來視予
卜休恒吉我二人共貞公其以予萬億
年敬天之休拜手稽首誨言
今爾罔不由慰日勤爾罔或戒不勤
詩
樹之榛栗椅桐梓漆爰伐琴瑟
湛湛露斯在彼杞棘顯允君子莫不令德
其桐其椅其實離離豈弟君子莫不令
===
儀
民之靡盈誰夙知而莫成
載穫濟濟有實其積萬億及秭
春秋
秋八月庚辰公及戎盟于唐〔隱公二年〕
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊公十有三年〕
秋七月辛巳豹及諸侯之
大夫盟于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕
冬晉人執虞公〔僖公五年〕
punctuated:
王拜手稽首曰：「公！不敢不敬天之休。來相宅，其作周匹休。公旣定宅，伻來，來視予卜休恒吉。我二人共貞。公其以予萬億年敬天之休。」拜手稽首誨言。
今爾罔不由慰日勤，爾罔或戒不勤。

詩
樹之榛栗，椅桐梓漆，爰伐琴瑟。
湛湛露斯，在彼杞棘。顯允君子，莫不令德。其桐其椅，其實離離。豈弟君子，莫不令儀。
民之靡盈，誰夙知而莫成？
載穫濟濟，有實其積，萬億及秭。

春秋
秋八月庚辰，公及戎盟于唐〔隱公二年〕。
春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏〔莊公十有三年〕。
秋七月辛巳，豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕。
冬，晉人執虞公〔僖公五年〕。
translation_en:
The king bowed with his hands together and touched his forehead to the ground, saying: “Duke! I dare not fail to revere Heaven’s favor. You have come to inspect the site for the capital, thereby securing for Zhou a blessing matching Heaven’s. Having settled the site, you sent a messenger to show me that the divination was favorable and consistently auspicious. Let us two together uphold what is right. May you help me revere Heaven’s favor for ten thousand million years.” He bowed with his hands together and touched his forehead to the ground in acknowledgment of the instructive words.
Now, let none of you fail to grow daily more diligent through encouragement; let none of you remain idle when admonished.

Book of Odes
Plant hazel and chestnut, and yi trees, paulownias, catalpas, and lacquer trees; in due course fell them to make qin and se zithers.
Heavy lies the dew upon those wolfberry bushes and thorn trees. The illustrious and trustworthy gentlemen all possess excellent virtue. Those paulownias and yi trees bear fruit in abundant clusters. The joyful and easygoing gentlemen all possess excellent deportment.
The people are never perfect: who understands early yet fails to attain maturity later?
They gather the harvest in throngs; full indeed are their heaps, in myriads upon myriads, reaching an immense number.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, in the eighth month, on the gengchen day, the duke made a covenant with the Rong at Tang. 〔Second year of Duke Yin.〕
In spring, the Marquis of Qi and representatives of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the xinsi day, Bao and the great officers of the various feudal lords made a covenant at Song. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
In winter, men of Jin seized the Duke of Yu. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
城中城〔成公九年〕
禮記
博聞強識而讓敦善行而不怠謂之君子
命有司爲民祈祀山川百源大雩帝用盛
樂乃命百縣雩祀百辟卿士有益於民
者以祈穀實
事君以自顯也
夫樂者先王之所以飾喜也軍旅鈇鉞者
先王之所以飾怒也故先王之喜怒皆
===
得其儕焉喜則天下和之怒則暴亂者
畏之先王之道禮樂可謂盛矣
第貳場
論
脩己以安百姓
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢文帝舉賢良方正能直言極諫者詔
〔二年〕
擬唐以孫伏伽爲治書侍御史誥〔武德元〕
punctuated:
城中城。〔成公九年〕

禮記
博聞強識而讓，敦善行而不怠，謂之君子。
命有司爲民祈祀山川百源，大雩帝，用盛樂。乃命百縣雩祀百辟卿士有益於民者，以祈穀實。
事君以自顯也。
夫樂者，先王之所以飾喜也；軍旅鈇鉞者，先王之所以飾怒也。故先王之喜怒，皆得其儕焉。喜則天下和之，怒則暴亂者畏之。先王之道，禮樂可謂盛矣。

第貳場
論
脩己以安百姓。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢文帝舉賢良方正能直言極諫者詔。〔二年〕
擬唐以孫伏伽爲治書侍御史誥。〔武德元〕
translation_en:
The inner city was fortified. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng.〕

Book of Rites
One who is widely learned and has a strong memory, yet remains modest, and who earnestly practices good conduct without flagging, is called a gentleman.
Order the responsible officials to offer prayers and sacrifices on behalf of the people to the mountains, rivers, and all sources of water, and to perform the great rain sacrifice to the Supreme Lord, employing grand music. Then order the hundred districts to offer rain sacrifices to former rulers, ministers, and officers who benefited the people, praying for grain to ripen.
One serves one's ruler in order to make one's own worth manifest.
Music was the means by which the former kings gave fitting expression to joy; armies and battle-axes were the means by which they gave fitting expression to anger. Thus the joy and anger of the former kings each found its appropriate expression. When they rejoiced, all under Heaven joined in harmony with them; when they were angry, the violent and rebellious feared them. In the Way of the former kings, ritual and music may indeed be called fully developed.

Second Session
Discourse
Cultivate oneself so as to bring peace to the common people.

Edicts, Proclamations of Appointment, and Memorials 〔One topic within this category [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Wen of the Han calling for the recommendation of worthy, good, upright, and principled men capable of speaking frankly and remonstrating unreservedly. 〔Second year.〕
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Sun Fujia as Censor for Judicial Review. 〔First year of the Wude era …〕

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
〔年〕
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表〔元祐元〕
〔年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
荒蕪田地
服舍違式
優恤軍屬
聽訟迴避
===
第叄塲
策五道
問帝王之治本諸學帝王之學本諸心堯
舜禹湯文武之治蕩蕩巍巍弗可尚已
一皆本之心學以見之事功者其曰人
心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
者羣聖傳心致治之要法也降及嬴秦
無論焉漢高帝不事詩書然恢濶大度
事多暗合于古人唐太宗不及禮樂而
punctuated:
〔年〕
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表〔元祐元〕〔年〕。
判語〔五條〕：官吏給由；荒蕪田地；服舍違式；優恤軍屬；聽訟迴避。

第叄塲
策五道
問：帝王之治本諸學，帝王之學本諸心。堯舜禹湯文武之治，蕩蕩巍巍，弗可尚已，一皆本之心學以見之事功者。其曰「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中」者，羣聖傳心致治之要法也。降及嬴秦，無論焉。漢高帝不事詩書，然恢濶大度，事多暗合于古人。唐太宗不及禮樂，而
translation_en:
… year.

Draft a memorial of thanks for the Song appointment of Cheng Yi as Expositor in the Chongzheng Hall. [First year of Yuanyou.]

Legal judgments [five topics]: Issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks; uncultivated farmland; clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed regulations; preferential relief for military dependents; recusal in hearing lawsuits.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The governance of emperors and kings is rooted in learning, and their learning is rooted in the mind. The governance of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu was so vast and lofty that it could not be surpassed. In every case, it was rooted in the learning of the mind and manifested in practical achievements. The saying, “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded; sincerely hold fast to the mean,” expresses the essential method by which the sages transmitted the teaching of the mind and achieved good governance. Coming down to the Qin dynasty of the Ying house, we need not discuss it. Emperor Gao of Han did not devote himself to the Odes and Documents, yet he was broad-minded and magnanimous, and his actions often unwittingly accorded with those of the ancients. Emperor Taizong of Tang fell short in rites and music, yet …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
好賢納諫駸駸乎熈皡之風焉宋太祖
陽施陰搆事亦譎矣然崇儒重道卒致
乾德開寶之治是三君者果天資之美
不學而能歟抑有得於心學之助歟我
太祖高皇帝丕顯之謨
太宗文皇帝丕承之烈直與二帝三王之治並
稱矣其在當時大廷便殿老臣宿儒相
與從容咨訪莫非精一執中之道觀心
有亭洪範有註論正心之章正而確揭
===
明德之典簡而明其法天運精育神復
命之道一皆心學之傳淵乎微矣然亦
可得而悉言歟我
皇上御極十有三年勵精圖治明物察倫仁孝
誠敬之道直接乎精一執中之傳其所
以脩之深宮而見之大廷以達之天下
者煥若日星則又與我
聖祖神宗其道固脗合而無間者也諸士子能
敬陳而三嘆之歟抑以觀仰
punctuated: 好賢納諫，駸駸乎熈皡之風焉。宋太祖陽施陰搆，事亦譎矣；然崇儒重道，卒致乾德、開寶之治。是三君者，果天資之美，不學而能歟？抑有得於心學之助歟？我太祖高皇帝丕顯之謨、太宗文皇帝丕承之烈，直與二帝三王之治並稱矣。其在當時，大廷便殿，老臣宿儒，相與從容咨訪，莫非精一執中之道。觀心有亭，洪範有註，論正心之章正而確，揭明德之典簡而明。其法天、運精、育神、復命之道，一皆心學之傳，淵乎微矣！然亦可得而悉言歟？我皇上御極十有三年，勵精圖治，明物察倫，仁孝誠敬之道，直接乎精一執中之傳。其所以脩之深宮而見之大廷，以達之天下者，煥若日星，則又與我聖祖神宗，其道固脗合而無間者也。諸士子能敬陳而三嘆之歟？抑以觀仰
translation_en:
…he esteemed worthy men and accepted remonstrance, steadily approaching the spirit of radiant harmony. Song Taizu acted openly while plotting secretly; his conduct, too, was deceptive. Yet he honored Confucian scholars and esteemed the Way, ultimately bringing about the good government of the Qiande and Kaibao reign periods. Did these three rulers truly possess such excellent natural endowments that they could achieve this without learning? Or did they benefit from the assistance of learning concerning the mind?

The illustrious plans of our Taizu, the Gao Emperor, and the achievements of our Taizong, the Wen Emperor, in magnificently carrying on his legacy rank alongside the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. In their time, whether in the great court or the private halls, they consulted senior ministers and seasoned Confucian scholars at leisure. These consultations concerned nothing other than the Way of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean. For contemplating the mind there was a pavilion; for the Great Plan there was a commentary. The essay discussing the rectification of the mind was sound and precise; the text elucidating luminous virtue was concise and clear. Their methods of modeling themselves on Heaven, circulating vital essence, nourishing the spirit, and returning to the source of life all belonged to the transmission of learning concerning the mind. How profound and subtle! Yet can these matters be fully expounded?

Our Emperor has occupied the throne for thirteen years, devoting his energies to good government, discerning things and examining human relationships. His Way of benevolence, filial piety, sincerity, and reverence directly continues the transmission of refinement, single-mindedness, and holding fast to the mean. What he cultivates deep within the palace, manifests in the great court, and extends throughout the realm shines like the sun and stars. His Way assuredly accords without the slightest gap with that of our sagely and divine imperial ancestors. Can you candidates respectfully expound this and repeatedly voice your admiration? Further, thereby to observe and look up to …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖明心之學
問太平作樂所以和神人合上下六律調
而後五音正理固然也周禮謂樂六變
則天神皆降八變則地祇皆出九變則
人鬼可享其變法可得聞歟漢書以五
音配於五行而考其德月令以六律分
於五方而應其時或謂呂有上生而無
下生又謂納音不同於納甲其詳可得
言歟太簇一也天以為徵地以為角姑
===
洗一也地以為徵天以為羽其義果何
用歟圜丘樂有圜鍾方澤樂有函鍾其
名何以異三鍾之變皆會于卯其意何
以同唐無徵音說者謂李嗣真求得於
弩營之中宋無商聲說者謂蔡元定惡
其有陵君之象然歟否歟鄭譯條從相
生為八十四調元稹宮調改革為八十
一調是歟非歟樂記所稱君臣民事物
咸寓於音亂則有殃樂元語所記四夷
punctuated:
聖明心之學。

問：太平作樂，所以和神人、合上下。六律調而後五音正，理固然也。《周禮》謂樂六變則天神皆降，八變則地祇皆出，九變則人鬼可享，其變法可得聞歟？《漢書》以五音配於五行而考其德，《月令》以六律分於五方而應其時。或謂呂有上生而無下生，又謂納音不同於納甲，其詳可得言歟？太簇一也，天以為徵，地以為角；姑洗一也，地以為徵，天以為羽，其義果何用歟？圜丘樂有圜鍾，方澤樂有函鍾，其名何以異？三鍾之變皆會于卯，其意何以同？唐無徵音，說者謂李嗣真求得於弩營之中；宋無商聲，說者謂蔡元定惡其有陵君之象，然歟否歟？鄭譯條從相生為八十四調，元稹宮調改革為八十一調，是歟非歟？《樂記》所稱君臣民事物，咸寓於音，亂則有殃。《樂元語》所記四夷
translation_en:
…the sagely sovereign’s learning of the mind.

Question: Music is created in an age of great peace to bring spirits and human beings into harmony and unite those above and below. Only after the six pitch standards are attuned are the five notes correct: this is certainly the principle. The Rites of Zhou states that after six transformations of the music, all celestial spirits descend; after eight transformations, all terrestrial spirits emerge; and after nine transformations, the spirits of the dead may receive offerings. May we hear how these transformations work? The History of the Han pairs the five notes with the Five Phases and examines their qualities; the Monthly Ordinances distributes the six pitch standards among the five directions so that they correspond to their seasons. Some say that the lü pitches permit upward generation but not downward generation, and that assigning sounds to the cyclical signs (nayin) differs from assigning the heavenly stems to the trigrams (najia). Can you explain these matters in detail? Taicu is a single pitch, yet Heaven takes it as zhi and Earth as jue; Guxian is a single pitch, yet Earth takes it as zhi and Heaven as yu. What significance do these distinctions actually have? The music of the Circular Mound includes Huanzhong, while that of the Square Pool includes Hanzhong. Why do their names differ? The transformations of the three zhong pitch standards all converge at mao: why do they share this significance? The Tang lacked the zhi note, and commentators say that Li Sizhen recovered it in a crossbow camp. The Song lacked the shang note, and commentators say that Cai Yuanding disliked its implication of encroaching upon the ruler. Is this so or not? Zheng Yi arranged successive pitch generation [?] to produce eighty-four modes, while Yuan Zhen reformed the gong modes to produce eighty-one modes. Were these correct or incorrect? The ruler, ministers, people, affairs, and things mentioned in the Record of Music are all embodied in the notes; when they become disordered, calamity follows. As for the four foreign peoples recorded in Sayings on the Origins of Music (Yue yuanyu)…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
制樂曰䟽禁昧離皆先王所作以順天
時亦必有說矣願詳言之以見考古之
學
問漢人尚評晉人尚駁皆私議也今與諸
士秉公議以尚論古人可乎漢高帝懲
亡秦孤立之失大封同姓及異姓功臣
以分制疆宇周以固矣然未及數世而
功臣徹侯誅戮殆盡至哀平之世中外
俱弱不可支持議者以漢有呂新之禍
===
多歸咎於外戚不知所以致此者果外
戚歟抑別有故歟唐太宗承亡隋極亂
之後大振乾綱以成不世之功宏以遠
矣然未及數世而政權下移國祚日傾
逮僖昭之世冠履倒置不可救藥議者
以唐有安朱之禍多歸咎於藩鎮不知
所以致此者果藩鎮歟抑別有故歟宋
藝祖厭五季兵戈之亂釋兵權戒殺戮
以安天下之民厚而仁矣然未及中葉
punctuated:
制樂曰䟽、禁、昧、離，皆先王所作，以順天時，亦必有說矣。願詳言之，以見考古之學。

問：漢人尚評，晉人尚駁，皆私議也。今與諸士秉公議，以尚論古人，可乎？漢高帝懲亡秦孤立之失，大封同姓及異姓功臣，以分制疆宇，周以固矣。然未及數世，而功臣徹侯誅戮殆盡；至哀平之世，中外俱弱，不可支持。議者以漢有呂新之禍，多歸咎於外戚。不知所以致此者，果外戚歟？抑別有故歟？唐太宗承亡隋極亂之後，大振乾綱，以成不世之功，宏以遠矣。然未及數世，而政權下移，國祚日傾；逮僖昭之世，冠履倒置，不可救藥。議者以唐有安朱之禍，多歸咎於藩鎮。不知所以致此者，果藩鎮歟？抑別有故歟？宋藝祖厭五季兵戈之亂，釋兵權，戒殺戮，以安天下之民，厚而仁矣。然未及中葉
translation_en:
…established music called Shu, Jin, Mei, and Li, all created by the former kings to accord with Heaven’s seasons: surely there must also be an explanation for this. Please explain in detail, demonstrating your learning in the investigation of antiquity.

Question: Men of the Han prized appraisal, and men of the Jin prized rebuttal; these were all private judgments. May we now join you gentlemen in maintaining impartial judgment to assess the men of antiquity? Emperor Gao of the Han, taking warning from the fallen Qin’s mistake of standing isolated, extensively enfeoffed members of his own clan and meritorious subjects of other surnames, dividing control of the realm among them. His arrangements were comprehensive and secure. Yet within only a few generations, the meritorious subjects holding the rank of marquis had almost all been executed. By the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping, both the central government and the regions were weak, and the dynasty could no longer sustain itself. Those discussing the calamities brought upon the Han by the Lü clan and the Xin dynasty mostly blame imperial relatives by marriage. But were imperial relatives by marriage truly the cause, or was there some other reason?

Emperor Taizong of the Tang succeeded to the aftermath of the utter disorder of the fallen Sui. He vigorously asserted imperial authority and accomplished achievements rare in any age. His undertaking was grand and far-reaching. Yet within only a few generations, political power had passed into subordinate hands, and the dynasty’s fortunes declined daily. By the reigns of Emperors Xizong and Zhaozong, caps and shoes had exchanged places—the hierarchy was inverted—and the situation was beyond remedy. Those discussing the calamities brought upon the Tang by An Lushan and Zhu Wen mostly blame the regional military commands. But were the regional military commands truly the cause, or was there some other reason?

The founding emperor of the Song, abhorring the warfare and disorder of the Five Dynasties, relieved commanders of their military powers and enjoined restraint in killing, thereby bringing peace to the people of the realm. His policies were generous and humane. Yet before the dynasty had reached its middle period…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而徽欽北狩高宗南遷逮至理度之季
大勢已去而竟不可支矣議者以宋有
金元之禍多歸咎於夷狄不知所以致
此者果夷狄歟抑別有故歟我
聖祖繼天立極創業垂統其宏綱大要以貽謀
後世者至精至備真能超三軼五而萬
世可行矣故外戚無干政也藩鎮無專
制也夷狄無驕橫也恩威行而情法盡
烏有漢唐宋末流之弊哉然天下之事
===
變每生於意料之所弗及而防微杜漸
尤臣子事君之至情今諸士幸際
聖明正忠言讜論得以自陳之日也其漢唐宋
致釁之由與我
國家今日所以持盈保治以衍億萬年無疆
之休者願詳言之毋隱
問象數之學其來尚矣近世考曆者或推
測之未精而談數者多粗迹之是務故
不能無可質者夫歲差之說古有之矣
punctuated:
而徽欽北狩，高宗南遷，逮至理度之季，大勢已去，而竟不可支矣。議者以宋有金元之禍，多歸咎於夷狄，不知所以致此者果夷狄歟？抑別有故歟？我聖祖繼天立極，創業垂統，其宏綱大要以貽謀後世者，至精至備，真能超三軼五，而萬世可行矣。故外戚無干政也，藩鎮無專制也，夷狄無驕橫也，恩威行而情法盡，烏有漢唐宋末流之弊哉？然天下之事變，每生於意料之所弗及，而防微杜漸，尤臣子事君之至情。今諸士幸際聖明，正忠言讜論得以自陳之日也。其漢唐宋致釁之由，與我國家今日所以持盈保治，以衍億萬年無疆之休者，願詳言之，毋隱。

問：象數之學，其來尚矣。近世考曆者，或推測之未精，而談數者，多粗迹之是務，故不能無可質者。夫歲差之說，古有之矣。
translation_en:
…yet Huizong and Qinzong were taken north as captives, and Gaozong moved south. By the closing years of the reigns of Lizong and Duzong, the overall situation was already lost, and the dynasty ultimately could no longer sustain itself. Those who discuss the disasters inflicted upon the Song by the Jin and Yuan mostly lay the blame on the foreign peoples. But was it truly these peoples who brought this about, or was there some other cause?

Our sagely founder succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, founded the dynasty and handed down its rule. The broad principles and essential provisions through which he planned for later generations were supremely refined and complete. They truly surpassed those of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and could be put into practice for ten thousand generations. Thus imperial relatives by marriage do not interfere in government, regional military governors do not exercise independent power, and foreign peoples do not act with arrogant impunity. Benevolence and authority are exercised, and full account is taken of human circumstances and the law. How could there be the abuses that afflicted the declining years of the Han, Tang, and Song? Yet upheavals in the realm often arise beyond the reach of anticipation. To guard against the slightest signs of trouble and arrest its gradual growth is above all an expression of the utmost devotion with which a subject serves his ruler. You gentlemen are fortunate now to live under a sagely and enlightened sovereign: this is precisely the time when you may personally present loyal words and forthright arguments. Explain in detail, concealing nothing, the causes that brought calamity upon the Han, Tang, and Song, and the means by which our state today may preserve its flourishing condition and good order, extending its boundless blessings for countless millions of years.

Question: The study of images and numbers has a long history. In recent times, some who investigate calendars have lacked precision in their calculations, while those who discuss numbers mostly concern themselves only with superficial manifestations. Thus there are inevitably matters requiring examination. The theory of annual precession has existed since antiquity…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
顓帝曆者實統宗會元之法宋熈寧中
用之不驗乃改正月建寅爲建丑以日
短星昴爲日短星東壁而更定新曆然
則洛下閎所謂八百年差一算者果相
合否乎唐大衍曆者得歩歲候氣之詳
宋皇祐中行之不合乃改閏十二月爲
閏正月移立春晷景爲立冬而造奉元
曆然則向子信所記八十年差一度者
又相合否乎占候之失古亦有之矣或
===
謂下漏家常患冬月水澁夏月水利以
爲水性之常又疑氷澌所壅萬方理之
終不應法然則得其傳者必有所據矣
或謂一日之氣卽其短長播爲刻分至
交一氣則頓易刻裏黃道觚而不圓縱
有强爲數以歩之者亦非乗理用算然
則盡其妙者必有可考矣若歲運又有
主氣客氣之分天月亦有二道九道之
異十二辰而有天時人事之別二十八
punctuated: 顓帝曆者，實統宗會元之法。宋熈寧中，用之不驗，乃改正月建寅爲建丑，以日短星昴爲日短星東壁，而更定新曆。然則洛下閎所謂八百年差一算者，果相合否乎？唐大衍曆者，得歩歲候氣之詳。宋皇祐中，行之不合，乃改閏十二月爲閏正月，移立春晷景爲立冬，而造奉元曆。然則向子信所記八十年差一度者，又相合否乎？占候之失，古亦有之矣。或謂下漏家常患冬月水澁、夏月水利，以爲水性之常，又疑氷澌所壅，萬方理之，終不應法。然則得其傳者，必有所據矣。或謂一日之氣，卽其短長播爲刻分，至交一氣，則頓易刻裏，黃道觚而不圓，縱有强爲數以歩之者，亦非乗理用算。然則盡其妙者，必有可考矣。若歲運，又有主氣、客氣之分；天月亦有二道、九道之異；十二辰而有天時、人事之別；二十八
translation_en:
The calendar of Emperor Zhuan is in fact a method for unifying the fundamental cycles and aligning the epochs [?]. During the Xining era of the Song, its use failed to accord with observations. Accordingly, the first month was changed from association with the branch yin to association with chou, and “at the shortest day, the culminating star is Mao” was changed to “at the shortest day, the culminating star is Dongbi”; a new calendar was then established. Does this actually agree with what Luoxia Hong called a discrepancy of one calculation unit every eight hundred years?

The Tang Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li) provided detailed methods for calculating the year and observing the seasonal qi. During the Huangyou era of the Song, its application failed to accord with observations. Accordingly, an intercalary twelfth month was changed to an intercalary first month, the gnomon shadow assigned to the Beginning of Spring was reassigned to the Beginning of Winter, and the Upholding the Origin Calendar (Fengyuan li) was produced. Does this, in turn, agree with the discrepancy of one degree every eighty years recorded by Xiang Zixin?

Errors in celestial observation and prognostication also existed in antiquity. Some say that keepers of water clocks have always been troubled by sluggish water flow in winter and rapid flow in summer. They regard this as the normal nature of water, yet also suspect obstruction by floating ice. Though they try every means of regulating it, it ultimately fails to conform to the prescribed standards. Those who have received the transmitted methods must therefore have some basis for their practice.

Some say that, for the qi of a given day, its length is apportioned into ke and fractions of a ke; when a new solar term begins, the graduations are abruptly changed [?], making the ecliptic angular rather than circular. Even if someone forces numerical values upon it to calculate its course, this is still not calculation in accordance with underlying principles. Those who fully comprehend its subtleties must therefore have something that can be examined.

As for the annual cycles, there is also a distinction between host qi and guest qi; for heaven and the moon [?], there is likewise a difference between two paths and nine paths. The twelve branches distinguish celestial timing from human affairs; the twenty-eight…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
宿而有三十三度十七度半之殊其詳
可得聞歟天運之周有行黃道之裏者
有行黃道之外者有行黃道之上者有
行黃道之下者有循度者有失度者有
犯經星者有犯客星者其義果何謂歟
有推步日蝕而知其强弱之限有占測
雨候而得其晦暘之宜有增六十甲子
而成上壽之數有獻九卷新曆而更乾
元之制者其人之得失可悉言歟渾儀
===
渾象之制何以不同韓顯符舒易簡之
造孰爲詳略馮相保章分職也至何時
而兼太史占候兼官也至何時而分若
有以祝融之功而推楚之治以虞舜之
德而占陳之存其有關於世道亦大矣
幸盡言之毋忽
問雲南乃古秦黔之地遠在邊徼控御惟
難自我
聖祖龍興混一區宇懷遠爲近一以中國治之
punctuated:
宿而有三十三度、十七度半之殊，其詳可得聞歟？天運之周，有行黃道之裏者，有行黃道之外者，有行黃道之上者，有行黃道之下者，有循度者，有失度者，有犯經星者，有犯客星者，其義果何謂歟？有推步日蝕而知其强弱之限，有占測雨候而得其晦暘之宜，有增六十甲子而成上壽之數，有獻九卷新曆而更乾元之制者，其人之得失可悉言歟？渾儀、渾象之制何以不同？韓顯符、舒易簡之造孰爲詳略？馮相、保章分職也，至何時而兼？太史占候兼官也，至何時而分？若有以祝融之功而推楚之治，以虞舜之德而占陳之存，其有關於世道亦大矣。幸盡言之，毋忽。

問：雲南乃古秦黔之地，遠在邊徼，控御惟難。自我聖祖龍興，混一區宇，懷遠爲近，一以中國治之。
translation_en:
…among the lunar lodges there are differences in extent, some spanning thirty-three degrees and others seventeen and a half degrees. May we hear the details? In the circuit of celestial motion, some bodies travel inside the ecliptic, some outside it, some above it, and some below it; some follow their prescribed courses, while others depart from them; some encroach upon fixed stars, while others encroach upon guest stars. What, precisely, do these things signify? Some have calculated solar eclipses and determined the limits of their greater or lesser magnitude; some have predicted rainy conditions and ascertained the proper alternation of overcast and sunny weather; some have added a sixty-year sexagenary cycle to arrive at the number of years constituting an exceptional lifespan; and some have presented a new calendar in nine scrolls, replacing the Qianyuan system. Can you explain fully the successes and errors of these men? How do the designs of the armillary sphere and celestial globe differ? Of the instruments made by Han Xianfu and Shu Yijian, which were more detailed and which less so? The functions of the Directors of Astronomy and Astrology were separate: when were they combined? Astronomical observation and prognostication were combined under the Grand Astrologer: when were they separated? As for inferring the governance of Chu from the achievements of Zhurong, or predicting the survival of Chen from the virtue of Yu Shun, these matters also have great bearing upon the course of human affairs. Please discuss them fully and neglect nothing.

Question: Yunnan is the land of ancient Qin and Qian [?], situated far away on the frontier and especially difficult to control. Since our sagely founder rose like a dragon and unified the realm, he brought distant peoples close through conciliation and governed them entirely according to the practices of the Central Kingdom…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
法至備矣奈何承平既久玩愒日滋亦
有當思患而預防者何也夫狼子野心
賓貢愆度土酋之桀驁甚矣未聞有懾
而震之者豈不犯無武之戒生計蕭條
賦役繁重土軍之窮困極矣未聞有撫
而恤之者豈不懷寡助之憂土酋之桀
驁固也而多惑於漢人之敎誘姦偽百
出果何道以禁之乎土軍之窮困固也
而又加以漢軍之逃亡營伍日虛果何
===
道以實之乎關隘設險夷夏之大防也
而石門失守三營罷戍則中國反受制
於外夷屯田額徵兵食之大計也而重
價求售以軍作民則外夷多置莊於中
國軍衞之儲每歲用之不充而有司積
貯者多朽腐而不可食所謂國有五寒
者非歟流品之官多取於廢斥之輩而
以才能進者又齟齬而不可行所謂君
子有五恥者非歟古之入滇者有置郡
punctuated: 法至備矣。奈何承平既久，玩愒日滋，亦有當思患而預防者，何也？夫狼子野心，賓貢愆度，土酋之桀驁甚矣，未聞有懾而震之者，豈不犯無武之戒？生計蕭條，賦役繁重，土軍之窮困極矣，未聞有撫而恤之者，豈不懷寡助之憂？土酋之桀驁固也，而多惑於漢人之敎誘，姦偽百出，果何道以禁之乎？土軍之窮困固也，而又加以漢軍之逃亡，營伍日虛，果何道以實之乎？關隘設險，夷夏之大防也，而石門失守，三營罷戍，則中國反受制於外夷。屯田額徵，兵食之大計也，而重價求售，以軍作民，則外夷多置莊於中國。軍衞之儲，每歲用之不充，而有司積貯者多朽腐而不可食，所謂國有五寒者非歟？流品之官，多取於廢斥之輩，而以才能進者，又齟齬而不可行，所謂君子有五恥者非歟？古之入滇者，有置郡
translation_en:
…the regulations are most comprehensive. Yet prolonged peace has brought an increasing tendency to idle away the days. What, then, are the dangers that ought to be anticipated and guarded against? With the untamed hearts of wolf cubs, the native chieftains violate the prescribed rules for attendance at court and presentation of tribute. Their insubordination is extreme, yet we hear of no one intimidating and overawing them. Does this not offend against the injunction against lacking military preparedness? Livelihoods languish, and taxes and labor services are burdensome. The native troops suffer the utmost destitution, yet we hear of no one comforting and relieving them. Should we not fear having few supporters? The native chieftains are certainly insubordinate, but they are also often led astray by the instruction and inducements of Han Chinese, producing fraud and deceit in a hundred forms. By what means can these truly be checked? The native troops are certainly impoverished, but there is also desertion among the Han troops, leaving the ranks emptier by the day. By what means can they truly be replenished?

Fortified passes constitute the great defensive barrier between the non-Chinese peoples and the Chinese. Yet Shimen has fallen, and the three camps have ceased to be garrisoned, so that China instead finds itself subject to the control of peoples beyond its borders. The assessed levies from military agricultural colonies are fundamental to provisioning the troops. Yet with sales sought at high prices [?] and military personnel treated as civilians, peoples from beyond the borders have established many estates within China. The stores of the military guards are insufficient for each year’s needs, while much of what the civil authorities have accumulated rots and becomes unfit to eat. Is this not what is meant by a state having ‘five afflictions of cold’ [?]? Officials within the graded service are mostly drawn from the ranks of the dismissed and rejected, while those advanced for their ability encounter obstruction and cannot put their abilities into practice. Is this not what is meant by a gentleman having ‘five causes for shame’?

Among those who entered Yunnan in antiquity, there were some who established commanderies…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
治於白崖不屯兵而諸夷竟服有勒石
碑於瀘川旣旋師而諸夷復叛有征討
封離而請兵務求其姦黨有檢校南寧
而置郡乃任其豪帥其得失可盡言歟
管子曰化夷之道九變而後安之不知
今日亦可循行否也願明告我將以聞
于
當宁
punctuated: 治於白崖，不屯兵而諸夷竟服；有勒石碑於瀘川，旣旋師而諸夷復叛；有征討封離，而請兵務求其姦黨；有檢校南寧，而置郡乃任其豪帥。其得失可盡言歟？管子曰：「化夷之道，九變而後安之。」不知今日亦可循行否也？願明告我，將以聞于當宁。
translation_en: …the seat of government at Baiya, where the various non-Han peoples ultimately submitted without troops being stationed there; some erected a stone inscription at Luchuan, but once the army withdrew, the various non-Han peoples rebelled again; some campaigned against Fengli [?] and requested troops, intent on hunting down its treacherous faction; some inspected Nanning and, upon establishing commanderies, appointed its powerful local chieftains to office. Can the successes and failures of these measures be fully explained? The Guanzi states: “The way to transform the non-Han peoples requires nine changes before they can be pacified.” I wonder whether this can also be followed and put into practice today. Please explain it clearly to me, so that I may report it to His Majesty.

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
中式舉人五十五名
第一名朱文質雲南府學生易
第二名陳辰雲南前衛人監生書
第三名謝寵貴州永寧宣撫司學生禮記
第四名李登雲南縣學生詩
第五名楊懷哲大理府學生春秋
第六名施繼遠雲南府學生書
第七名史筆曲靖衛人監生詩
===
第八名田時中貴州思南府學生易
第九名呂鳳來賓川州學生春秋
第十名王廷佐通海縣學生禮記
第十一名張鑽大理府學生詩
第十二名楊坦昆明縣學生易
第十三名秦國賢嶍峨縣學生書
第十四名徐州嵩明州學生易
第十五名黃明賢晉寧州學生詩
第十六名張汝學雲南府學生易
punctuated:
中式舉人五十五名。

第一名朱文質，雲南府學生，《易》。
第二名陳辰，雲南前衛人，監生，《書》。
第三名謝寵，貴州永寧宣撫司學生，《禮記》。
第四名李登，雲南縣學生，《詩》。
第五名楊懷哲，大理府學生，《春秋》。
第六名施繼遠，雲南府學生，《書》。
第七名史筆，曲靖衛人，監生，《詩》。
第八名田時中，貴州思南府學生，《易》。
第九名呂鳳來，賓川州學生，《春秋》。
第十名王廷佐，通海縣學生，《禮記》。
第十一名張鑽，大理府學生，《詩》。
第十二名楊坦，昆明縣學生，《易》。
第十三名秦國賢，嶍峨縣學生，《書》。
第十四名徐州，嵩明州學生，《易》。
第十五名黃明賢，晉寧州學生，《詩》。
第十六名張汝學，雲南府學生，《易》。
translation_en:

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰君子道者三我無能焉仁者不憂知
者不惑勇者不懼子貢曰夫子自道也
陳扆
考試官教諭張批聖人子貢之意體認俱到
辭亦渾厚
考試官教授黄批識得聖賢氣象不徒工於
文者
===
聖人以君子之道而不居賢者以為辭之謙也
夫君子之道聖人之所優為也而猶不自居焉
賢者以為辭之謙眞知足以知聖人者哉昔夫
子意謂學貴於大成理難於速契吾固不敢以
自棄而亦安敢以自誣耶誠以君子以德則盛
矣以業則大矣而語其為道則有三焉顧我學
之不講也德之不脩也而反之于身皆無能焉
何則自其純於理而有仁之名仁者渾然無欲
斯不憂矣而我未免於憂也自其明於理而有
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
子曰：「君子道者三，我無能焉：仁者不憂，知者不惑，勇者不懼。」子貢曰：「夫子自道也。」
陳扆
考試官教諭張批：「聖人、子貢之意，體認俱到，辭亦渾厚。」
考試官教授黄批：「識得聖賢氣象，不徒工於文者。」

聖人以君子之道而不居，賢者以為辭之謙也。夫君子之道，聖人之所優為也，而猶不自居焉。賢者以為辭之謙，眞知足以知聖人者哉！昔夫子意謂：「學貴於大成，理難於速契。吾固不敢以自棄，而亦安敢以自誣耶？誠以君子以德則盛矣，以業則大矣，而語其為道，則有三焉。顧我學之不講也，德之不脩也，而反之于身，皆無能焉。何則？自其純於理而有仁之名，仁者渾然無欲，斯不憂矣，而我未免於憂也；自其明於理而有
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said: “There are three aspects to the Way of the gentleman, none of which I am capable of: the benevolent are free from anxiety; the wise are free from perplexity; the courageous are free from fear.” Zigong said: “The Master is describing himself.”

Chen Yi 陳扆

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “He fully grasps the intentions of both the Sage and Zigong. His language, too, is substantial and profound.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “He understands the bearing of sages and worthies; his accomplishment is more than merely literary.”

The Sage declined to claim for himself the Way of the gentleman; the worthy understood his words as an expression of modesty. Now, the Way of the gentleman is something the Sage practices with ease, yet he still declined to claim it for himself. The worthy understood these words as modesty: truly, his understanding was sufficient to comprehend the Sage!

Once, the Master’s meaning was this: “In learning, what matters is complete attainment; understanding principle is difficult to achieve quickly. I certainly dare not give up on myself, but how could I dare to make false claims for myself? For the gentleman is indeed abundant in virtue and great in accomplishment; yet, speaking of his Way, it has three aspects. But I have failed to pursue learning thoroughly and to cultivate virtue; when I examine myself, I find myself capable of none of these three. Why is this? Through purity in principle, one earns the name of benevolent. The benevolent are wholly free from selfish desires and thus free from anxiety, whereas I am not yet free from anxiety. Through clarity in principle, one earns …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
知之名知者洞然無蔽斯不惑矣而我未免於
惑也自其強此理而又宥勇之名勇者毅然無
屈斯不懼矣而我未免於懼也是其有愧於君
子者多矣時子貢在侍乃作而言曰至道固不
易窺而盛德終於難掩夫子道集羣聖罔弗備
矣聖由天縱蔑以加矣故有稱夫子之仁者必
將曰仁之至也有稱夫子之知者必將曰知之
盡也有稱夫子之勇者又必將曰不賴勇而裕
如也今乃曰我無能焉是蓋聖不自聖之心形
===
而為謙已之至自不覺措之詞而遂有是過甚
焉耳矣而在夫子也則固有不得而辭也哉抑
立必俱立之心發而為誨人之切自不容惜之
言而姑為是退托焉耳矣而在夫賜也亦遽肯
信以為然也哉吁夫子遜之子貢知之授受之
間兩無負矣抑夫子斯言多為子貢發蓋孔門
顏子而下穎悟莫若子貢但務方人容有矜已
騖遠而自治或疎故借之已以警之不然他日
與回孰愈之問莫我知也之歎何皆獨於子貢
punctuated:
知之名，知者洞然無蔽，斯不惑矣，而我未免於惑也。自其強此理而又宥勇之名，勇者毅然無屈，斯不懼矣，而我未免於懼也。是其有愧於君子者多矣。時子貢在侍，乃作而言曰：「至道固不易窺，而盛德終於難掩。夫子道集羣聖，罔弗備矣；聖由天縱，蔑以加矣。故有稱夫子之仁者，必將曰仁之至也；有稱夫子之知者，必將曰知之盡也；有稱夫子之勇者，又必將曰不賴勇而裕如也。今乃曰我無能焉，是蓋聖不自聖之心，形而為謙已之至，自不覺措之詞，而遂有是過甚焉耳矣。而在夫子也，則固有不得而辭也哉！抑立必俱立之心，發而為誨人之切，自不容惜之言，而姑為是退托焉耳矣。而在夫賜也，亦遽肯信以為然也哉！」
吁！夫子遜之，子貢知之，授受之間，兩無負矣。抑夫子斯言，多為子貢發。蓋孔門顏子而下，穎悟莫若子貢，但務方人，容有矜已；騖遠，而自治或疎，故借之已以警之。不然，他日與回孰愈之問，莫我知也之歎，何皆獨於子貢
translation_en:
…the name of wisdom. The wise are thoroughly clear-sighted and free of obscurity, and thus have no perplexity; yet I have not escaped perplexity. From being steadfast in this principle comes also the name of courage [?]. The courageous are resolute and unyielding, and thus have no fear; yet I have not escaped fear. In many respects, then, I fall short of the gentleman.
At that time Zigong was attending him. He rose and said: “The highest Way is indeed difficult to fathom, yet abundant virtue ultimately cannot be concealed. Your Way, Master, brings together that of all the sages, lacking nothing. Your sagehood is Heaven-endowed; nothing can be added to it. Thus anyone praising your benevolence must call it benevolence at its utmost; anyone praising your wisdom must call it wisdom in its fullness; and anyone praising your courage must say that you act with ease without needing to rely on courage. Yet now you say, ‘I am capable of none of these.’ Surely this is the heart of a sage who does not regard himself as a sage, manifesting itself in the utmost humility: unconsciously you put it into words, and so have merely carried your self-deprecation too far. But these qualities, Master, are surely ones you cannot disclaim! Or perhaps your resolve, when establishing yourself, necessarily to establish others as well has expressed itself in an earnest desire to teach. Unable to begrudge words of instruction, you have simply adopted this self-effacing stance for the moment. Yet could I, Ci, readily accept it as true?”
Ah! The Master spoke modestly, and Zigong understood him. Between teacher and recipient, neither failed the other. Moreover, these words of the Master were largely spoken for Zigong’s sake. For among the disciples of Confucius, below Master Yan, none equaled Zigong in quickness of understanding. Yet he devoted himself to comparing others and might therefore have been conceited; he pursued distant aims, while perhaps neglecting the cultivation of himself. Thus the Master used his own person as an example to admonish him. Otherwise, on other occasions, why were his question, “Who is superior, you or Hui?” and his lament, “No one understands me,” both addressed exclusively to Zigong …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
焉發之夷考其終至聞性與天道則於所謂仁
知勇三者思之過半矣此固見夫子之曲成而
亦以見子貢之速肖云
尊賢則不惑
朱文質
同考試官教諭尹批聖人動君微旨子能發之
考試官教諭張批精確
考試官教授黃批講不惑最精切
人君能重乎君子斯可以進於明矣夫君子之
===
有關於君德也大矣苟非尊重而得以親之其
何從以進吾之明也哉昔夫子對哀公以九經
尊賢之效意謂人君一心惟在所養君子養之
以善則知矣但人君處崇高之極而視夫韋布
之微固已難親而易疎而彼君子負道德之高
而審於去就之義則又難進而易退非有以尊
之孰得而致之乃若慕古王公之風內則盡敬
于凡所以樂善而忘勢者無所不用其極鑒今
諸侯之失外則盡禮于凡所以折節以下士者
punctuated:
焉發之？夷考其終，至聞性與天道，則於所謂仁知勇三者，思之過半矣。此固見夫子之曲成，而亦以見子貢之速肖云。

尊賢則不惑
朱文質
同考試官教諭尹批：「聖人動君微旨，子能發之。」
考試官教諭張批：「精確。」
考試官教授黃批：「講不惑最精切。」

人君能重乎君子，斯可以進於明矣。夫君子之有關於君德也大矣。苟非尊重而得以親之，其何從以進吾之明也哉？昔夫子對哀公以九經，尊賢之效，意謂人君一心，惟在所養。君子養之以善，則知矣。但人君處崇高之極，而視夫韋布之微，固已難親而易疎；而彼君子負道德之高，而審於去就之義，則又難進而易退。非有以尊之，孰得而致之？乃若慕古王公之風，內則盡敬，于凡所以樂善而忘勢者，無所不用其極；鑒今諸侯之失，外則盡禮，于凡所以折節以下士者，
translation_en:
…were these addressed to him? On examining his eventual attainment, when he came to hear about human nature and the Way of Heaven, he had already grasped the greater part of what are called the three virtues of benevolence, wisdom, and courage. This shows the Master's ability to perfect others according to their particular capacities, and also Zigong's rapid progress in resembling him.

“By Honoring the Worthy, One Is Free from Perplexity”
Zhu Wenzhi
Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor, comments: “You have brought out the sage's subtle intention in moving the ruler.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Precise.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “The explanation of ‘free from perplexity’ is exceptionally incisive and apt.”

If a ruler can esteem men of virtue, he can advance toward clear understanding. For men of virtue have a great bearing on a ruler's virtue. Unless I honor and esteem them and thereby gain their close association, how can I advance my understanding? Formerly, when the Master answered Duke Ai concerning the nine guiding principles, his meaning regarding the effect of honoring the worthy was that everything depends on how the ruler's mind is nourished. When men of virtue nourish it with goodness, it becomes wise. Yet the ruler occupies the pinnacle of exalted rank, and when he regards the lowly men clad in plain leather and cloth, he already finds it difficult to draw close to them and easy to keep them at a distance. Those men of virtue, for their part, possess lofty moral attainments and carefully judge whether accepting or leaving office accords with righteousness; thus they are difficult to bring forward and quick to withdraw. Without a means of honoring them, who could succeed in attracting them? If, then, the ruler admires the example of the kings and dukes of antiquity, inwardly he will show the utmost reverence, doing everything possible to delight in goodness and forget his own power. Taking warning from the failings of the feudal lords of the present, outwardly he will observe the utmost courtesy in all the ways of humbling himself before men of learning…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
無所愛於其情悅矣而能養也養矣而能舉也
隆之以親師取友之恭而讒諂不得以間之結
之以言聽計從之契而貨色不得以沮之夫然
懿德之好自有以動其樂用之心而謙光之施
又有以為受言之地將見納約之資動有所悟
沃心之助日罔自知義理得於薰陶之益而察
中庸于兩端遠而聖賢大學之道亦將躍然於
心目之間矣聞見充於講論之功而析萬殊於
一貫上而帝王心法之傳亦將了然於精神之
===
會矣其不惑者有如此以之脩身而身益脩以
之用人而人益辨尚何文武之政有不舉哉抑
此道惟古能盡之明哉良哉卓乎不可尚已魯
有孔子而不知所以尊之攝相三月定公似矣
齊人歸女樂季桓子受之惡在其為貴德而奚
異乎其惑也然東周之望遽能忘情耶故因哀
公問政即以九經啟之列尊賢於脩身之次而
及其效焉使知身為治本賴賢以脩而知人非
自明不可意獨至矣惜乎哀之猶夫定也
punctuated: 無所愛於其情。悅矣而能養也，養矣而能舉也。隆之以親師取友之恭，而讒諂不得以間之；結之以言聽計從之契，而貨色不得以沮之。夫然，懿德之好自有以動其樂用之心，而謙光之施又有以為受言之地。將見納約之資，動有所悟；沃心之助，日罔自知。義理得於薰陶之益，而察中庸于兩端，遠而聖賢大學之道，亦將躍然於心目之間矣。聞見充於講論之功，而析萬殊於一貫，上而帝王心法之傳，亦將了然於精神之會矣。其不惑者有如此，以之脩身而身益脩，以之用人而人益辨，尚何文武之政有不舉哉？抑此道惟古能盡之。明哉！良哉！卓乎不可尚已！魯有孔子，而不知所以尊之。攝相三月，定公似矣；齊人歸女樂，季桓子受之，惡在其為貴德，而奚異乎其惑也？然東周之望，遽能忘情耶？故因哀公問政，即以九經啟之，列尊賢於脩身之次，而及其效焉，使知身為治本，賴賢以脩，而知人非自明不可，意獨至矣。惜乎哀之猶夫定也！
translation_en:
…he holds nothing back in expressing his feelings. Delighting in worthy men, he can nurture them; nurturing them, he can advance them to office. He honors them with the reverence shown in drawing close to teachers and choosing friends, so that slanderers and flatterers cannot come between them. He binds them to himself through the trust expressed in heeding their words and following their counsel, so that wealth and sensual pleasures cannot thwart them. Thus his love of fine virtue will stir their willingness to serve, while the radiance of his humility will provide an opening for receiving their advice. Then, with the benefit of counsel introduced through what he already understands, he will gain insight at every turn; with aid that nourishes his mind, he will improve daily without himself being aware of it. Through their formative influence he will grasp moral principles and discern the mean between the two extremes. Even the far-reaching Way of the sages and worthies, set forth in the Great Learning, will spring vividly before his mind’s eye. Through discussion his knowledge will expand, and he will distinguish the myriad particular things within the single thread that unites them. Even the exalted transmission of the emperors’ and kings’ teachings of the mind will become clear in his spiritual understanding.

Such will be his freedom from perplexity. Applying this to cultivating himself, he will become ever more cultivated; applying it to employing others, he will distinguish their qualities ever more clearly. What aspect of the government of Kings Wen and Wu could then remain unimplemented? Yet only in antiquity was this Way fully realized. How discerning were those rulers! How worthy their ministers! Their excellence could not be surpassed!

Lu had Confucius, yet did not know how to honor him. When Confucius served as acting chief minister for three months, Duke Ding seemed to approach this ideal. But when the people of Qi presented female musicians, Ji Huanzi accepted them. Where was their esteem for virtue in this, and how did it differ from being deluded? Yet could Confucius so readily relinquish his hope of creating an Eastern Zhou? Thus, when Duke Ai asked about government, Confucius enlightened him with the nine guiding principles, placing honoring the worthy immediately after cultivating oneself and explaining its effects. He meant to make the duke understand that one’s own person is the foundation of government and that its cultivation depends upon worthy men, while discerning others requires that one first possess clear understanding oneself. His intention was supremely earnest. Alas, Duke Ai was just like Duke Ding!

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
友也者友其德也不可以有挾也
楊懷哲
考試官敎諭張批發出孟子論友語意還淳
黜浮之文可以式矣
考試官敎授黄批辭理明當是可與論友者
大賢論友資於人者重而有於已者輕也夫所
資於友者重其德也使有所挾焉則豈取友之
道哉孟子告萬章之意如此今夫朋友乃生人
之大倫爲天下之達道故獨學者來寡聞之譏
===
而麗澤者取相資之益雖論諸學而定交實同
其氣以爲求也是友之云者將拍肩執袂以爲
容悅而已邪抑朋攀類引以相結納而已邪是
故直也諒也多聞也仁足以成人之美而義足
以責人之善彼之所有者德也吾惟因言以觀
其行所足畏也從而友之朝夕相磨于以藉其
薰陶之力因迹以考其心所可益也從而友之
肝膽相示于以仰其切磋之功德業之勸過失
之規胥焉賴之蓋將相觀以爲善而淬礪焉以
punctuated:
友也者，友其德也，不可以有挾也。

楊懷哲

考試官敎諭張批：發出孟子論友語意，還淳黜浮之文，可以式矣。

考試官敎授黄批：辭理明當，是可與論友者。

大賢論友，資於人者重，而有於已者輕也。夫所資於友者，重其德也。使有所挾焉，則豈取友之道哉？孟子告萬章之意如此。今夫朋友，乃生人之大倫，爲天下之達道。故獨學者來寡聞之譏，而麗澤者取相資之益。雖論諸學，而定交實同其氣以爲求也。是友之云者，將拍肩執袂以爲容悅而已邪？抑朋攀類引以相結納而已邪？是故直也，諒也，多聞也，仁足以成人之美，而義足以責人之善。彼之所有者德也，吾惟因言以觀其行，所足畏也，從而友之，朝夕相磨，于以藉其薰陶之力；因迹以考其心，所可益也，從而友之，肝膽相示，于以仰其切磋之功。德業之勸，過失之規，胥焉賴之。蓋將相觀以爲善，而淬礪焉以
translation_en:
“Friendship means befriending another’s virtue; one must not presume upon any advantage.”

Yang Huaizhe

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “This brings out the meaning of Mencius’s words on friendship. An essay that restores simplicity and rejects superficiality: it may serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “The language and reasoning are clear and apt. Here is someone with whom one may discuss friendship.”

In discussing friendship, the great worthy placed weight on what one draws from others and little weight on what one possesses oneself. What one values in drawing upon a friend is his virtue. If one presumes upon some advantage, how could that be the proper way to choose friends? Such was the meaning of Mencius’s words to Wan Zhang. Now friendship is one of the great human relationships, a universally binding way throughout the world. Thus those who study alone incur the criticism of being poorly informed, while those who join together like adjoining lakes gain the benefit of mutual assistance. Though this is discussed in terms of learning, forming friendships indeed involves seeking those of kindred spirit [?]. Does what we call friendship mean merely patting shoulders and grasping sleeves to ingratiate oneself? Or merely attaching oneself to companions and drawing in others of one’s kind to forge connections?

Thus friends should be upright, trustworthy, and widely learned. Their benevolence should suffice to bring others’ admirable qualities to fruition, and their righteousness to demand goodness of others. What such a person possesses is virtue. Through his words I observe his conduct; finding it worthy of reverence, I befriend him. We polish one another morning and evening, and thereby I draw upon his power to nurture and transform me. Through his deeds I examine his heart; finding what can benefit me, I befriend him. We lay our innermost thoughts bare to one another, and thereby I look to the fruits of our mutual refinement. For encouragement in virtue and worthy endeavors, and correction of faults and errors, I rely on him in all these things. The aim is to observe one another so as to do good, and to temper and hone ourselves so as to…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
自新也信誓之期平生之託乆焉要之蓋將因
人以成已而道義焉以相終也友非所以友其
德乎若夫長也貴也兄弟也勢足以傾於一時
而力足以兼乎天下我之所有者此也以此而
恃諸已歟適足以爲長傲遂非之資耳於性分
乎何加以比而施諸人歟徒足以爲席寵怙侈
之地耳於輕重乎何有德色者距人千里之外
不惟失乎人而因以失乎已也驕氣者自矜一
已之長非惟喪乎名而且喪乎業也友而可以
===
有挾乎是知德之與勢輕重殊科在君子權之
而已於此而不失其倫斯之爲能友也夫甞聞
之古之教者七年論學取友謂之小成自天子
以至於庶人一也追而考之堯舜以下若晉平
若費惠若獻子猶有聞者自此而友道日廢在
上者以莫予違爲賢在下者以巧附爲能無復
知所謂貴貴尊賢之義輔仁之風嗚呼微矣世
道之不古彝倫之攸斁又何怪焉故詩存伐木
谷風之刺易示致一斯孚之占有以也夫
punctuated:
自新也。信誓之期，平生之託，乆焉要之，蓋將因人以成已，而道義焉以相終也。友非所以友其德乎？若夫長也、貴也、兄弟也，勢足以傾於一時，而力足以兼乎天下，我之所有者此也。以此而恃諸已歟？適足以爲長傲遂非之資耳，於性分乎何加？以比而施諸人歟？徒足以爲席寵怙侈之地耳，於輕重乎何有？德色者，距人千里之外，不惟失乎人，而因以失乎已也。驕氣者，自矜一已之長，非惟喪乎名，而且喪乎業也。友而可以有挾乎？是知德之與勢，輕重殊科，在君子權之而已。於此而不失其倫，斯之爲能友也夫！
甞聞之，古之教者，七年論學取友，謂之小成，自天子以至於庶人一也。追而考之，堯舜以下，若晉平，若費惠，若獻子，猶有聞者。自此而友道日廢，在上者以莫予違爲賢，在下者以巧附爲能，無復知所謂貴貴尊賢之義、輔仁之風。嗚呼，微矣！世道之不古，彝倫之攸斁，又何怪焉？故《詩》存《伐木》《谷風》之刺，《易》示致一斯孚之占，有以也夫！
translation_en:
…to renew oneself. The pledges made in good faith and the commitments of a lifetime are upheld over the years: the purpose is to perfect oneself through others and to remain faithful to one another in the Way and righteousness to the end. Is friendship not a matter of befriending another’s virtue? As for seniority, noble rank, and brothers—prestige sufficient to overawe one’s contemporaries and power sufficient to encompass all under Heaven—these may be things that I possess. But should I rely upon them? They would merely furnish the means to foster arrogance and persist in wrongdoing. What would they add to my inherent moral nature? Should I use these to impose upon others [?]? They would merely provide grounds for resting on favor and indulging in extravagance. What weight would they carry? An air of moral superiority keeps others a thousand li away: one not only loses others but thereby loses oneself. An arrogant disposition prides itself on one’s own advantages: one loses not only one’s reputation but also one’s accomplishments. Can one, then, enter friendship relying upon such advantages? Thus we know that virtue and power belong to different orders of importance; it is for the gentleman to weigh them. To preserve the proper relationships in this is truly to know how to be a friend!
I have heard that, in education in antiquity, the ability in the seventh year to discuss learning and choose friends was called “minor accomplishment.” From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, the principle was the same. Looking back into the past, from Yao and Shun onward, we still hear of such examples as Duke Ping of Jin, Duke Hui of Fei, and Xianzi. Thereafter, the way of friendship declined day by day. Those above deemed worthy anyone who never opposed them; those below considered skillful ingratiation an accomplishment. No one any longer understood the meaning of honoring the noble and respecting the worthy, or the practice of helping one another cultivate benevolence. Alas, how faint these had become! What wonder, then, that the ways of the world no longer resembled antiquity and that the enduring human relationships fell into decay? Thus the Book of Odes preserves the admonitions of “Felling Trees” and “Valley Wind,” and the Book of Changes presents the prognostication that unity of purpose brings trust. There is indeed a reason for this!

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易
豚魚吉信及豚魚也利涉大川乘木舟虛
也中孚以利貞乃應乎天也
朱文質
同考試官教諭尹批孚貞之理辭足以發
考試官教諭張批確而正
考試官教授黃批雅健
彖傳釋中孚之辭孚貞之義舉之矣蓋孚且貞
天之道也則其感物而濟險也庸舍此而他求
===
乎夫子彖傳若曰中孚之卦有曰豚魚吉者厥
義維何蓋豚魚者罔覺者也感而通者信之浹
也立人之道信而已矣信則精誠神應妙必動
之機而物莫能外體信達順本無心之感而物
罔弗從是信足以及乎豚魚矣豚魚且然維人
維靈有弗感矣乎中孚之吉有如此者何言乎
利涉大川也蓋卦焉全體外實中虛擬象乎舟
虛而乘巽之木以行乎兌澤唯虛也實德中涵
故能涉天下之險而無虞唯巽也誠順積中故
punctuated:
易

「豚魚吉」，信及豚魚也。「利涉大川」，乘木舟虛也。中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。

朱文質

同考試官教諭尹批：孚貞之理，辭足以發。
考試官教諭張批：確而正。
考試官教授黃批：雅健。

彖傳釋中孚之辭，孚貞之義舉之矣。蓋孚且貞，天之道也，則其感物而濟險也，庸舍此而他求乎？夫子彖傳若曰：中孚之卦有曰「豚魚吉」者，厥義維何？蓋豚魚者，罔覺者也；感而通者，信之浹也。立人之道，信而已矣。信則精誠神應，妙必動之機，而物莫能外；體信達順，本無心之感，而物罔弗從。是信足以及乎豚魚矣。豚魚且然，維人維靈，有弗感矣乎？中孚之吉有如此者。何言乎「利涉大川」也？蓋卦焉全體，外實中虛，擬象乎舟虛，而乘巽之木，以行乎兌澤。唯虛也，實德中涵，故能涉天下之險而無虞；唯巽也，誠順積中，故
translation_en:
Book of Changes

“Good fortune with pigs and fish”: trustworthiness extends even to pigs and fish. “It is beneficial to cross the great river”: one rides in a wooden boat with a hollow interior. In Inner Truth (Zhongfu), it is beneficial to remain correct; only thus does one accord with Heaven.

Zhu Wenzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor: “The wording adequately brings out the principles of sincerity and correctness.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Sound and correct.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “Elegant and vigorous.”

In explaining the wording of Inner Truth, the Commentary on the Judgments sets forth the meaning of sincerity and correctness. For sincerity joined with correctness is the Way of Heaven. In moving other beings and overcoming danger, how could one abandon this and seek elsewhere?

The Master’s Commentary on the Judgments seems to say: The hexagram Inner Truth includes the words “Good fortune with pigs and fish.” What do they mean? Pigs and fish are creatures without understanding; that they can be moved and respond shows how thoroughly trustworthiness permeates them. The Way by which human beings establish themselves is simply trustworthiness. With trustworthiness, pure sincerity elicits a numinous response, wondrously activating the impulse that unfailingly moves things; nothing can lie outside its reach. Embodying trustworthiness and attaining accord, one’s influence proceeds without deliberate intent, and nothing fails to follow. Thus trustworthiness can extend even to pigs and fish. If even pigs and fish respond in this way, could human beings, endowed with spiritual intelligence, fail to be moved? Such is the good fortune of Inner Truth.

Why does it say, “It is beneficial to cross the great river”? Taken as a whole, the hexagram is solid on the outside and empty within, resembling the hollow interior of a boat. Riding upon the wood of Xun, it travels over the marsh of Dui. Because it is empty, substantial virtue is held within, enabling one to traverse the dangers of the world without apprehension. Because it is yielding, sincerity and compliance accumulate within, and therefore …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
能拯天下之難而有濟是孚足以濟乎大川矣
大川且然履道坦坦有弗順矣乎中孚之利有
如此者夫至信可以感物矣涉險矣而尤利於
貞者何耶蓋維天之命於穆不已者一孚貞焉
耳今焉有孚顒若而貞固以守乎天理我與天
一而已矣至誠無息而中正以觀乎天下天卽
我而已矣先天焉而天莫之違也後天焉而奉
厥天時也豈不有以應乎天哉天且弗違而况
於人乎况於豚魚乎况於大川乎然則中孚而
===
本於正也不亦宜哉彖傳之旨深矣大抵天下
之道二誠與偽正與邪而已矣故信非正則諒
諒者道之蔽也正非誠則忒忒者道之慝也其
何以感物神化而冒天下之道哉故文王於中
孚拳拳以孚貞之義開示萬世扶焉抑焉宰造
化之力著心易之本焉者也於戲非夫子之聖
之至其孰能與於此
極天下之賾者存乎卦鼓天下之動者存
乎辭化而裁之存乎變推而行之存乎
punctuated:
能拯天下之難而有濟，是孚足以濟乎大川矣。大川且然，履道坦坦，有弗順矣乎？中孚之利有如此者。夫至信可以感物矣，涉險矣，而尤利於貞者，何耶？蓋維天之命，於穆不已者，一孚貞焉耳。今焉有孚顒若，而貞固以守乎天理，我與天一而已矣。至誠無息，而中正以觀乎天下，天卽我而已矣。先天焉，而天莫之違也；後天焉，而奉厥天時也。豈不有以應乎天哉？天且弗違，而况於人乎？况於豚魚乎？况於大川乎？然則中孚而本於正也，不亦宜哉？《彖傳》之旨深矣！大抵天下之道二，誠與偽、正與邪而已矣。故信非正則諒，諒者，道之蔽也；正非誠則忒，忒者，道之慝也。其何以感物神化，而冒天下之道哉？故文王於中孚，拳拳以孚貞之義開示萬世，扶焉抑焉，宰造化之力，著心易之本焉者也。於戲！非夫子之聖之至，其孰能與於此？

極天下之賾者存乎卦，鼓天下之動者存乎辭，化而裁之存乎變，推而行之存乎
translation_en:
…one can rescue the world from its difficulties and bring relief: such trustworthiness suffices to cross a great river. If even a great river can be crossed, could anything fail to go smoothly when one treads a broad and level path? Such are the benefits of Inner Truth. Yet if utmost trustworthiness can move things and carry one through danger, why is it especially beneficial to remain correct and steadfast? The mandate of Heaven, profound and unceasing, is simply trustworthiness joined with correctness. When one possesses trustworthiness in a reverent spirit and firmly preserves heavenly principle, oneself and Heaven are one. When utmost sincerity never ceases and one surveys all under Heaven with centrality and correctness, Heaven is oneself. If one acts before Heaven, Heaven does not contravene one; if one acts after Heaven, one follows Heaven’s seasons. Is this not a means of responding to Heaven? If even Heaven does not contravene one, how much less would people? How much less pigs and fish? How much less a great river? Is it not fitting, then, that Inner Truth should be rooted in correctness? Profound indeed is the meaning of the Commentary on the Judgments!

Broadly speaking, the ways of the world divide into two: sincerity and falsity, correctness and perversity, and nothing more. Thus trustworthiness without correctness becomes rigid fidelity; such fidelity obscures the Way. Correctness without sincerity becomes deviation; such deviation corrupts the Way. How could either move things, transform them with spiritual efficacy, and encompass the Way of all under Heaven? Hence, in Inner Truth, King Wen earnestly used the meaning of trustworthiness and correctness to instruct all generations, sustaining the one and restraining the other. Here he manifested the power to govern the processes of creation and transformation, and made evident the foundation of the Changes within the heart-mind [?]. Alas! Had the Master not attained the utmost sagehood, who could have participated in this understanding?

What fathoms the deepest intricacies of all under Heaven lies in the hexagrams; what stirs all movement under Heaven lies in the statements. Transforming and fashioning things lies in change; extending and putting them into practice lies in…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
通神而明之存乎其人默而成之不言
而信存乎德行
田時中
同考試官敎諭尹批純正細密深於易者
考試官敎諭張批切當
考試官敎授黃批析理明措詞整
大傳論易備天下之用必言用之所以妙於天
下焉蓋卦爻變通天下之能事畢矣待其人而
後行也不有在於德行也哉且天下之賾易理
===
之散見也究極於雜陳之中而廣大悉備之無
遺則存乎卦卦立而賾無不探矣天下之動易
理之發用也鼓動於利用之際而殊塗百慮之
皆順則存乎辭辭告而動無不效矣陰陽動靜
有自然之化也而裁之存乎變蓋進退極而陰
陽易位動靜分而剛柔趨時易窮則變化裁不
在玆乎陰陽變易有可行之道也而推之存乎
通蓋變以趨時而當動之理寓易以從道而攸
往之幾形易變則通推行不在是乎然是變通
punctuated:
通。神而明之，存乎其人；默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。

田時中

同考試官敎諭尹批：純正細密，深於易者。
考試官敎諭張批：切當。
考試官敎授黃批：析理明，措詞整。

大傳論易備天下之用，必言用之所以妙於天下焉。蓋卦爻變通，天下之能事畢矣，待其人而後行也，不有在於德行也哉？且天下之賾，易理之散見也。究極於雜陳之中，而廣大悉備之無遺，則存乎卦；卦立而賾無不探矣。天下之動，易理之發用也。鼓動於利用之際，而殊塗百慮之皆順，則存乎辭；辭告而動無不效矣。陰陽動靜，有自然之化也，而裁之存乎變。蓋進退極而陰陽易位，動靜分而剛柔趨時，易窮則變，化裁不在玆乎？陰陽變易，有可行之道也，而推之存乎通。蓋變以趨時而當動之理寓，易以從道而攸往之幾形，易變則通，推行不在是乎？然是變通
translation_en:
…free passage. To comprehend it with spiritual illumination depends upon the right person; to accomplish it silently and inspire trust without speaking depends upon virtuous conduct.

Tian Shizhong

Comment by Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor: “Pure and correct, subtle and meticulous: the work of one deeply versed in the Changes.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Apt and fitting.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “Clear in its analysis of principle, orderly in its wording.”

When the Great Commentary discusses how the Changes encompasses all applications under Heaven, it must explain what makes its application so wondrous throughout the world. Through the hexagrams and their lines, change and free passage, all that can be accomplished under Heaven is fully encompassed. Yet these await the right person before they can be put into practice. Does this not depend upon virtuous conduct?

The mysteries of all under Heaven are scattered manifestations of the principles of the Changes. To investigate them exhaustively amid their manifold array, encompassing their breadth and greatness without omission, depends upon the hexagrams. Once the hexagrams are established, no mystery remains unexplored. The movements of all under Heaven are the principles of the Changes coming into operation. To set these movements in motion at the point of beneficial application, bringing diverse paths and a hundred deliberations into accord, depends upon the statements. Once the statements give instruction, no movement fails to achieve its effect.

In yin and yang, movement and stillness, there is spontaneous transformation; shaping it depends upon change. When advance and retreat reach their limits, yin and yang exchange positions; when movement and stillness are differentiated, the firm and yielding respond to the time. When the Changes reaches an impasse, it changes. Does not transforming and shaping reside in this?

In the changing of yin and yang, there is a Way that can be put into practice; carrying it forward depends upon free passage. Through change that responds to the time, the principle of appropriate action is embodied; through alteration that follows the Way, the incipient possibilities of proceeding take form. When the Changes changes, passage opens. Does not carrying forward and putting into practice reside in this? Yet this change and free passage…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
也精義入神而周知乎變化之道知來藏往而
大明其終始之幾是必齋戒是存而人之至者
焉能與於此苟非其人道不虛行矣然其神明
也無瀆再三而至理渾成於已無騰口說而微
幾妙契於心是必窮神知化而德之盛者焉能
與於此苟不至德至道不疑矣是則大用備於
易而妙用係於人所以聖人用易而必神明其
德也夫大抵有言畫之易也卦爻也無言心之
易也德行也聖人洗心退藏於密心易具矣百
===
姓日用而不知易安得而不作也乎故有言之
易甚非聖人之得已者而乃以德行望之人無
非欲同歸於無言之域也歟不此之務而徒卦
爻焉是卜抑亦不占而已
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝
陳扆
考試官教諭張批命意脩辭宛然虞廷氣象
考試官教授黃批說出大禹祗承意純雅可錄
punctuated:
也。精義入神，而周知乎變化之道；知來藏往，而大明其終始之幾。是必齋戒是存，而人之至者焉能與於此。苟非其人，道不虛行矣。然其神明也，無瀆再三，而至理渾成於已；無騰口說，而微幾妙契於心。是必窮神知化，而德之盛者焉能與於此。苟不至德，至道不疑矣。是則大用備於易，而妙用係於人，所以聖人用易而必神明其德也夫！大抵有言，畫之易也，卦爻也；無言，心之易也，德行也。聖人洗心，退藏於密，心易具矣。百姓日用而不知，易安得而不作也乎？故有言之易，甚非聖人之得已者，而乃以德行望之人，無非欲同歸於無言之域也歟！不此之務，而徒卦爻焉，是卜抑亦不占而已。

書
文命敷于四海，祗承于帝。
陳扆
考試官教諭張批：命意脩辭，宛然虞廷氣象。
考試官教授黃批：說出大禹祗承意，純雅可錄。
translation_en:
…such is transformation and free passage. By refining understanding of principles until one penetrates the spiritual, one comprehensively knows the way of transformation; by knowing what is to come and storing up what has passed, one clearly understands the subtle beginnings of endings and beginnings. Only those who preserve reverent purification and are consummate in their humanity can participate in this. Without the right person, the Way does not operate of itself. As for making that efficacy spiritually luminous, one does not profane it by repeated consultation, and ultimate principle becomes an integral whole within oneself; one does not indulge in verbal exposition, and the subtlest workings find wondrous accord within the mind. Only those who fathom the spiritual, understand transformation, and possess abundant virtue can participate in this. Without consummate virtue, the ultimate Way is not doubted [?]. Thus the Changes contains the full range of applications, but their wondrous exercise depends upon the person. This is why the sage, in using the Changes, must make his virtue spiritually luminous!

Broadly speaking, the Changes expressed in words is the Changes of drawn figures: the hexagrams and their lines. The wordless Changes is the Changes of the mind: virtue and conduct. The sage purifies his mind and withdraws into hidden depths; the Changes of the mind is fully present within him. Yet the common people use it daily without knowing it. How, then, could the Changes have remained unwritten? Thus the sage truly had no choice but to produce the Changes in words. In expecting virtue and conduct of others, did he not desire that all should return together to the realm beyond words? If one fails to pursue this and attends only to hexagrams and lines, this is merely divination—or indeed amounts to no divination at all.

Book of Documents

“His civilizing influence spread throughout the Four Seas; he reverently served the emperor.”

Chen Yi

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The conception and phrasing vividly evoke the atmosphere of Shun’s court.”

Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “It brings out the meaning of Great Yu’s reverent service. Pure and elegant, it merits inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
已成天下之大化猶獻天下之大猷史臣賛聖
人然也甚矣聖人之不自滿假也大化旣成於
天下而猶獻其猷於帝焉圖治之心何至哉史
臣紀大禹之謨而首之以此蓋謂昔禹之佐舜
也天下之大患旣平致治之大功已定由是祗
台德先著而爲聲敎之布流行洋溢有不疾而
速之機也方懋厥德發而爲敎化之施浸漬浹
洽有不行而至之妙也漸於東海被於西海無
遠弗届燦然禮樂衣冠之會矣曁於南海及於
===
北海舉世丕冒煥然聲名文物之區矣是蓋職
盡于錫圭之餘化行于功成之日而禹之心不
但已也誠以好問如舜而望治之心無窮禹於
是而敬應之彼此有協恭之美樂善如舜求道
之心罔極禹於是而將順之明良孚一德之休
下而民德之觀感係焉則君臣之艱不可以不
愼也而經世之大要是陳豈曰治已隆矣責難
其少置耶上而天道之昭鑒存焉則善惡之辯
不可以不嚴也而保邦之鴻謨是獻豈曰君已
punctuated: 已成天下之大化，猶獻天下之大猷，史臣賛聖人然也。甚矣，聖人之不自滿假也！大化旣成於天下，而猶獻其猷於帝焉，圖治之心何至哉！史臣紀大禹之謨，而首之以此，蓋謂昔禹之佐舜也，天下之大患旣平，致治之大功已定。由是祗台德先，著而爲聲敎之布，流行洋溢，有不疾而速之機也；方懋厥德，發而爲敎化之施，浸漬浹洽，有不行而至之妙也。漸於東海，被於西海，無遠弗届，燦然禮樂衣冠之會矣；曁於南海，及於北海，舉世丕冒，煥然聲名文物之區矣。是蓋職盡于錫圭之餘，化行于功成之日，而禹之心不但已也。誠以好問如舜，而望治之心無窮，禹於是而敬應之，彼此有協恭之美；樂善如舜，求道之心罔極，禹於是而將順之，明良孚一德之休。下而民德之觀感係焉，則君臣之艱不可以不愼也，而經世之大要是陳，豈曰治已隆矣，責難其少置耶？上而天道之昭鑒存焉，則善惡之辯不可以不嚴也，而保邦之鴻謨是獻，豈曰君已
translation_en:
Though he had already brought about the great moral transformation of all under Heaven, he still presented grand counsels for its governance: thus did the historian praise the sage. How utterly the sage refused to rest in self-satisfaction! Even after that great transformation had been accomplished throughout the realm, he still offered his counsels to the emperor. How profound was his concern for good government! In recording the Counsels of the Great Yu, the historian placed this first. His meaning was that, when Yu assisted Shun, the great calamity afflicting the realm had already been quelled, and the great achievement of establishing good government was secure. Thus, reverently taking his own virtue as the lead, he manifested it in the dissemination of moral instruction; flowing abroad in abundance, it possessed the efficacy of moving swiftly without haste. Exerting himself in the cultivation of his virtue, he expressed it through transforming instruction; permeating and suffusing all, it possessed the wondrous power of arriving without travelling. It reached the Eastern Sea and extended to the Western Sea, leaving no distant place untouched: a splendid gathering of rites, music, and ceremonial dress! It reached the Southern Sea and extended to the Northern Sea, generously covering the whole world: a radiant realm of illustrious reputation and cultural refinement!

Thus he fully discharged his duties after receiving the ceremonial jade tablet, and his transforming influence spread once his labours had succeeded. Yet Yu’s concern did not end there. For someone as fond of inquiry as Shun had an inexhaustible desire for good government; Yu responded to him reverently, and the two displayed the beauty of harmonious devotion. Someone as delighted in goodness as Shun had a boundless desire to seek the Way; Yu supported and furthered his intentions, and enlightened ruler and worthy minister realized the excellence of being united in virtue. Below, the people’s moral character depended upon what they observed and were moved by. Therefore, the difficulties of being ruler and minister had to be treated with care, and Yu set forth the essential principles of governing the world. Could he have said that government had already attained its height, and that urging the ruler to undertake difficult duties might therefore be set aside for a while? Above, there remained the clear scrutiny of the Way of Heaven. Therefore, the distinction between good and evil had to be rigorously maintained, and Yu offered his grand counsels for preserving the state. Could he have said that the ruler was already …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖矣陳善姑少緩耶是則化成既見澤民之仁
謨陳又見致君之義古之大臣當大任而遠慮
也如此夫抑論治化之盛未有加于有虞之世
也而君臣上下方且勉力不怠每皇皇然惟恐
難成之功易隳而謀猷之陳交相儆戒君不自
聖臣不自滿相與都俞吁咈于一堂之上惟日
不足此其治所以卓乎不可及也後世論絶德
者曰禹之功臯陶之謨自今觀之禹豈徒功而
已哉
===
王拜手稽首曰公不敢不敬天之休來相
宅其作周匹休公既定宅伻來來視予
卜休恒吉我二人共貞公其以予萬億
年敬天之休拜手稽首誨言
施繼遠
考試官教諭張批形容尊異周公處親切
考試官教授黃批成王叙謝之情此作盡之
賢王敬禮大臣必叙其建都之美而謝其卜都
之辭也蓋建都稽卜事未有重于此者賢王叙
punctuated:
聖矣，陳善姑少緩耶？是則化成既見澤民之仁，謨陳又見致君之義。古之大臣當大任而遠慮也如此夫！抑論治化之盛，未有加于有虞之世也，而君臣上下方且勉力不怠，每皇皇然惟恐難成之功易隳，而謀猷之陳交相儆戒。君不自聖，臣不自滿，相與都俞吁咈于一堂之上，惟日不足。此其治所以卓乎不可及也。後世論絶德者曰：「禹之功，臯陶之謨。」自今觀之，禹豈徒功而已哉！

王拜手稽首曰：「公不敢不敬天之休，來相宅，其作周匹休。公既定宅，伻來，來視予卜休恒吉。我二人共貞，公其以予萬億年敬天之休。」拜手稽首，誨言。
施繼遠
考試官教諭張批：形容尊異周公處親切。
考試官教授黃批：成王叙謝之情，此作盡之。

賢王敬禮大臣，必叙其建都之美，而謝其卜都之辭也。蓋建都稽卜，事未有重于此者。賢王叙
translation_en:
…already a sage, may the presentation of good counsel be relaxed a little? Thus, the completion of moral transformation already displayed his benevolence in benefiting the people; the presentation of his counsels further displayed his righteousness in bringing his ruler to perfection. Such was the foresight with which the great ministers of antiquity bore their weighty responsibilities!
As for the flourishing of transformative government, no age surpassed that of Youyu. Yet ruler and ministers, high and low, continued to exert themselves without flagging. They were constantly anxious lest achievements difficult to accomplish should easily be undone, and in presenting their counsels they admonished and cautioned one another. The ruler did not regard himself as a sage, nor were his ministers complacent. Together in a single hall they voiced approval and dissent, finding the days too short. This is why their government stood so eminently beyond comparison. Those of later ages who discussed surpassing virtue spoke of “Yu’s achievements and Gaotao’s counsels.” Viewed from the present discussion, could Yu’s greatness have consisted in achievements alone?

The king bowed with hands joined and touched his head to the ground, saying: “You, Duke, dared not fail to revere Heaven’s favor. You came to inspect the site of the capital, thereby securing for Zhou a corresponding blessing. Having settled the site, you sent a messenger here to show me that the divination was favorable and consistently auspicious. Let us two together uphold what is right. May you, Duke, join me in revering Heaven’s favor for countless millions of years.” He bowed with hands joined and touched his head to the ground, requesting words of instruction.
Shi Jiyuan
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The passages portraying the exceptional honor accorded to the Duke of Zhou are apt and vivid.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “This composition fully conveys King Cheng’s feelings as he recounts the Duke’s services and expresses his thanks.”

When a worthy king honors a great minister with reverent courtesy, he must recount the excellence of the minister’s work in establishing the capital and express thanks for his words reporting the divination concerning it.
