The sages of high antiquity all created music. Some established it without bringing it to completion; others lived so long ago that their work cannot be investigated. From Huangdi, Yao, and Shun down to Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou, music first attained full development. Yet it did not go beyond the six pitch standards and five tones. Huangzhong, Taicu, Guxian, Ruibin, Yize, and Wuyi are the yang pitch standards; Dalu, Jiazhong, Zhonglü, Linzhong, Nanlü, and Yingzhong are the yin pitch standards. Gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu are the five tones. There are twelve pitch pipes in all. Each has a diameter of slightly more than three fen and an internal circumference of nine fen; the Huangzhong pipe is nine cun long. From Dalu onward, the yang and yin pitch pipes alternate and become progressively shorter, reaching their limit at Yingzhong. They are used to create music and regulate…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
音聲則長者聲下短者聲高下者則重濁
而舒遲高者則輕清而剽疾如以黃鍾爲
宫則用林鍾爲徵太蔟爲商南吕爲羽姑
洗爲角應鍾爲變宫蕤賓爲變徵七律自
成均而聲自和諧太蔟以下以次而均之
則聲以漸而和而五音正矣所以和神人
者此也所以合上下者此也按之周禮其
祀天也以圜鍾爲宫黃鍾爲角太蔟爲徵
姑洗爲羽其數合至夷則無清宫焉直至
===
圜鍾之清宫凡六變也其祀地也以函鍾
爲宫太蔟爲角姑洗爲徵南吕爲羽其數
合至南吕無清宫焉直至太吕之清宫凡
八變也其求人鬼也以黃鍾爲宫太吕爲
角太蔟爲徵應鍾爲羽其數合至應鍾無
清宫焉直至黃鍾之清宫凡九變也以是
而禮諸天神地祇人鬼也而有不享矣乎
漢書曰盛德在木其音角者依於仁也在
火其音徵者立於禮也在金其音商者發
punctuated:
音聲，則長者聲下，短者聲高；下者則重濁而舒遲，高者則輕清而剽疾。如以黃鍾爲宫，則用林鍾爲徵，太蔟爲商，南吕爲羽，姑洗爲角，應鍾爲變宫，蕤賓爲變徵，七律自成均，而聲自和諧。太蔟以下，以次而均之，則聲以漸而和，而五音正矣。所以和神人者此也，所以合上下者此也。按之《周禮》，其祀天也，以圜鍾爲宫，黃鍾爲角，太蔟爲徵，姑洗爲羽，其數合至夷則，無清宫焉，直至圜鍾之清宫，凡六變也。其祀地也，以函鍾爲宫，太蔟爲角，姑洗爲徵，南吕爲羽，其數合至南吕，無清宫焉，直至太吕之清宫，凡八變也。其求人鬼也，以黃鍾爲宫，太吕爲角，太蔟爲徵，應鍾爲羽，其數合至應鍾，無清宫焉，直至黃鍾之清宫，凡九變也。以是而禮諸天神、地祇、人鬼也，而有不享矣乎？
《漢書》曰：「盛德在木，其音角者，依於仁也；在火，其音徵者，立於禮也；在金，其音商者，發
translation_en:
…sounds: longer pipes produce lower sounds, and shorter pipes higher sounds. Lower sounds are weighty and deep, relaxed and slow; higher sounds are light and clear, swift and brisk. For example, if Huangzhong is taken as gong, Linzhong serves as zhi, Taicu as shang, Nanlü as yu, Guxian as jue, Yingzhong as altered gong, and Ruibin as altered zhi. These seven pitches naturally form a scale, and their sounds naturally harmonize. Beginning with Taicu, if scales are formed on each successive pitch, the sounds harmonize in progression, and the five notes are correctly ordered. This is how spirits and human beings are brought into harmony; this is how those above and below are united. Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that in sacrifices to Heaven, Yuanzhong serves as gong, Huangzhong as jue, Taicu as zhi, and Guxian as yu. The numerical sequence reaches Yize, but the upper-octave gong has not yet been reached [?]; it continues to the upper-octave gong of Yuanzhong, making six transformations in all. In sacrifices to Earth, Hanzhong serves as gong, Taicu as jue, Guxian as zhi, and Nanlü as yu. The numerical sequence reaches Nanlü, but the upper-octave gong has not yet been reached [?]; it continues to the upper-octave gong of Tailü, making eight transformations in all. In summoning human spirits, Huangzhong serves as gong, Tailü as jue, Taicu as zhi, and Yingzhong as yu. The numerical sequence reaches Yingzhong, but the upper-octave gong has not yet been reached [?]; it continues to the upper-octave gong of Huangzhong, making nine transformations in all. When these are used to perform rites for the celestial spirits, terrestrial deities, and human spirits, could any fail to accept the offerings?
The History of the Han states: “When flourishing virtue resides in Wood, its note is jue, for it rests upon benevolence. When it resides in Fire, its note is zhi, for it is established upon ritual propriety. When it resides in Metal, its note is shang, for it issues forth…”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
於義也在水其音羽者妙於智也在土其
音宮者本乎信也所謂道五常之行者非
歟月令曰東方律中仲呂南方律中夷則
西方律中應鍾北方律中太簇自子而至
巳皆陽也自午而至亥皆陰也所謂合生
氣之和者非歟以相生言之陽律陽呂皆
下生陰律陰呂皆上生謂律無下生呂之
理豈其然乎以易數言之乾納甲而坤納
癸始于乾而終于坤納音則始于金而終
===
于土謂法有不同未之考乎徵者物之成
也羽者物之終也天功成於正月故天以
太簇為角地以太簇為徵天功畢於三月
故天以姑洗為羽地以姑洗為徵義以時
而異之耳不曰夾鍾而曰圜鍾者以天體
言也不曰林鍾而曰函鍾者以地體言也
名以用而別之耳圜鍾函鍾黃鍾同會于
卯者卯為昏明之交當其晝夜之間而𦘕
之所以交上下而通幽明也其意安得而
punctuated: 於義也；在水，其音羽者，妙於智也；在土，其音宮者，本乎信也。所謂道五常之行者，非歟？《月令》曰：「東方律中仲呂，南方律中夷則，西方律中應鍾，北方律中太簇。」自子而至巳，皆陽也；自午而至亥，皆陰也。所謂合生氣之和者，非歟？以相生言之，陽律陽呂皆下生，陰律陰呂皆上生。謂律無下生呂之理，豈其然乎？以易數言之，乾納甲而坤納癸，始于乾而終于坤；納音則始于金而終于土。謂法有不同，未之考乎？徵者，物之成也；羽者，物之終也。天功成於正月，故天以太簇為角，地以太簇為徵；天功畢於三月，故天以姑洗為羽，地以姑洗為徵。義以時而異之耳。不曰夾鍾而曰圜鍾者，以天體言也；不曰林鍾而曰函鍾者，以地體言也。名以用而別之耳。圜鍾、函鍾、黃鍾同會于卯者，卯為昏明之交，當其晝夜之間而𦘕之，所以交上下而通幽明也。其意安得而
translation_en: …arises from righteousness. When virtue resides in water, its note is yu, finding its subtle expression in wisdom; when it resides in earth, its note is gong, rooted in trustworthiness. Is this not what is meant by giving expression to the operation of the Five Constant Virtues? The Monthly Ordinances says: “In the east, the pitch accords with Zhonglü; in the south, with Yize; in the west, with Yingzhong; and in the north, with Taicu.” From zi through si, all are yang; from wu through hai, all are yin. Is this not what is meant by bringing the vital energies into harmony? In terms of the pitches generating one another, the yang pitches in both the lü 律 and lü 呂 categories all generate downward, while the yin pitches in both categories all generate upward. Can it really be true that there is no principle by which a lü 律 pitch generates a lü 呂 pitch downward? In terms of the numerical principles of the Book of Changes, Qian takes the stem jia and Kun takes the stem gui: the sequence begins with Qian and ends with Kun. The system of assigned tones, nayin, begins with metal and ends with earth. Those who say that the methods differ—have they failed to examine this? The note zhi signifies the completion of things; the note yu signifies their ending. Heaven’s work reaches completion in the first month; thus, in music for Heaven, Taicu serves as jue, and in music for Earth, Taicu serves as zhi. Heaven’s work concludes in the third month; thus, in music for Heaven, Guxian serves as yu, and in music for Earth, Guxian serves as zhi. Their significance simply varies with the season. The name Yuanzhong, “Round Bell,” is used instead of Jiazhong with reference to the form of Heaven; the name Hanzhong, “Enclosing Bell,” is used instead of Linzhong with reference to the form of Earth. The names are simply distinguished according to their use. Yuanzhong, Hanzhong, and Huangzhong all converge at mao because mao is the juncture of darkness and light. Marking it out [?] at the boundary between day and night serves to bring above and below into communication and to connect the unseen and the visible. How could their underlying meaning…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
不同唐無徵音謂李嗣眞以散車一鐸而
補其闕傳之妄也宋無商聲謂蔡元定以
其臣陵君而不用或一道也六律六吕有
從聲有變聲而鄭譯條具之爲八十四調
不免有犯聲側聲正殺寄殺之謬十二律
各七均乃成八十四調而元稹爲琵琶八
十三調不免有偏字倚字雙字半字之訛
此皆三代以下之音也姑舍是禮記曰宫
亂則荒其君驕商亂則陂其臣壞角亂則
===
憂其民怨徵亂則哀其事勤羽亂則危其
財匱五者皆亂迭相陵謂之慢如此則國
之滅亡無日矣故曰聲音之道與政通焉
樂元語曰東夷之樂曰離持矛舞助時生
也南夷之樂曰兜持羽舞助時養也西夷
之樂曰禁持戟舞助時煞也北夷之樂曰
昧持干舞助時藏也故曰先王制夷狄樂
不制夷狄禮焉夫知聲而不知音者禽獸
也知音而不知樂者庸衆也知樂而不如
punctuated:
不同？唐無徵音，謂李嗣眞以散車一鐸而補其闕，傳之妄也。宋無商聲，謂蔡元定以其臣陵君而不用，或一道也。六律六吕，有從聲，有變聲，而鄭譯條具之爲八十四調，不免有犯聲、側聲、正殺、寄殺之謬。十二律各七均，乃成八十四調，而元稹爲琵琶八十三調，不免有偏字、倚字、雙字、半字之訛。此皆三代以下之音也。姑舍是。《禮記》曰：「宫亂則荒，其君驕；商亂則陂，其臣壞；角亂則憂，其民怨；徵亂則哀，其事勤；羽亂則危，其財匱。五者皆亂，迭相陵，謂之慢。如此，則國之滅亡無日矣。」故曰：「聲音之道，與政通焉。」
《樂元語》曰：「東夷之樂曰離，持矛舞，助時生也；南夷之樂曰兜，持羽舞，助時養也；西夷之樂曰禁，持戟舞，助時煞也；北夷之樂曰昧，持干舞，助時藏也。」故曰：「先王制夷狄樂，不制夷狄禮焉。」夫知聲而不知音者，禽獸也；知音而不知樂者，庸衆也；知樂而不如
translation_en:
…not be the same? The Tang lacked the zhi tone; the claim that Li Sizhen supplied the deficiency with a single bell from a carriage [?] is a false tradition. The Song lacked the shang tone; the claim that Cai Yuanding left it unused because it represented ministers encroaching upon their ruler may offer one explanation. The six yang pitch standards and six yin pitch standards have both accompanying tones and altered tones. Zheng Yi set these out systematically as eighty-four modes, yet could not avoid errors involving encroaching tones, oblique tones, regular endings, and borrowed endings. Each of the twelve pitch standards has seven modal scales, making eighty-four modes; yet Yuan Zhen made eighty-three modes for the pipa, inevitably introducing errors involving partial, dependent, double, and half notation signs [?]. These are all musical systems dating from after the Three Dynasties. Let us set them aside for now. The Record of Rites says: “When gong is disordered, there is dissipation: the ruler is arrogant. When shang is disordered, there is perversity: the ministers are corrupt. When jue is disordered, there is sorrow: the people are resentful. When zhi is disordered, there is grief: public undertakings are burdensome. When yu is disordered, there is peril: financial resources are exhausted. When all five are disordered and encroach upon one another in turn, this is called insolent disorder. In such circumstances, the state's destruction is imminent.” Thus it says: “The principles of sound and music are interconnected with government.”
The Primal Sayings on Music (Yue yuan yu) says: “The music of the eastern Yi is called Li: they dance holding spears, assisting the season's work of generation. The music of the southern Yi is called Dou: they dance holding feathers, assisting the season's work of nourishment. The music of the western Yi is called Jin: they dance holding halberds, assisting the season's work of killing. The music of the northern Yi is called Mei: they dance holding shields, assisting the season's work of storing away.” Thus it is said: “The former kings regulated the music of the Yi and Di, but did not regulate their rites.” Those who recognize sounds but do not understand musical tones are birds and beasts; those who understand musical tones but do not understand music are the common multitude; those who understand music but do not [understand?] …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
德者三代以下之人也自羲黃以來其樂
可得而知也言其德則如天之無不幬也
如地之無不載也如日月之無不照臨也
言其法則通變以宜民也神化以合俗也
言其時則天地訢合也陰陽相得也萬物
煦嫗也德之盛也和之至也自是而下秦
漢唐宋音日以侈而化日以漓桑間濮上
之音徧滿天下而清廟之奏寂然無聞惡
怪其治之不古若也是知樂之音不必求
===
也節之禮義以養其心道之平和以養其
情出之優柔以宣其言然後播之聲詩薦
之郊廟歌之朝廷布之邦國以奮至德之
光以動四氣之和以著萬物之理此之謂
大樂與天地同和此之謂比隆三代否則
偕伶夔而奏咸池大章於秦皇漢武之廷
何益乎勝國以來音樂漸缺
朝廷之上亦嘗講求而古樂至今未盡復意
者於身心教化之道未之先乎此實
punctuated: 德者，三代以下之人也。自羲黃以來，其樂可得而知也。言其德，則如天之無不幬也，如地之無不載也，如日月之無不照臨也；言其法，則通變以宜民也，神化以合俗也；言其時，則天地訢合也，陰陽相得也，萬物煦嫗也。德之盛也，和之至也。自是而下，秦漢唐宋，音日以侈，而化日以漓。桑間濮上之音徧滿天下，而清廟之奏寂然無聞，惡怪其治之不古若也？是知樂之音不必求也。節之禮義以養其心，道之平和以養其情，出之優柔以宣其言，然後播之聲詩，薦之郊廟，歌之朝廷，布之邦國，以奮至德之光，以動四氣之和，以著萬物之理。此之謂大樂與天地同和，此之謂比隆三代。否則，偕伶夔而奏咸池大章於秦皇漢武之廷，何益乎？勝國以來，音樂漸缺，朝廷之上亦嘗講求，而古樂至今未盡復。意者，於身心教化之道未之先乎？此實
translation_en:
…virtue [?] are people of the ages after the Three Dynasties. From the time of Xi and Huang—Fuxi and the Yellow Emperor—onward, their music can be known. As for its virtue, it was like Heaven, which shelters everything; like Earth, which bears everything; and like the sun and moon, which illuminate everything. As for its methods, it adapted to changing circumstances to benefit the people and transformed them imperceptibly to accord with their customs. As for its times, Heaven and Earth joined in joyous harmony, yin and yang complemented one another, and all things were warmed and nurtured. Such was the fullness of virtue and the utmost degree of harmony.

Thereafter, through the Qin, Han, Tang, and Song, musical sounds grew daily more extravagant, while moral transformation grew daily weaker. The music of Sangjian and Pushang filled the world, while the performances of the Pure Temple fell utterly silent. How could one wonder that government failed to equal that of antiquity? Thus we know that there is no need to seek out the sounds of music themselves. Regulate people through ritual and righteousness to nurture their minds; guide them through balance and harmony to nurture their feelings; let these emerge with gentle ease to give expression to their words. Only then disseminate them through song and poetry, offer them at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, sing them at court, and spread them throughout the realm, thereby making the radiance of consummate virtue shine forth, stirring the harmony of the vital forces of the four seasons, and revealing the principles of all things. This is what is meant by saying that great music shares the harmony of Heaven and Earth; this is what is meant by matching the grandeur of the Three Dynasties. Otherwise, even if one joined Ling and Kui in performing the Xianchi and Dazhang at the courts of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han, what benefit would there be?

Since the former dynasty, music has gradually become incomplete. The court has indeed investigated and sought it out, yet ancient music has still not been fully restored. Might this be because the cultivation of body and mind and the work of moral transformation have not been given priority? This truly…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖君賢相之所當加之意焉者若夫
聖學之原聲律之本別有說焉而尚未之遑也
第三問
李登
同考試官教諭李批拳拳於持盈保治之道忠
愛溢於言表
同考試官教諭趙批以防微慎德爲保治之道
良爲有見
考試官教諭張批達治體
===
考試官教授黃批以審勢謹微立意最是
立長治之法者存乎勢寓治亂之機者存
乎微君子當審勢以創法謹微以運機焉
耳矣知創法矣而勢弗審焉未免後車覆
轍之弊知審勢矣而微弗謹焉未免尾大
不掉之患均之害治道焉故明君英辟審
勢以操天下之權是謂之善法而功可久
矣謹微以銷未然之變是謂之善機而業
可大矣雖然權變之際難言也子欲除前
punctuated:
聖君賢相之所當加之意焉者。若夫聖學之原、聲律之本，別有說焉，而尚未之遑也。

第三問
李登

同考試官教諭李批：拳拳於持盈保治之道，忠愛溢於言表。
同考試官教諭趙批：以防微慎德爲保治之道，良爲有見。
考試官教諭張批：達治體。
考試官教授黃批：以審勢謹微立意，最是。

立長治之法者存乎勢，寓治亂之機者存乎微。君子當審勢以創法，謹微以運機焉耳矣。知創法矣，而勢弗審焉，未免後車覆轍之弊；知審勢矣，而微弗謹焉，未免尾大不掉之患，均之害治道焉。故明君英辟審勢以操天下之權，是謂之善法，而功可久矣；謹微以銷未然之變，是謂之善機，而業可大矣。雖然，權變之際難言也。子欲除前
translation_en:
…what a sage ruler and worthy ministers ought to give particular attention to. As for the source of sagely learning and the foundations of musical pitch, there is a separate discussion to be had, but there has not yet been leisure to undertake it.

Third Question
Li Deng

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: He is deeply concerned with the way to sustain prosperity and preserve good government; loyalty and devotion overflow beyond his words.
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor: He takes guarding against incipient dangers and attending carefully to virtue as the way to preserve good government. This is truly perceptive.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: He understands the essentials of government.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: Making the assessment of circumstances and vigilance over small beginnings his central argument is most appropriate.

Establishing institutions for lasting good government depends upon circumstances; the incipient causes of order and disorder lie in small beginnings. The gentleman must assess circumstances to create institutions and attend carefully to small beginnings to direct those incipient developments—that is all. If one knows how to create institutions but fails to assess circumstances, one cannot escape the error of a following carriage overturning in the same ruts. If one knows how to assess circumstances but fails to attend carefully to small beginnings, one cannot escape the danger of a tail grown too large to move. Both alike harm the way of government. Thus an enlightened ruler, an outstanding sovereign, assesses circumstances in order to hold authority over all under Heaven. This is called sound institutional practice, and its achievements can endure. He attends carefully to small beginnings to dispel disturbances before they arise. This is called skillful handling of incipient developments, and his undertaking can become great. Even so, the juncture at which discretionary adaptation is required is difficult to discuss. You wish to eliminate the … of earlier…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
人月旦私駁之弊秉公持正以與執事者
尚論古人可乎夫嬴秦郡縣天下二世而
失鹿者孤立之弊也漢高帝起而懲之分
王同姓昆弟及異姓功臣以彊榦聯支焉
立法可謂周固矣然僅及一傳而吕雉者
出牝雞晨鳴僭干天憲始則韓彭以讒疑
受戮終則劉氏以曖昧見誅所遺者惟長
沙王吳芮朱虚侯劉章數人耳矣當時無
平勃輩調和于內安保漢氏之血食哉迨
===
哀平二帝之世昔之磐石之宗巳殫微而
不可支孝元王后乃收璽綬而竊據之至
舉天下之兵付之巨姦之手而漢之子孫
稽首若崩矣議者以禄產新莽之姦足以
移漢而不知吕雉之猖亂孝元之稔惡溺
愛外戚之所致也程頤氏曰婦居尊位吕
氏是也非常之變不可言也其是之謂乎
隋煬任用匪人二傳而短祚者失驩之弊
也唐太宗起而懲之振綱秩度抑宦寺之
punctuated:
人月旦私駁之弊，秉公持正，以與執事者尚論古人，可乎？夫嬴秦郡縣天下，二世而失鹿者，孤立之弊也。漢高帝起而懲之，分王同姓昆弟及異姓功臣，以彊榦聯支焉。立法可謂周固矣。然僅及一傳，而吕雉者出，牝雞晨鳴，僭干天憲。始則韓彭以讒疑受戮，終則劉氏以曖昧見誅，所遺者惟長沙王吳芮、朱虚侯劉章數人耳矣。當時無平勃輩調和于內，安保漢氏之血食哉？迨哀平二帝之世，昔之磐石之宗巳殫微而不可支，孝元王后乃收璽綬而竊據之，至舉天下之兵付之巨姦之手，而漢之子孫稽首若崩矣。議者以禄產、新莽之姦足以移漢，而不知吕雉之猖亂、孝元之稔惡，溺愛外戚之所致也。程頤氏曰：「婦居尊位，吕氏是也，非常之變，不可言也。」其是之謂乎？
隋煬任用匪人，二傳而短祚者，失驩之弊也。唐太宗起而懲之，振綱秩度，抑宦寺之
translation_en:
…the faults of earlier men in passing personal judgments and making partisan criticisms, and, upholding impartiality and rectitude, join you, sir, in discussing the ancients—would this be possible?
The Qin dynasty of the Ying house organized the realm into commanderies and counties, yet lost its dominion in the second generation: this was the consequence of standing alone. Emperor Gao of Han arose and took warning from this. He enfeoffed his brothers and kinsmen of the same surname, together with meritorious ministers of other surnames, as kings, thereby strengthening the trunk and linking the branches. His institutional arrangements may indeed be called comprehensive and secure. Yet barely one succession had passed when Lü Zhi appeared: the hen crowed at dawn, and she presumptuously encroached upon Heaven’s ordinances. First Han Xin and Peng Yue were executed because of slander and suspicion; later members of the Liu house were put to death on obscure grounds. Those left were only a few men, such as Wu Rui, King of Changsha, and Liu Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu. Without men like Chen Ping and Zhou Bo maintaining concord within the court at that time, how could the continuance of the Han house’s ancestral sacrifices have been assured?
By the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping, the imperial clan, once firm as bedrock, had dwindled into weakness and could no longer sustain itself. Empress Xiaoyuan then took possession of the imperial seal and its cord and usurped control of them, going so far as to place all the realm’s troops in the hands of a great traitor, while the descendants of Han bowed their heads to the ground as though collapsing. Commentators hold that the treachery of Lü Lu, Lü Chan, and Wang Mang of Xin was sufficient to overthrow Han. They do not understand that Lü Zhi’s lawless disorder and Empress Xiaoyuan’s fostering of evil resulted from their excessive affection for their maternal and marital kin. Cheng Yi said: “A woman occupying the exalted position—Lady Lü is an example—is an extraordinary aberration, beyond what can be discussed.” Was this not what he meant?
Emperor Yang of Sui employed unworthy men, and the dynasty’s allotted span was cut short after two successions: this was the consequence of losing people’s goodwill. Emperor Taizong of Tang arose and took warning from this. He reinvigorated the guiding principles of government, set its regulations in order, and restricted the eunuchs’…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
官無過四品立法可謂宏遠矣然未及數
世而高力士李輔國程元振者相繼並出
依馮城社竊弄刑賞始則省決章奏終則
叅預軍謀其甚者陵辱宰相僭領宿衛而
太阿之柄下移矣當時無李郭輩以振揚
于外安保唐宗之不綴旒乎迨僖昭二宗
之世昔之冠履之分已倒置而莫能辨王
守澄楊復恭乃脅乘輿而播遷之甘心國
老蹀血禁塗而唐之宗社莽為丘墟矣議
===
者以祿山朱温之惡足以覆唐而不知李
輔國之階釁王守澄之從逆狎恩恃愛之
所致也司馬光曰宦官之禍唐慘于漢漢
不握兵唐握兵也非是之謂乎五季兵戈
之擾生靈塗炭之苦極矣黷兵之弊也宋
藝祖起而懲之釋藩鎮之權戒殺戮之慘
以安天下之民存心可謂仁厚矣然未及
中葉而王安石者出負偏僻之學濟紛更
之政始則變法以榷民財終則要君而拂
punctuated:
官無過四品，立法可謂宏遠矣。然未及數世，而高力士、李輔國、程元振者相繼並出，依馮城社，竊弄刑賞。始則省決章奏，終則叅預軍謀，其甚者陵辱宰相，僭領宿衛，而太阿之柄下移矣。當時無李郭輩以振揚于外，安保唐宗之不綴旒乎？迨僖昭二宗之世，昔之冠履之分已倒置而莫能辨，王守澄、楊復恭乃脅乘輿而播遷之，甘心國老，蹀血禁塗，而唐之宗社莽為丘墟矣。議者以祿山、朱温之惡足以覆唐，而不知李輔國之階釁、王守澄之從逆，狎恩恃愛之所致也。司馬光曰：「宦官之禍，唐慘于漢，漢不握兵，唐握兵也。」非是之謂乎？

五季兵戈之擾，生靈塗炭之苦極矣，黷兵之弊也。宋藝祖起而懲之，釋藩鎮之權，戒殺戮之慘，以安天下之民，存心可謂仁厚矣。然未及中葉，而王安石者出，負偏僻之學，濟紛更之政，始則變法以榷民財，終則要君而拂
translation_en:
…their official ranks were not to exceed the fourth rank. Such legislation may indeed be called far-reaching. Yet within a few generations, Gao Lishi, Li Fuguo, and Cheng Yuanzhen emerged in succession. Sheltering behind the throne, like pests protected by city walls and earth-god shrines, they usurped control over punishments and rewards. At first they reviewed and decided upon memorials; eventually they participated in military deliberations. The worst among them humiliated chief ministers and presumptuously took command of the palace guards: the hilt of Tai’a, the sword of sovereign authority, passed into subordinate hands. Had there been no men like Li Guangbi and Guo Ziyi to uphold the dynasty in the field, how could anyone have guaranteed that the Tang sovereign would not become a mere dangling pennant?

By the reigns of Xizong and Zhaozong, the former distinction between crown and shoes—ruler and subject—had been overturned beyond recognition. Wang Shoucheng and Yang Fugong coerced the emperor and drove him into exile, vented their malice upon the state’s elder ministers, and trampled through blood on the palace roads. The Tang ancestral temples and altars of state became desolate ruins. Commentators hold that the wickedness of An Lushan and Zhu Wen sufficed to overthrow the Tang, yet fail to recognize that Li Fuguo’s fomenting of disorder and Wang Shoucheng’s adherence to rebellion arose from their taking liberties with imperial favor and relying upon the ruler’s affection. Sima Guang said: “The calamity wrought by eunuchs was more grievous under the Tang than under the Han. Under the Han they did not command troops; under the Tang they did.” Was this not precisely what he meant?

During the Five Dynasties, the turmoil of warfare and the people’s suffering reached their utmost extremes. These were the evils of wanton militarism. The founding emperor of the Song arose and took warning from them. He stripped the regional military governors of their power and guarded against the horrors of slaughter, thereby bringing peace to the people of the realm. His intentions may indeed be called humane and generous. Yet before the dynasty’s midpoint, Wang Anshi emerged, relying upon narrow and unorthodox learning to advance a program of disruptive administrative changes. At first he changed the laws to monopolize the people’s wealth; eventually he coerced the sovereign and opposed…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
正議其所欲者在用兵破遼以炫志肆功
耳矣當旹吕誨文彥博諸賢雖極力捄正
于其間而宋之精神命脉已消索而無餘
卒之徽欽北狩而不返高宗南遷而弗競
者皆援引共事之人踵其故智以貽患于
無窮也逮理度二宗之世昔之碩儒正士
悉擯斥而弗用而史彌遠賈似道韓侂胄
之徒接踵用事乃內蔽主聽外藩群邪浸
淫反覆舉中原而陷之夷焉議者以金元
===
之難足以亡宋而不知安石之變法史賈
之弄權文姦飾儒之所致也富弼曰安石
雖有時名然好偏執見置諸宰輔天下必
受其禍信哉言乎夫漢之禍不在外戚而
在女主之竊柄由人主昵私愛而忘大計
也故外戚因之以釀亂唐之禍不在藩鎮
而在宦官之擅政由人主狎近習而遠君
子也故藩鎮因之以叛君宋之禍不在夷
狄而在士夫之亂政由人主務忠厚而少
punctuated:
正議，其所欲者在用兵破遼，以炫志肆功耳矣。當旹吕誨、文彥博諸賢雖極力捄正于其間，而宋之精神命脉已消索而無餘。卒之徽欽北狩而不返，高宗南遷而弗競者，皆援引共事之人踵其故智，以貽患于無窮也。逮理度二宗之世，昔之碩儒正士悉擯斥而弗用，而史彌遠、賈似道、韓侂胄之徒接踵用事，乃內蔽主聽，外藩群邪，浸淫反覆，舉中原而陷之夷焉。議者以金元之難足以亡宋，而不知安石之變法、史賈之弄權，文姦飾儒之所致也。富弼曰：「安石雖有時名，然好偏執見，置諸宰輔，天下必受其禍。」信哉言乎！

夫漢之禍不在外戚，而在女主之竊柄，由人主昵私愛而忘大計也，故外戚因之以釀亂。唐之禍不在藩鎮，而在宦官之擅政，由人主狎近習而遠君子也，故藩鎮因之以叛君。宋之禍不在夷狄，而在士夫之亂政，由人主務忠厚而少
translation_en:
…sound counsel. What he desired was merely to wage war and defeat the Liao, flaunting his ambitions and indulging his pursuit of military achievement. Although worthy men such as Lü Hui and Wen Yanbo exerted themselves to correct matters at the time, the Song’s vitality and lifeblood had already been utterly depleted. That Huizong and Qinzong ultimately went on a “northern hunt”—being taken captive—and never returned, and that Gaozong moved south and failed to regain strength, all resulted from the men Wang Anshi had brought into office to work with him following his old devices, thereby bequeathing endless calamity. By the reigns of Lizong and Duzong, the great scholars and upright men of earlier times had all been excluded from service, while the likes of Shi Miyuan, Jia Sidao, and Han Tuozhou wielded power in succession. Within the court they blocked information from reaching the ruler; outside it they shielded the whole company of wicked men. Through their spreading influence and repeated machinations, they delivered the entire Central Plain into the hands of the barbarians. Commentators consider the calamities inflicted by the Jin and Yuan sufficient to account for the Song’s destruction, but fail to recognize that it resulted from Anshi’s changes to the laws and Shi’s and Jia’s manipulation of power, cloaking their treachery in the outward guise of Confucian learning. Fu Bi said: “Although Anshi enjoys a reputation in our day, he is fond of obstinately maintaining biased opinions. If he is placed among the chief councillors, all under Heaven will surely suffer the resulting calamity.” How true these words were!

The source of the Han’s calamity lay not in imperial in-laws but in female rulers’ usurpation of authority. This arose because the sovereign indulged his private affections and forgot the greater interests of the state; imperial in-laws consequently took advantage of this to foment disorder. The source of the Tang’s calamity lay not in regional military commands but in eunuchs’ monopolization of government. This arose because the sovereign was overly familiar with his attendants and kept worthy men at a distance; regional military commanders consequently took advantage of this to rebel against their ruler. The source of the Song’s calamity lay not in the barbarians but in scholar-officials’ disruption of government. This arose because the sovereign strove for generosity and kindness but lacked…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
旌别也故夷狄因之以猾夏夫幾微之際
治亂之係大矣可不謹哉可不慎哉洪惟
我
國家繼天立極其創業垂統以貽謀裕後者
至精至備萬世行矣其處閨門也
恩嚴並用
後宫不得以預政馭閹宦也驅使有職機密
不得以與聞待士夫也忠信重祿秩有禮
矣至於旌别功罪之典考課黜陟之法一
===
毫無假借者此所以百六十餘年之久法
守日嚴人心日定以外戚無干政也以藩
鎮無專制也以夷狄無驕横也一切外患
不生而享國有道之長矣執事又謂天下
之事變每生于意料之弗及而防微杜漸
尤臣子事君之至情以下詢承學予草茆
士也曷足以知此然嘗讀易而知謹微之
漸矣易曰履霜堅氷至蓋言天下之事變
非一朝一夕之故其所由來者漸矣由辨
punctuated:
旌别也，故夷狄因之以猾夏。夫幾微之際，治亂之係大矣，可不謹哉？可不慎哉？洪惟我國家繼天立極，其創業垂統以貽謀裕後者，至精至備，萬世行矣。其處閨門也，恩嚴並用，後宫不得以預政；馭閹宦也，驅使有職，機密不得以與聞；待士夫也，忠信重祿，秩有禮矣。至於旌别功罪之典、考課黜陟之法，一毫無假借者。此所以百六十餘年之久，法守日嚴，人心日定，以外戚無干政也，以藩鎮無專制也，以夷狄無驕横也，一切外患不生，而享國有道之長矣。
執事又謂：「天下之事變，每生于意料之弗及，而防微杜漸，尤臣子事君之至情。」以下詢承學。予草茆士也，曷足以知此？然嘗讀《易》而知謹微之漸矣。《易》曰：「履霜，堅氷至。」蓋言天下之事變，非一朝一夕之故，其所由來者漸矣，由辨
translation_en:
…discriminating judgment; thus the foreign peoples took advantage of this to throw the Chinese realm into disorder. At the point when developments are barely perceptible, the stakes for order and disorder are great indeed. Can one fail to be watchful? Can one fail to be cautious? Reverently considering our dynasty, which succeeds Heaven and establishes the supreme standard, its founding achievements and the succession it established, its plans bequeathed to posterity and provision for later generations, are supremely refined and complete, fit to be followed for ten thousand generations. In managing the inner apartments, it employs both kindness and severity: the rear palace may not participate in government. In controlling eunuchs, it assigns duties to those it employs: they may not be privy to confidential affairs. In treating scholar-officials, it extends loyalty and trust, provides generous emoluments, and orders their ranks according to ritual propriety. As for the regulations distinguishing merit from wrongdoing and the procedures for evaluating performance, dismissing, and promoting, it allows not the slightest indulgence. This is why, for more than 160 years, observance of the laws has grown ever stricter and people’s hearts ever more settled: imperial relatives by marriage have not interfered in government, regional military commanders have not exercised independent authority, and foreign peoples have not behaved arrogantly and wantonly. No external troubles have arisen, and the dynasty has enjoyed the longevity that comes from possessing the Way.
You further state: “Changes in the affairs of the world often arise beyond what can be anticipated; guarding against the imperceptible and blocking harmful developments at their inception is especially expressive of a subject’s utmost devotion in serving his ruler.” You graciously put this question to those pursuing their studies. I am but a scholar of humble station: how could I be qualified to understand this? Yet I have read the Book of Changes and learned about watching over small beginnings as they develop. The Book of Changes says: “Treading on frost, one knows that solid ice is coming.” This means that changes in the affairs of the world do not result from a single morning or evening; what brings them about develops gradually, owing to discernment…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之弗早辨也抑甞讀典謨而知慎德之治
矣書曰與治同道罔不興與亂同事罔不
亡終始慎厥與惟明明后蓋言治亂無常
惟德是與耳君天下者誠能謹于幾微以
清治亂之原而始終慎德以立治道之本
則漢唐宋末流之弊不生而
國家保盈致治之道實在於此請以爲
今日獻
第四問
===
謝寵
同考試官教諭文批文有根據甞究心天文者
考試官教諭張批悉陳象數足驗窮理之學
考試官教授黃批考究精切傑作也
法象莫大乎天地而星曆之職所由詳衍
數莫先乎四時而推步之法所由盡稽諸
古昔欽若昊天敬授人時者布曆之敬也
分命羲和審時驗方者校曆之精也夫推
測天道治曆明時天下萬事莫不由此故
punctuated:
之弗早辨也。抑甞讀典謨而知慎德之治矣。《書》曰：「與治同道，罔不興；與亂同事，罔不亡。終始慎厥與，惟明明后。」蓋言治亂無常，惟德是與耳。君天下者誠能謹于幾微，以清治亂之原，而始終慎德，以立治道之本，則漢唐宋末流之弊不生，而國家保盈致治之道，實在於此。請以爲今日獻。
第四問
謝寵
同考試官教諭文批：文有根據，甞究心天文者。
考試官教諭張批：悉陳象數，足驗窮理之學。
考試官教授黃批：考究精切，傑作也。
法象莫大乎天地，而星曆之職所由詳；衍數莫先乎四時，而推步之法所由盡。稽諸古昔，欽若昊天，敬授人時者，布曆之敬也；分命羲和，審時驗方者，校曆之精也。夫推測天道，治曆明時，天下萬事莫不由此，故
translation_en:
…not having discerned it early enough. Moreover, I have read the Canons and Counsels and learned how government rests on care for virtue. The Book of Documents says: “Those who follow the same way as good government invariably flourish; those who pursue the same affairs as disorder invariably perish. To take care, from beginning to end, over what one associates with—this marks an enlightened ruler.” This means that order and disorder are not constant: they depend solely on virtue. If the ruler of all under Heaven truly attends carefully to the slightest beginnings, thereby purifying the source of order and disorder, and takes care for virtue from beginning to end, thereby establishing the foundation of good government, then the abuses of the declining years of the Han, Tang, and Song will not arise. Here indeed lies the state's way to preserve its fullness and achieve good government. I beg to offer this as my contribution today.
Fourth Question
Xie Chong
Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: “The essay is well grounded; its author has devoted thought to astronomy.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “It fully sets forth celestial phenomena and numerical relationships, amply demonstrating learning devoted to investigating principles.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “Its investigations are precise and pertinent. A masterpiece.”
Among models and patterns, none are greater than Heaven and Earth; through them the duties concerning astronomy and the calendar are elaborated. In developing numerical calculations, nothing takes precedence over the four seasons; through them the methods of astronomical computation are fully worked out. Looking back to antiquity, reverently following August Heaven and respectfully communicating the seasons to the people exemplified the reverence with which the calendar was promulgated. Separately commissioning Xi and He to ascertain the seasons and verify the directions exemplified the precision with which the calendar was checked. Now, calculating the course of Heaven, regulating the calendar, and clarifying the seasons are the basis of every affair under Heaven; therefore…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
古之聖王重之秦火以後曆法不傳久矣
近世考曆者率多牽合疎漏而推測之未
精蔓引膚窺而粗跡之是務紛紛莫定愈
究愈差而終昧夫一定之法端可慨已且
以歲差之說言之古顓帝曆統宗會元之
法也宋熈寧中用之不驗乃改正月建寅
爲建丑以日短星昴爲日短星東壁而更
定新曆及考之顓曆斗差六度歲差一辰
則未及六十年已有推移矣洛下閎謂八
===
百年差一筭者非妄說乎唐大衍曆步歲
候氣之法也宋皇祐中行之不合乃改閏
十二月爲閏正月移立春晷景爲立冬而
更造奉元曆及考之大衍失五十餘刻乃
移其閏是過六十年已有遷轉矣向子信
謂八十年差一度者不近道乎以占候之
失言之下漏之家常患冬月水澁而行遲
夏月水利而行速又疑冬澁而遲者氷澌
所壅也至萬方理之終不應法者何耶蓋
punctuated: 古之聖王重之。秦火以後，曆法不傳久矣。近世考曆者，率多牽合疎漏，而推測之未精；蔓引膚窺，而粗跡之是務。紛紛莫定，愈究愈差，而終昧夫一定之法，端可慨已。且以歲差之說言之，古顓帝曆，統宗會元之法也。宋熈寧中，用之不驗，乃改正月建寅爲建丑，以日短星昴爲日短星東壁，而更定新曆。及考之顓曆，斗差六度，歲差一辰，則未及六十年已有推移矣。洛下閎謂八百年差一筭者，非妄說乎？唐大衍曆，步歲候氣之法也。宋皇祐中，行之不合，乃改閏十二月爲閏正月，移立春晷景爲立冬，而更造奉元曆。及考之大衍，失五十餘刻，乃移其閏，是過六十年已有遷轉矣。向子信謂八十年差一度者，不近道乎？以占候之失言之，下漏之家常患冬月水澁而行遲，夏月水利而行速，又疑冬澁而遲者，氷澌所壅也。至萬方理之，終不應法者，何耶？蓋
translation_en:
…the sage kings of antiquity therefore attached great importance to it. After the Qin burning of books, the calendrical methods long ceased to be transmitted. In recent times, those investigating calendars have generally forced correspondences and left gaps, failing to achieve precision in their calculations. They draw far-fetched connections and examine matters superficially, attending only to their outward traces. Their conflicting accounts yield no settled conclusion; the further they investigate, the further they stray, remaining ignorant of the fixed principles. This is truly lamentable.
To speak first of precession: the ancient calendar of Emperor Zhuanxu provided a method for coordinating calendrical cycles and bringing them together at a common epoch. During the Xining reign of the Song, its application failed to accord with observation. They therefore changed the first month's designation from yin to chou, replaced “the day is shortest, and the culminating constellation is Mao” with “the day is shortest, and the culminating constellation is Dongbi,” and established a revised calendar. Yet comparison with the Zhuanxu calendar showed a discrepancy of six degrees in the Dipper's position and a precessional discrepancy of one celestial sector. Thus a shift had already occurred in fewer than sixty years. Was not Luoxia Hong's assertion that there would be an error of one counting unit [?] in eight hundred years an unfounded claim?
The Tang Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan Calendar) provided a method for calculating the year and determining the seasonal nodes. During the Huangyou reign of the Song, its application failed to agree with observation. They therefore changed an intercalary twelfth month into an intercalary first month, transferred the gnomon-shadow value for the Beginning of Spring to the Beginning of Winter, and newly compiled the Revering the Origin Calendar (Fengyuan Calendar). Comparison with the Dayan Calendar revealed an error of more than fifty ke, or hundredths of a day, whereupon they shifted its intercalary month. Thus, after sixty years, a displacement had already occurred. Was not Xiang Zixin's assertion that the discrepancy amounts to one degree in eighty years close to the truth?
To speak of errors in observation: those who operate water clocks constantly worry that in winter the water flows sluggishly and slowly, while in summer it flows freely and swiftly. They further suspect that its sluggishness and slowness in winter result from obstruction by ice. Yet even after they try every means of correcting this, it still fails to conform to the prescribed standards. Why is this? It is because…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
冬至日行速天運已朞而過表故百刻而
有餘夏至日行遲天運未朞而日至表故
百刻而不及此理旣明以之覆求晷景漏
刻無不合者或以水性之利澁而局方以
求驗不亦迂乎又謂一日之氣卽其短長
播爲刻分則氣至有定數而可占矣今氣
至而交乃頓易刻裒而卒無一定之術者
何耶蓋測日之法以圓法相盪而得裒則
裒無不均以妥法相盪而得差則差有定
===
數此理旣明順循之以索變衡無不通者
或以爲黃道觚而不圓乃强爲數以步之
不亦謬乎以歲運言之相火之下水氣承
之土位之下風氣承之客氣也歲半以前
天政主之歲半以後地政主之主氣也日
之所由爲黃道南北極之中爲赤道天之
二道也南朱北黑東青西白黃道内外各
四幷而爲九者月之九道也十二辰之内
若勝光爲王者向明而治功曹爲歲功成
punctuated:
冬至日行速，天運已朞而過表，故百刻而有餘；夏至日行遲，天運未朞而日至表，故百刻而不及。此理旣明，以之覆求晷景漏刻，無不合者。或以水性之利澁而局方以求驗，不亦迂乎？又謂一日之氣，卽其短長，播爲刻分，則氣至有定數而可占矣。今氣至而交，乃頓易刻裒，而卒無一定之術者，何耶？蓋測日之法，以圓法相盪而得裒，則裒無不均；以妥法相盪而得差，則差有定數。此理旣明，順循之以索變衡，無不通者。或以爲黃道觚而不圓，乃强爲數以步之，不亦謬乎？
以歲運言之，相火之下，水氣承之；土位之下，風氣承之：客氣也。歲半以前，天政主之；歲半以後，地政主之：主氣也。日之所由爲黃道，南北極之中爲赤道：天之二道也。南朱北黑，東青西白，黃道内外各四，幷而爲九者，月之九道也。十二辰之内，若勝光爲王者向明而治，功曹爲歲功成
translation_en:
…At the winter solstice, the sun moves swiftly: heaven has completed its circuit and passed the gnomon, so the interval exceeds one hundred ke. At the summer solstice, the sun moves slowly: heaven has not yet completed its circuit when the sun reaches the gnomon, so the interval falls short of one hundred ke. Once this principle is understood, applying it to reexamine gnomon shadows and water-clock measurements yields agreement in every case. If someone instead confines his method to the ease or resistance with which water flows and seeks verification on that basis, is this not misguided? It is also said that, by taking the length of the day at each solar term and dividing it into ke and their subdivisions, the arrival of the solar term can be predicted by fixed numerical values. Yet why, when a solar term arrives and the transition occurs, do the accumulated ke [?] suddenly change, leaving no consistently applicable procedure? In methods for measuring the sun, calculations by the circular method are combined to obtain an accumulation [?], and these accumulations are invariably uniform; calculations by the tuo method [?] are combined to obtain differences, and these differences have fixed numerical values. Once this principle is understood, following it to investigate variations and balances [?] leaves nothing inexplicable. Some, however, suppose that the ecliptic is angular rather than circular and contrive numerical values to calculate its course. Is this not erroneous?
Speaking of the annual cycles: beneath ministerial fire, water qi sustains it; beneath the position of earth, wind qi sustains it. These are the guest qi. Before the midpoint of the year, the governance of heaven presides; after the midpoint, the governance of earth presides. These are the host qi. The route followed by the sun is the ecliptic, and the circle midway between the north and south poles is the equator: these are heaven’s two paths. Red in the south, black in the north, blue-green in the east, and white in the west, with four paths inside the ecliptic and four outside it, making nine altogether: these are the moon’s nine paths. Among the twelve celestial stations, Shengguang signifies the ruler facing the light and governing, while Gongcao signifies the completion of the year’s work…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而會計小吉爲婚姻酒食之事大吉主文
武大臣之事皆人事也大魁從魁太乙天
罡登明傳送大衝神后之數皆天時也二
十八宿而有三十三度者自日之所行三
百六十五度而分之也又少而爲十七度
半者自黃道之斜直取虛宿以爲斗分也
以天運言之有行黃道之裏者有行黃道
之外者有行黃道之上者有行黃道之下
者蓋一歲一月之中一陰一陽之際各有
===
消長非曆數之可盡也有循度者有失度
者有犯經星者有犯客星者蓋以一那一
剎之中一會一元之間各有四時非世法
之可悉也以推步言之衛朴造宋曆知崇
天蝕限之弱熈寧蝕限之强止運平度而
疾徐得中焉沈存中占雨候知濕土用事
而厥陰難成燥金入候而太陰難伸不待
他求而自臻至理焉楊文鎰謂支干相承
止乎六十儻兩周甲子共成上壽乃失之
punctuated:
而會計，小吉爲婚姻酒食之事，大吉主文武大臣之事，皆人事也。大魁、從魁、太乙、天罡、登明、傳送、大衝、神后之數，皆天時也。二十八宿而有三十三度者，自日之所行三百六十五度而分之也。又少而爲十七度半者，自黃道之斜直，取虛宿以爲斗分也。
以天運言之，有行黃道之裏者，有行黃道之外者，有行黃道之上者，有行黃道之下者。蓋一歲一月之中，一陰一陽之際，各有消長，非曆數之可盡也。有循度者，有失度者，有犯經星者，有犯客星者。蓋以一那一剎之中，一會一元之間，各有四時，非世法之可悉也。
以推步言之，衛朴造宋曆，知崇天蝕限之弱、熈寧蝕限之强，止運平度而疾徐得中焉。沈存中占雨候，知濕土用事而厥陰難成，燥金入候而太陰難伸，不待他求而自臻至理焉。楊文鎰謂支干相承，止乎六十，儻兩周甲子，共成上壽，乃失之
translation_en:
…and the settling of accounts; Xiaoji concerns marriage, wine, and food, while Daji governs the affairs of senior civil and military officials. These all concern human affairs. The numerical correspondences of Dakui, Congkui, Taiyi, Tiangang, Dengming, Chuansong, Dachong, and Shenhou all concern celestial timing. That among the twenty-eight lunar lodges there is one spanning thirty-three degrees results from dividing the 365 degrees traversed by the sun. The smaller span of seventeen and a half degrees derives from the obliquity or directness of the ecliptic, taking the lodge Xu as the basis for the fractional degree associated with Dou [?].
Speaking of celestial motions, some bodies move inside the ecliptic, some outside it, some above it, and some below it. Within each year and month, at each juncture of yin and yang, there are waxing and waning that calendrical calculation cannot fully encompass. Some bodies follow their prescribed courses; others depart from them. Some encroach upon fixed stars; others encroach upon guest stars. Within a single na [?] or a single instant, and within a hui or a yuan cosmic cycle, there are in each case four seasons, which worldly methods cannot fully comprehend.
Speaking of astronomical computation, Wei Pu, in preparing a calendar for the Song, recognized that the eclipse limit of the Chongtian calendar was too small and that of the Xining calendar too large. By using only mean degrees of motion, he struck the proper balance between faster and slower movement. Shen Cunzhong, in predicting the conditions for rain, understood that when damp earth held sway, jueyin—terminal yin—could scarcely develop, and that when dry metal entered its seasonal phase, taiyin—greater yin—could scarcely extend its influence. Without seeking elsewhere, he thereby arrived at the underlying principles. Yang Wenyi said that the succession of earthly branches and heavenly stems goes no further than sixty, and that if the sixty-year cycle were completed twice, together they would constitute the full span of exceptional longevity. Yet his error lay in…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
穿鑿者故苗守信表爲無據之言吳昭素
以新曆經紀爲二卷晨昏日躔刻分各一
卷爲書以獻蓋頗有條理者故元象宗稱
爲閫蘊之書渾儀者測天之器設于崇臺
卽古璣衡以候垂象者也渾象者象天之
器置于密室用水激之以符天行者也韓
顯符造渾儀倣晉孔挺之法而表漏皆遺
其簡畧而無取者乎舒易簡造渾儀用唐
一行之法而頗爲詳悉其齟齬而難行者
===
乎周有馮相氏掌歲月日辰之位保章氏
觀動靜吉凶之變至秦乃合而兼之拜爲
太史之官而占候之職專焉漢太史令以
著述爲宗而兼掌曆象至魏乃析而分之
始有著作郎之置而天官之任重焉以至
史伯知楚之必治而原其祖功史趙知陳
氏之不亡而考其宗德此則知人知天而
明乎治亂之機者矣夫象數理之器也推
測數之精也今之學者膚淺膠固遞相沿
punctuated:
穿鑿者，故苗守信表爲無據之言。吳昭素以新曆經紀爲二卷，晨昏、日躔、刻分各一卷，爲書以獻，蓋頗有條理者，故元象宗稱爲閫蘊之書。

渾儀者，測天之器，設于崇臺，卽古璣衡以候垂象者也。渾象者，象天之器，置于密室，用水激之，以符天行者也。韓顯符造渾儀，倣晉孔挺之法，而表漏皆遺，其簡畧而無取者乎？舒易簡造渾儀，用唐一行之法，而頗爲詳悉，其齟齬而難行者乎？

周有馮相氏，掌歲月日辰之位；保章氏，觀動靜吉凶之變。至秦乃合而兼之，拜爲太史之官，而占候之職專焉。漢太史令以著述爲宗，而兼掌曆象。至魏乃析而分之，始有著作郎之置，而天官之任重焉。以至史伯知楚之必治，而原其祖功；史趙知陳氏之不亡，而考其宗德。此則知人知天，而明乎治亂之機者矣。

夫象數，理之器也；推測，數之精也。今之學者膚淺膠固，遞相沿
translation_en:
…a case of strained interpretation; hence Miao Shouxin characterized it as an assertion without foundation. Wu Zhaosu compiled and presented a work comprising two juan on the principles of the new calendar and one juan each on dawn and dusk, the sun’s course, and subdivisions of time. It was evidently quite well organized, and thus Yuan Xiangzong [?] praised it as a book revealing the subject’s innermost mysteries.

The armillary sphere is an instrument for measuring the heavens, installed on a lofty terrace: it is the ancient rotating mechanism and sighting tube used to observe the phenomena displayed above. The celestial globe is an instrument representing the heavens, placed in an enclosed chamber and driven by water so that it accords with celestial motion. Han Xianfu constructed an armillary sphere following the method of Kong Ting of the Jin, but omitted both the gnomon and the clepsydra. Was it perhaps too rudimentary to be of use? Shu Yijian constructed an armillary sphere using the method of Yixing of the Tang, and it was quite elaborate and comprehensive. Was it perhaps too cumbersome to operate?

Under the Zhou there was the Astronomer, who oversaw the positions associated with the year, month, day, and celestial stations, and the Astrologer, who observed changes in movement and stillness and their auspicious or inauspicious implications. Under the Qin these functions were combined in the office of Grand Astrologer, which had exclusive responsibility for observation and prognostication. Under the Han, the Director of Astronomy took historical writing as his principal task while also overseeing calendrical calculations and celestial phenomena. Under the Wei these functions were separated, and the office of Editorial Director was first established, while the responsibilities of the astronomical office became weightier. Further, Shi Bo knew that Chu would certainly become well governed by tracing its ancestors’ achievements; Shi Zhao knew that the Chen lineage would not perish by examining its ancestral virtue. These were men who understood both human affairs and Heaven and discerned the incipient workings of order and disorder.

Celestial configurations and numbers are the instruments of principle; calculation and measurement are the refinements of numerical knowledge. Scholars today are superficial and rigid, successively following one another…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
習而弗能研究其已然之故是以曆數之
士無慮數百家終無一人有定見以明差
法者善乎孟軻氏曰天之高也星辰之遠
也苟求其故千歲之日至可坐而致矣朱
熹氏曰曆法當先論太虛以見三百六十
五度四分度之一皆有定位然後論天行
以見天度加損虛度之歲分歲分既定然
後七政可齊此二賢據理推測之正論而
學者所當潛心而𠾱求者也雖然愚抑有
===
===
說焉夫觀象數以考天文者曆家之事也
推天以合人者也察天文之順逆以脩德
者君子之事也以人而合天者也有天下
國家者乃若泥象數推測之學而無脩已
畏天之誠信甘石術數之文而鮮尊儒重
道之實將見景星慶雲徒昭佚逸之應而
日食天變諉爲無情之警此王安石之言
所以貽禍于萬世而未已也愚見如此然
杞人之憂隱而切焉不知執事者以爲贅
punctuated: 習，而弗能研究其已然之故。是以曆數之士，無慮數百家，終無一人有定見以明差法者。善乎孟軻氏曰：「天之高也，星辰之遠也，苟求其故，千歲之日至，可坐而致矣。」朱熹氏曰：「曆法當先論太虛，以見三百六十五度四分度之一皆有定位，然後論天行，以見天度加損虛度之歲分。歲分既定，然後七政可齊。」此二賢據理推測之正論，而學者所當潛心而𠾱求者也。雖然，愚抑有說焉。夫觀象數以考天文者，曆家之事也，推天以合人者也；察天文之順逆以脩德者，君子之事也，以人而合天者也。有天下國家者，乃若泥象數推測之學，而無脩已畏天之誠，信甘石術數之文，而鮮尊儒重道之實，將見景星慶雲徒昭佚逸之應，而日食天變諉爲無情之警。此王安石之言所以貽禍于萬世而未已也。愚見如此，然杞人之憂隱而切焉，不知執事者以爲贅
translation_en:
…following established habits, without being able to investigate the reasons why things have come to be as they are. Thus, although specialists in calendrical calculation number in the hundreds of schools, not one possesses a settled understanding that clarifies the methods for correcting discrepancies. Well did Meng Ke say: “High as heaven is and distant as the stars are, if we seek their underlying causes, we can determine the solstices a thousand years hence while remaining seated.” Zhu Xi said: “In calendrical methods, one must first discuss the Great Void, to see that each of its three hundred sixty-five and one-quarter degrees has a fixed position. Only then should one discuss heaven’s movement, to determine the annual fraction by which the degrees of heaven’s movement exceed or fall short of the degrees of the Void [?]. Once the annual fraction is determined, the motions of the Seven Luminaries can be brought into concord.” These are the sound arguments of two worthies who based their calculations on principle; scholars should devote themselves to their earnest investigation [?]. Nevertheless, I venture to offer a further observation.

Observing configurations and numbers to examine celestial patterns is the work of calendrical specialists: they extrapolate from heaven to bring it into accord with human affairs. Examining the regularities and irregularities of celestial patterns in order to cultivate virtue is the work of the gentleman: he brings human conduct into accord with heaven. If those who rule the realm and its states become mired in the study of configurations, numbers, and calculation, without sincerely cultivating themselves and standing in awe of heaven, and trust the writings on technical arts and calculations of Gan and Shi while showing little real respect for Confucian scholars or regard for the Way, then auspicious stars and felicitous clouds will serve merely as signs sanctioning their ease and indulgence, while solar eclipses and celestial anomalies will be dismissed as warnings devoid of intent. This is why Wang Anshi’s words have brought calamity upon countless generations without end. Such is my humble view. Yet my anxiety, like that of the man of Qi who feared that heaven would fall, is deeply felt and urgent. I do not know whether you, sir, will regard these as superfluous…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
言否也
第五問
楊懷哲
考試官敎諭張批以恩信爲今日感化之急
務最是
考試官敎授黃批籌畫斷制確有的見
善捄弊者有通變之法而行之存乎人善
識治者有感化之道而行之盡乎變夫捄
弊無法則弊將日深而小人犯刑感化無
===
道則政將日隳而君子犯義率是道也中
土不可一日焉而况于滇乎此所以廑執
事今日之憂愚也言及之而不敢默且雲
南之地古稱荒服在漢唐則皆叛服不常
在宋則不通於中國元雖兼倂羈縻而已
惟我
聖祖混一區宇裂其地而城池之籍其人而冠
裳之蓋始復帝王之舊以中國之治治之
矣顧承平日久玩愒日滋是以土酋桀驁
punctuated:
言否也。

第五問
楊懷哲

考試官敎諭張批：以恩信爲今日感化之急務，最是。

考試官敎授黃批：籌畫斷制，確有的見。

善捄弊者，有通變之法，而行之存乎人；善識治者，有感化之道，而行之盡乎變。夫捄弊無法，則弊將日深而小人犯刑；感化無道，則政將日隳而君子犯義。率是道也，中土不可一日焉，而况于滇乎？此所以廑執事今日之憂，愚也言及之而不敢默。且雲南之地，古稱荒服，在漢唐則皆叛服不常，在宋則不通於中國，元雖兼倂，羈縻而已。惟我聖祖混一區宇，裂其地而城池之，籍其人而冠裳之，蓋始復帝王之舊，以中國之治治之矣。顧承平日久，玩愒日滋，是以土酋桀驁。
translation_en:
…whether you regard these as superfluous words.

Fifth Policy Question
Yang Huaizhe

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “He takes benevolence and trustworthiness as the urgent means of moral transformation today. This is entirely correct.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “His planning and judgments show genuinely sound insight.”

Those skilled at remedying abuses have methods of adapting to changing circumstances, but putting these into practice depends on people. Those skilled at discerning good governance have a way of transforming people through moral influence, but its full implementation depends on adaptation. If there is no method for remedying abuses, abuses will deepen daily, and petty men will transgress the penal laws. If there is no way of effecting moral transformation, government will deteriorate daily, and gentlemen will violate righteousness. The central lands cannot go a single day without following this way; how much more is this true of Dian? This is what now burdens you, honored examiners, with concern. Though ignorant, I venture to speak of it and dare not remain silent.

The territory of Yunnan was anciently called the remote outer domain. Under the Han and Tang, it repeatedly shifted between rebellion and submission. Under the Song, it had no intercourse with the central realm. Although the Yuan annexed it, their control amounted only to loose rein. Only when our Sagely Progenitor united the realm did he apportion its territory and establish walled cities and moats, register its people and clothe them in caps and robes. Thus he began to restore the ancient order of the sage emperors and kings, governing it by the institutions of the central realm. Yet, as peace has endured for many years, complacency and indolence have increased daily. Consequently, the native chieftains have grown unruly…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
未聞有震懾之者執事曰豈不犯無武之
戒愚則曰馭夷狄如馭犬羊姑惟察其情
順其好惡不服而後威之又不服而後殲
之如此則師直為壯足以讋服其心矣何
桀驁之足虞哉土軍窮困未聞有撫恤之
者執事曰豈不懷寡助之憂愚亦曰凡土
軍本無糧餉苟不節其力均其勞佚則舟
中無非敵國若居閑蠲其戍役而赴敵給
之糗糒則親上死長肘腋之變不生何寡
===
助之足憂哉至於漢人之教誘土酋惟當
申潛通夷寨之令謹姦細漏洩之防使不
得挾漢貨以出入諸夷為耳目以探聽消
息則姦偽之百出者不患其不弭矣漢軍
之逃亡日甚惟當罷官司無名之征禁徵
呼迫逐之擾而又稽餘丁以補役嚴勾察
以清隊則營伍之日虛者不患其不實矣
以關隘言之昔穎國西平之克平大理遂
分兵以下鶴慶麗江收三營之砦破石門
punctuated:
未聞有震懾之者。執事曰：「豈不犯無武之戒？」愚則曰：「馭夷狄如馭犬羊，姑惟察其情，順其好惡，不服而後威之，又不服而後殲之。如此，則師直為壯，足以讋服其心矣，何桀驁之足虞哉？」土軍窮困，未聞有撫恤之者。執事曰：「豈不懷寡助之憂？」愚亦曰：「凡土軍，本無糧餉，苟不節其力，均其勞佚，則舟中無非敵國。若居閑蠲其戍役，而赴敵給之糗糒，則親上死長，肘腋之變不生，何寡助之足憂哉？」至於漢人之教誘土酋，惟當申潛通夷寨之令，謹姦細漏洩之防，使不得挾漢貨以出入諸夷，為耳目以探聽消息，則姦偽之百出者，不患其不弭矣。漢軍之逃亡日甚，惟當罷官司無名之征，禁徵呼迫逐之擾，而又稽餘丁以補役，嚴勾察以清隊，則營伍之日虛者，不患其不實矣。
以關隘言之，昔穎國、西平之克平大理，遂分兵以下鶴慶、麗江，收三營之砦，破石門
translation_en:
…yet I have heard of no one who has struck fear into them. You ask: “Does this not incur the reproach of lacking martial strength?” I would reply: “Controlling the barbarians is like controlling dogs and sheep. First ascertain their dispositions and accommodate their likes and dislikes. Only if they refuse to submit should one intimidate them; only if they still refuse should one annihilate them. In this way, the army derives strength from the justice of its cause, sufficient to overawe their hearts into submission. Why, then, need their defiance cause apprehension?”
The native troops are impoverished and distressed, yet I have heard of no one who has cared for or relieved them. You ask: “Should we not fear having little support?” I would also reply: “Native troops ordinarily receive neither grain allowances nor pay. If their strength is not conserved and their toil and rest equitably apportioned, everyone in the same boat will become an enemy. If, when they are idle, they are exempted from garrison service, and when they face the enemy they are supplied with parched grain and dried rice, they will cherish their superiors and die for their commanders. No upheaval will arise from those close at hand. Why, then, need lack of support cause concern?”
As for Han people instructing and inciting native chieftains, one should reaffirm the prohibition against clandestine dealings with barbarian stockades and guard carefully against spies and the leakage of information. Prevent them from carrying Han goods in and out among the various barbarian peoples and from acting as their eyes and ears to gather intelligence. Then there will be no need to fear that their manifold treacheries and deceptions cannot be suppressed. As for the daily increase in desertions among Han troops, one should abolish the authorities’ unauthorized exactions and prohibit the harassment of demands, summonses, coercion, and pursuit. Furthermore, investigate the surplus males in military households to fill vacancies in service, and rigorously enforce the tracing and inspection of absentees to put the ranks in order. Then there will be no need to fear that the increasingly depleted units cannot be brought up to strength.
As for the strategic passes, in former times, after the Duke of Ying and the Marquis of Xiping conquered and pacified Dali, they divided their forces to take Heqing and Lijiang, captured the stockade at Sanying, and breached Shimen…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之關自此而畧永昌而定百夷是前此猶
有關砦而今皆撤之矣吾恐倉卒有警而
夷兵或反據之我豈無失險之悔邪故設
兵戍守是爲遠圖未可以無虞而忽之也
以屯田言之今瀾滄鶴慶之田膏腴千頃
姦人皆詭作民田利重價之售捐足食之
資於是乎有外夷莊有外夷佃蓋額已損
三之一而冊籍亦倂毁矣吾恐外患不作
變且中起我豈有噬臍之及邪故齎糧召
寇是生厲階未可以細故而輕之也軍儲
之入催科者視爲巳帑旣不足取盈之數
則諉之歲凶逋負何恠乎歲用之不充歟
若推選殷富有行義者主之豈有是耶民
糧之貯充積者將以備荒今地方不宜久
貯而不肯出陳易新何恠乎朽腐之不可
食若一以常平之法處之豈有是耶單快
謂國有五寒今倉廩空虚亦其一矣建官
惟賢任事惟能今顧以遠方目雲南而流
punctuated:
之關，自此而畧永昌，而定百夷。是前此猶有關砦，而今皆撤之矣。吾恐倉卒有警，而夷兵或反據之，我豈無失險之悔邪？故設兵戍守，是爲遠圖，未可以無虞而忽之也。
以屯田言之，今瀾滄、鶴慶之田，膏腴千頃，姦人皆詭作民田，利重價之售，捐足食之資。於是乎有外夷莊，有外夷佃，蓋額已損三之一，而冊籍亦倂毁矣。吾恐外患不作，變且中起，我豈有噬臍之及邪？故齎糧召寇，是生厲階，未可以細故而輕之也。
軍儲之入，催科者視爲巳帑，旣不足取盈之數，則諉之歲凶逋負，何恠乎歲用之不充歟？若推選殷富有行義者主之，豈有是耶？民糧之貯，充積者將以備荒，今地方不宜久貯，而不肯出陳易新，何恠乎朽腐之不可食？若一以常平之法處之，豈有是耶？單快謂國有五寒，今倉廩空虚，亦其一矣。
建官惟賢，任事惟能。今顧以遠方目雲南，而流
translation_en:
… Pass. From there they subdued Yongchang and pacified the various Yi peoples. Thus, formerly there were still fortified passes and stockades, but now all have been dismantled. I fear that, should an emergency suddenly arise, Yi troops might occupy them instead. Would we then have no cause to regret losing these strategic positions? Stationing troops to guard them is therefore a plan for the long term; we must not neglect it merely because there is no immediate danger.
As for military agricultural colonies, the lands at Lancang and Heqing now comprise a thousand qing of fertile fields. Unscrupulous men fraudulently register them as civilian land, seeking the profit from selling them at high prices and forfeiting the resources that ensure adequate provisions. Consequently, there are estates held by outside Yi and tenant farms worked by outside Yi. The registered allotment has already diminished by one-third, and the registers themselves have also been destroyed. I fear that even without an external threat, upheaval may arise within. Would it then be possible to remedy our predicament through futile regret? Supplying provisions that invite raiders thus creates the beginnings of disaster; we must not dismiss this as a minor matter.
Those responsible for collecting revenues for military reserves regard them as their own treasury [?]. When the amounts fall short of the required total, they blame bad harvests and unpaid arrears. How, then, can we be surprised that annual expenditures cannot be met? If prosperous men of upright conduct were selected to oversee these revenues, could this happen? Grain levied from the people is accumulated in storage to prepare for famine. Yet local conditions are unsuitable for prolonged storage, and officials are unwilling to issue the old grain and replace it with new. How can we be surprised that it rots and becomes inedible? If it were managed entirely according to the ever-normal granary system, could this happen? Shan Kuai [?] said that a state has five sources of chilling dread. The present emptiness of the granaries is one of them.
In establishing offices, choose only the worthy; in entrusting duties, choose only the capable. Yet now Yunnan is regarded as a remote region, and the regularly ranked …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
品之官率以廢斥之士充之則負才而矜
邑者乃或怠於自勵其以才能進者又多
跋前疐後而復難於展布劉向謂君子有
五耻今居其位無其言有其言無其行亦
其一矣我思古人寤辟有摽且如漢諸葛
武侯之生擒孟獲置郡治於白崖而不留
一兵以守計若疎矣然諸夷慕德莫不去
山林而居平地是萬代所瞻仰也隋史萬
歲之擊破爨翫勒石碑於濫川且奏請將
===
翫入朝功若偉矣然納賄沉江不一年而
翫復反又萬世之遺臭也漢以從事楊竦
討封離之叛而大破之旣降其二十六種
又奏長吏姦猾侵夷者九十人減死州中
此其得綏夷之道甚可嘉也唐以檢校韋
仁壽按行南寧旣置七州十五縣又因其
豪帥以爲宰牧蠻夷悅服非其能服夷之
心克致是耶夫由前所言則救弊不爲不
周由後所言則用人不可不謹而變通之
punctuated: 品之官，率以廢斥之士充之，則負才而矜邑者，乃或怠於自勵；其以才能進者，又多跋前疐後，而復難於展布。劉向謂君子有五耻，今居其位無其言，有其言無其行，亦其一矣。我思古人，寤辟有摽。且如漢諸葛武侯之生擒孟獲，置郡治於白崖，而不留一兵以守，計若疎矣；然諸夷慕德，莫不去山林而居平地，是萬代所瞻仰也。隋史萬歲之擊破爨翫，勒石碑於濫川，且奏請將翫入朝，功若偉矣；然納賄沉江，不一年而翫復反，又萬世之遺臭也。漢以從事楊竦討封離之叛，而大破之，旣降其二十六種，又奏長吏姦猾侵夷者九十人，減死州中，此其得綏夷之道，甚可嘉也。唐以檢校韋仁壽按行南寧，旣置七州十五縣，又因其豪帥以爲宰牧，蠻夷悅服，非其能服夷之心，克致是耶？夫由前所言，則救弊不爲不周；由後所言，則用人不可不謹，而變通之
translation_en:
…posts in the ranked official service are generally filled with men who have been dismissed or rejected. Those who possess talent yet are resentful [?] may consequently neglect to spur themselves onward; those who advance through ability, moreover, often stumble at every turn and find it difficult to put their abilities to use. Liu Xiang said that a gentleman has five causes for shame. To hold an office without speaking as one should, or to speak without acting accordingly, is one of them. “I think of the men of old; awake, I beat my breast.”

Consider Marquis Wu, Zhuge Liang of the Han: he captured Meng Huo alive and established the commandery seat at Baiya, yet left not a single soldier to defend it. His strategy might seem careless. Yet the various non-Han peoples admired his virtue, and all left the mountain forests to settle on level ground. For this he is looked up to through ten thousand generations. Shi Wansui of the Sui defeated Cuan Wan, had a stone monument inscribed at Lanchuan, and memorialized requesting that Wan be brought to court. His achievement might seem magnificent. Yet he accepted bribes and sank [something] in the river [?]; within a year Wan rebelled again. This, in turn, left a name that stinks through all ages.

The Han commissioned Administrative Assistant Yang Song to suppress Feng Li’s rebellion, and he inflicted a crushing defeat. Having secured the submission of its twenty-six tribal groups, he also reported ninety senior local officials whose deceitful conduct had encroached upon the non-Han peoples; their death sentences were commuted within the province [?]. His grasp of the way to pacify these peoples is highly commendable. The Tang commissioned Acting Official Wei Renshou to make an inspection tour of Nanning. He established seven prefectures and fifteen counties, then appointed their powerful local leaders as magistrates and prefects. The non-Han peoples submitted gladly. Could he have achieved this without winning their hearts?

Thus, on the basis of what was said earlier, the measures for remedying abuses can hardly be considered incomplete; on the basis of what was said afterward, one must exercise care in employing men, and the methods of adapting to circumstances…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
法盡矣而執事復以管子九變之說策其
可否且曰我將以聞于
當宁何其憂之深計之遠耶夫管子之謀非吾
所及愚請以近而易見者言之今夫滇之
民率夷之半焉然皆錯居海服編之圖甲
服食中國之土田供輸公家之稅賦無事
則耒耜而食力有事則踴躍以赴調蓋無
異內綏之良氓而非前代叛服之無常者
但今之治夷者弗為久遠之圖而惟智術苛
===
擾之是務是以黠詐之徒始則革面終則
携貳小則剽掠大則屯聚誠有如前日安
鳳之變者矣于是徙而分之以散其黨革
而錮之以耗其勢嚴文移之防以杜其姦
卒之上之所以處之者日密而下之剝削
以濟其私者日以濫為夷民者方將控訴
之無及而又何怪夫窮而之盜也為今計
者誠能矜其頑愚之罪憫其剝削之苦立
甦息之法以示之恩申誅求之禁以昭之
punctuated: 法盡矣。而執事復以管子九變之說策其可否，且曰：「我將以聞于當宁。」何其憂之深、計之遠耶！夫管子之謀，非吾所及。愚請以近而易見者言之。今夫滇之民，率夷之半焉，然皆錯居海服，編之圖甲，服食中國之土田，供輸公家之稅賦。無事則耒耜而食力，有事則踴躍以赴調，蓋無異內綏之良氓，而非前代叛服之無常者。但今之治夷者，弗為久遠之圖，而惟智術苛擾之是務。是以黠詐之徒，始則革面，終則携貳；小則剽掠，大則屯聚，誠有如前日安鳳之變者矣。于是徙而分之，以散其黨；革而錮之，以耗其勢；嚴文移之防，以杜其姦。卒之，上之所以處之者日密，而下之剝削以濟其私者日以濫。為夷民者，方將控訴之無及，而又何怪夫窮而之盜也？為今計者，誠能矜其頑愚之罪，憫其剝削之苦，立甦息之法以示之恩，申誅求之禁以昭之
translation_en: …the methods of adapting to circumstances have thus been fully set out. Yet you further ask, in this policy question, whether Guanzi’s theory of the nine transformations is practicable, and say: “I shall report this to the sovereign.” How deep your concern and how far-reaching your deliberations! Guanzi’s strategies are beyond my capacities. I venture instead to speak of matters close at hand and readily apparent. Among the people of Dian, roughly half are Yi. Yet they all live intermingled within the realm [?], are enrolled in the tu and jia household registers, draw their sustenance from the lands of China, and deliver taxes to the government. In peaceful times they wield ploughs and live by their own labor; when need arises, they eagerly answer mobilization orders. They are thus no different from the peaceable common people of the interior [?], rather than those of former ages who alternated unpredictably between rebellion and submission. But those who govern the Yi today make no plans for the distant future, devoting themselves solely to cunning devices and oppressive harassment. Consequently, the crafty among them initially display outward compliance but eventually become disaffected; on a small scale they plunder, and on a large scale they gather in armed bands. Indeed, disturbances such as the recent uprising of An Feng have occurred. Thereupon, the authorities relocate and divide them to disperse their followers, dismiss them and bar them from office to diminish their power, and tighten safeguards governing official correspondence to prevent their intrigues. In the end, the measures imposed upon them from above become ever more elaborate, while exploitation by subordinates for private gain grows ever more unrestrained. The Yi people find themselves unable even to lodge complaints. Why, then, be surprised that desperation drives them to banditry? In devising a policy for the present, if only one could show compassion for offenses arising from their obstinacy and ignorance, pity their suffering under exploitation, establish measures allowing them to recuperate as a demonstration of benevolence, and reiterate the prohibition against extortion so as to make manifest to them…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
信梗化則勦之効順則置之構隙則解之
一待以中國之法而不絶之以禽獸如是
則恩信之下魍魎可化而況於夷乎況于
率化之民乎由是執事所謂一切之慮可
以潛消默釋而環滇皆良民矣又何必一
一整頓而勞心以紛更爲也彼服心如諸
葛而善變如管子者其長治之法不知有
加於此者乎是知善治夷者不在乎操縱
智術之繁而在乎恩信以感化之耳矣此
===
固今日之急務而不可緩者否則三營石
門之增戍雖雄鎮矣而疆圉之憂恐未遽
巳也惟執事者其留意以庇我滇民焉幸
甚
punctuated: 信。梗化則勦之，効順則置之，構隙則解之，一待以中國之法，而不絶之以禽獸。如是，則恩信之下，魍魎可化，而況於夷乎？況于率化之民乎？由是，執事所謂一切之慮，可以潛消默釋，而環滇皆良民矣。又何必一一整頓，而勞心以紛更爲也？彼服心如諸葛而善變如管子者，其長治之法，不知有加於此者乎？是知善治夷者，不在乎操縱智術之繁，而在乎恩信以感化之耳矣。此固今日之急務而不可緩者。否則，三營、石門之增戍，雖雄鎮矣，而疆圉之憂，恐未遽巳也。惟執事者其留意，以庇我滇民焉，幸甚！
translation_en: …trustworthiness. If they resist civilizing influence, suppress them; if they demonstrate submission, leave them in peace; if they stir up disputes, resolve them. Treat them uniformly according to the laws of the Central Kingdom, rather than excluding them as birds and beasts. In this way, under benevolence and good faith, even demons could be transformed—how much more so the non-Han peoples, and still more those who already follow our civilizing influence! Thus all the concerns you have mentioned could quietly dissolve, and throughout Yunnan all would be law-abiding people. Why, then, must you set each matter in order individually and weary your mind with a profusion of changes? Even those who could win people's hearts like Zhuge Liang and adapt skillfully like Master Guan—could their methods for securing lasting order surpass this? From this we know that skill in governing non-Han peoples lies not in elaborate techniques of manipulation and calculation, but simply in transforming them through benevolence and good faith. This is indeed an urgent task today that admits of no delay. Otherwise, although the increased garrisons at Sanying and Shimen provide formidable strongholds, I fear that anxieties over the frontier will not soon cease. May you give this your attention and thereby protect our people of Yunnan. That would be a great blessing!

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試錄後序
粤嘉靖甲午秋乃雲貴大比
登賢書成澤也當後錄以終
義則臨文盱衡而賛曰喈蔚
矣哉滇之文乎其士之脩辭
崇古齊軌中州近則有唱第
于臚句魁選於春官者矣茲
===
舉也一一焉彬彬焉限于額
計而弗獲兼登者尚繁有士
蔚矣哉滇之文乎恒言目滇
曰遐域澤也竊載稽古滇域
非遐也青陽黃軒之封壤也
黑水玄禹之導跡也逮德下
衰靡莫據鬼方擾矣建武葉
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試錄後序

粤嘉靖甲午秋，乃雲貴大比，登賢書成。澤也當後錄以終義，則臨文盱衡而賛曰：「喈蔚矣哉，滇之文乎！其士之脩辭崇古，齊軌中州，近則有唱第于臚句、魁選於春官者矣。茲舉也，一一焉，彬彬焉，限于額計而弗獲兼登者，尚繁有士。蔚矣哉，滇之文乎！」恒言目滇曰遐域，澤也竊載稽古，滇域非遐也，青陽黃軒之封壤也，黑水玄禹之導跡也。逮德下衰，靡莫據，鬼方擾矣。建武葉
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Yunnan-Guizhou Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the jiawu year of Jiajing [1534], Yunnan and Guizhou held their great triennial examination, and the register enrolling the worthy was completed. I, Ze, was to append a postface to bring the record’s purpose to completion. Facing the text, I raised my eyes and offered this praise: “How splendid is the literary culture of Dian [Yunnan]! Its scholars refine their language and revere antiquity, keeping pace with the central provinces. Recently, some have had their ranks proclaimed at the court ceremony and have headed the selections of the Ministry of Rites. In this examination, each and every one displayed cultivated accomplishment. Since the number admitted was restricted by a quota, many scholars could not all be enrolled. How splendid is the literary culture of Dian!”

Common speech calls Dian a distant region. Yet I, Ze, have ventured to examine antiquity: Dian is no distant region. It was territory enfeoffed by Qingyang and Huang Xuan [?]; its Black River bears the traces of Xuan Yu’s channeling works [?]. When virtue subsequently declined, the Mimo occupied it and the Guifang caused disturbances. In the Jianwu era, Ye…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
榆氏郡永平蘭津開路德又
下衰而鐵橋阻玉斧畫矣跡
是以論非德盛而流光化行
而服遠乎故曰地過日月之
表誠登三咸五之盛跡也我
太祖高皇帝德隆黃夏業懋炎漢
以世運輪衍之寔五帝之黃
===
也三王之夏也漢又不足言
也滇之啓閉合分足徵之矣
不然何黃夏啓而殷周閉兩
漢合而唐宋分乎故滇文之
蔚也實彰
聖代文治之廣矣大矣况漸漬以
百六十年之育養哉今
punctuated: 榆氏郡，永平蘭津開路。德又下衰，而鐵橋阻、玉斧畫矣。跡是以論，非德盛而流光、化行而服遠乎？故曰：「地過日月之表。」誠登三咸五之盛跡也。我太祖高皇帝德隆黃夏，業懋炎漢，以世運輪衍之寔，五帝之黃也，三王之夏也，漢又不足言也。滇之啓閉合分，足徵之矣。不然，何黃夏啓而殷周閉，兩漢合而唐宋分乎？故滇文之蔚也，實彰聖代文治之廣矣、大矣！况漸漬以百六十年之育養哉！今
translation_en:
…Yeyu was established as a commandery [?], and during the Yongping reign a route was opened at Lanjin. Virtue again declined: the Iron Bridge became a barrier, and the jade axe marked a boundary. Judging from these events, was it not flourishing virtue that spread its radiance, and the extension of civilizing influence that brought distant peoples into submission? Hence the saying: “The territory extends beyond the bounds of the sun and moon.” These were truly splendid achievements, ranking with the Three Sovereigns and matching the Five Emperors.

Our Emperor Taizu Gao possessed virtue as exalted as that of Huangdi and the Xia, and achievements surpassing those of the Han, which ruled under the power of Fire. In the actual succession and unfolding of the ages, he was the Huangdi of the Five Emperors, the Xia ruler among the Three Kings; the Han scarcely merits further mention. Yunnan’s opening and closing, its incorporation and separation, amply attest to this. Otherwise, why was it opened under Huangdi and the Xia but closed under the Yin and Zhou, incorporated under the two Han dynasties but separated under the Tang and Song? Thus the flourishing of literary culture in Yunnan truly manifests the breadth and greatness of our sagely dynasty’s civil governance! How much more so after its gradual permeation by a hundred and sixty years of nurture! Now …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
皇仁聖以文致太平
明詔於文體三致意焉士生兹時
沐浴涵泳能無慨然矣乎詩
曰思皇多士生此王國王國
克生維周之楨子諸士詎以
遐自畫乎奚足以文爲鞶帨
之藻也飾羽之畫也見其外
===
矣未見其內也
聖天子所以寤寐賢雋以臻三五
者如兹而已乎先正有言學
者傳誦云乎哉必也貫乎道
文者苟作云乎哉必也濟乎
義〔澤〕也於斯文無能爲役敢
藉是言爲子諸士誦之以終
punctuated:
皇仁聖，以文致太平，明詔於文體三致意焉。士生兹時，沐浴涵泳，能無慨然矣乎？詩曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。王國克生，維周之楨。」子諸士詎以遐自畫乎？奚足以文爲鞶帨之藻也、飾羽之畫也？見其外矣，未見其內也。
聖天子所以寤寐賢雋以臻三五者，如兹而已乎？先正有言：「學者傳誦云乎哉？必也貫乎道。文者苟作云乎哉？必也濟乎義。」〔澤〕也於斯文無能爲役，敢藉是言爲子諸士誦之，以終
translation_en:
… the Emperor, benevolent and sagely, brings about great peace through cultural cultivation. In his luminous edicts he has repeatedly emphasized literary style. Scholars born in this age, steeped in and nourished by these blessings, cannot fail to be stirred to resolve! The Book of Odes says: “Illustrious are the many scholars born in this royal kingdom. The kingdom indeed brings them forth: they are the pillars of Zhou.” Would you scholars set limits upon yourselves because you live so far away? How could it suffice to treat writing as ornament upon a sash and handkerchief, or as painted decoration upon feathers? That is to see its outward appearance without seeing its inner substance.
Could this alone be what the sagely Son of Heaven seeks when, waking and sleeping, he longs for worthy and outstanding men, so as to attain the achievements of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors? A worthy predecessor said: “Does learning mean merely transmitting and reciting? It must penetrate the Way. Does writing mean merely composing at will? It must give effect to righteousness.” I, [Ze], am incapable of rendering service to this literary tradition, yet venture to borrow these words and recite them to you scholars, so as to bring to completion …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鹿鳴之義
河南開封府陳州商水縣儒
學教諭張澤謹序
punctuated:
鹿鳴之義。
河南開封府陳州商水縣儒學教諭張澤謹序。
translation_en:
…the meaning of “The Deer Cry” (Lu ming).
Zhang Ze, Instructor of the Confucian School of Shangshui County, Chenzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, respectfully composed this preface.

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
雲貴鄉試録序
國家誕昭文德斂才徵言無遠
邇舉孰化率教以奉揚
休命歲甲午寔賓興之期巡按
雲南監察御史董珊矢心在
公遵度維寅飭事維預總兵
官黔國公沐紹勛巡撫副都
===
御史胡訓靖綏崇獎士類聿
興巡撫貴州副都御史戴書
都督僉事楊仁巡按御史王
杏皆秉精合德以觀厥成而
行人席大賓以宣
詔適亦駐玆先是前巡按御史楊
聘考官于列省皆奉慎簡
punctuated:
雲貴鄉試録序

國家誕昭文德，斂才徵言，無遠邇，舉孰化率教，以奉揚休命。歲甲午，寔賓興之期。巡按雲南監察御史董珊，矢心在公，遵度維寅，飭事維預。總兵官黔國公沐紹勛、巡撫副都御史胡訓，靖綏崇獎，士類聿興。巡撫貴州副都御史戴書、都督僉事楊仁、巡按御史王杏，皆秉精合德，以觀厥成。而行人席大賓，以宣詔適亦駐玆。先是，前巡按御史楊，聘考官于列省，皆奉慎簡
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Yunnan–Guizhou Provincial Examination

The dynasty has magnificently displayed its civil virtue, gathered talent, and solicited counsel. People near and far alike have been thoroughly transformed [?] and have followed its teachings, reverently carrying forward its gracious commands. The jiawu year [1534] was indeed the appointed time for honoring and advancing worthy candidates. Dong Shan, Investigating Censor serving as Regional Inspector of Yunnan, pledged himself to the public good, observed the regulations with reverence, and made preparations in advance. Mu Shaoxun, Regional Commander and Duke of Qian, and Hu Xun, Grand Coordinator and Vice Censor-in-chief, maintained peace and offered generous encouragement, and the scholars flourished. Dai Shu, Grand Coordinator of Guizhou and Vice Censor-in-chief; Yang Ren, Assistant Commissioner-in-chief; and Wang Xing, Regional Inspector, all brought sincerity and shared purpose to seeing the undertaking through to completion. Xi Dabin, a Messenger charged with proclaiming an imperial edict, also happened to be staying here.

Before this, the former Regional Inspector, Yang, had sought Examiners from the various provinces, where all respectfully undertook careful selection …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以至〔珠〕與教諭張〔澤〕充考試
官尹〔一仁〕趙〔琬〕李〔純〕文〔大才〕
充同考試官提調則左布政
使張〔峨〕左參政黃〔祺〕監試則
按察使衞〔道〕僉事辛〔東山〕綜
理防範則右布政使袁〔擯〕右
參政馬〔龠〕左參議劉〔彭年〕按
===
察副使鄒〔輗〕車〔純〕僉事劉〔道〕
都指揮僉事馮〔立〕馮〔鳴鳳〕貴
州左布政使周〔忠〕左參政曾
〔鵬〕按察副使林〔茂竹〕馮〔裕〕陳
〔則清〕僉事康〔世隆〕都指揮僉
事田〔茂〕狄〔遠〕逮百執事則罔
不夙夜肅慎以恊于成右參
punctuated: 以至。〔珠〕與教諭張〔澤〕充考試官，尹〔一仁〕、趙〔琬〕、李〔純〕、文〔大才〕充同考試官。提調則左布政使張〔峨〕、左參政黃〔祺〕；監試則按察使衞〔道〕、僉事辛〔東山〕；綜理防範則右布政使袁〔擯〕、右參政馬〔龠〕、左參議劉〔彭年〕、按察副使鄒〔輗〕、車〔純〕、僉事劉〔道〕、都指揮僉事馮〔立〕、馮〔鳴鳳〕，貴州左布政使周〔忠〕、左參政曾〔鵬〕、按察副使林〔茂竹〕、馮〔裕〕、陳〔則清〕、僉事康〔世隆〕、都指揮僉事田〔茂〕、狄〔遠〕。逮百執事，則罔不夙夜肅慎，以恊于成。右參
translation_en:
…and arrived. Zhu [?] and Zhang Ze, Instructor, served as Examiners. Yin Yiren, Zhao Wan, Li Chun, and Wen Dacai served as Associate Examiners.

The Proctors were Zhang E, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Huang Qi, Left Administration Vice Commissioner. Supervising the examination were Wei Dao, Surveillance Commissioner, and Xin Dongshan, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner.

Overall management and security precautions were entrusted to Yuan Bin, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Ma Yue, Right Administration Vice Commissioner; Liu Pengnian, Left Administration Assistant Commissioner; Zou Ni and Che Chun, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Liu Dao, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; and Feng Li and Feng Mingfeng, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners. Those from Guizhou were Zhou Zhong, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zeng Peng, Left Administration Vice Commissioner; Lin Maozhu, Feng Yu, and Chen Zeqing, Surveillance Vice Commissioners; Kang Shilong, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner; and Tian Mao and Di Yuan, Assistant Regional Military Commissioners.

Down to all the functionaries, none failed to exercise solemn care morning and night, cooperating to bring the undertaking to completion. The Right Administration …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
政初果右參議華金副使王
閣僉事杜朝紳都指揮僉事
蕭鼒貴州左參議張楠則先
期入
賀均與賛襄焉廼合提學副使
陳煥暨貴州按察使韓士英
僉事戴亢所選士一千五百
===
===
有奇三試之取中式者五十
有五拜録其名氏與文之優
者以
獻珠乃進諸士告之曰夫文渾
渾噩噩瀚以充矣衍衍繹繹
翕以布矣煒燁灼爛渙諸物
矣髙朗宣融萃諸人矣是故
punctuated:
政初果、右參議華金、副使王閣、僉事杜朝紳、都指揮僉事蕭鼒、貴州左參議張楠，則先期入賀，均與賛襄焉。廼合提學副使陳煥暨貴州按察使韓士英、僉事戴亢所選士一千五百有奇，三試之，取中式者五十有五。拜録其名氏與文之優者以獻。
珠乃進諸士告之曰：「夫文，渾渾噩噩，瀚以充矣；衍衍繹繹，翕以布矣；煒燁灼爛，渙諸物矣；髙朗宣融，萃諸人矣。是故
translation_en:
…Vice Administration Commissioner Chu Guo, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Hua Jin, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Ge, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Du Chaoshen, Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Xiao Zi, and Guizhou’s Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Zhang Nan had entered the imperial court ahead of the appointed time to offer congratulations; all likewise contributed their assistance. Thereupon, the candidates selected by Education Intendant Chen Huan, who held the rank of Surveillance Vice Commissioner, together with those selected by Guizhou Surveillance Commissioner Han Shiying and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Dai Kang, were assembled, numbering more than fifteen hundred. They were examined in three sessions, and fifty-five were selected as successful candidates. Their names and the best of their writings were reverently recorded for presentation to the throne.
Zhu then summoned the candidates forward and addressed them: “Literary culture, in its primal simplicity and wholeness, is vast and all-pervading. Unfolding and developing, it spreads in harmonious unity. Brilliant and radiant, it manifests itself throughout the myriad things. Lofty, luminous, expansive, and harmonious, it finds its concentration in human beings. Therefore…”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
上世會道中世昭文汙世狥
物隆世命人文之變也夫雲
貴古秦黔之徼也前世無文
焉然山川物采固有可紀而
薦者矣隆崇蜿蜒山喬而穎
矣澒洞淵澄水順而靜矣齒
角金貝羽罽文石之屬利用
===
於天下者物珍而富矣人皆
曰此秦黔之文而西南之煥
如者也孰知山川之靈運之
氣機物采之華發之寶藏精
祕所積終當應之人文而後
已耳亦何貴於物之文也
皇上光裕大德作新善類
banxin: 雲貴鄉試錄前序 四
punctuated:
上世會道，中世昭文，汙世狥物，隆世命人，文之變也。夫雲貴，古秦黔之徼也。前世無文焉，然山川物采，固有可紀而薦者矣。隆崇蜿蜒，山喬而穎矣；澒洞淵澄，水順而靜矣；齒角金貝羽罽文石之屬，利用於天下者，物珍而富矣。人皆曰：「此秦黔之文，而西南之煥如者也。」孰知山川之靈，運之氣機；物采之華，發之寶藏。精祕所積，終當應之人文而後已耳，亦何貴於物之文也！
皇上光裕大德，作新善類，
translation_en:
…in highest antiquity, cultural expression accorded with the Way; in the middle age, it manifested refinement; in a debased age, it pursued material things; in a flourishing age, it entrusted responsibilities to men. Such are the transformations of cultural expression. Yunnan and Guizhou were anciently the frontier of Qin and Qian [?]. In former ages they lacked literary culture, yet their mountains, rivers, and the splendor of their natural products certainly offered things worthy of recording and presenting. Towering and winding, their mountains are lofty and outstanding; vast, deep, and clear, their waters flow smoothly and lie still. Ivory, horn, gold, cowries, feathers, woolen fabrics, patterned stones, and other products useful throughout the realm are precious and abundant. People all say: “These are the adornments of Qin and Qian [?], the resplendent beauty of the southwest.” Who realizes that the spiritual potency of these mountains and rivers works through the dynamic forces of vital energy, and that the splendor of their natural products issues from their treasure stores? The accumulated subtle and hidden essences must ultimately find their answering expression in human culture, and only then reach fulfillment. Why, then, prize the adornment of material things alone?
His Majesty has gloriously extended his great virtue and renewed men of worth…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
鴻恩麗澤滂洽海內者十有三
年矣于是兩省逢掖之士咸
祓除振響以揚靈効才於方
嶽之下故玆今日之所薦者
莫非嚮往思奮承休順則之
文渢渢乎可誦可式者矣是
故精深之謂賾鬯達之謂明
===
渾璞之謂醇雋雅之謂則參
伍以變錯綜而通之之謂文
淵乎備矣豈非近被
棫樸菁莪之化遠孕山川物采
之靈毓精會元以闡今日之
郁郁者乎昔者成周三年之
比合六鄉之士考其德行道
punctuated: 鴻恩麗澤滂洽海內者十有三年矣。于是兩省逢掖之士，咸祓除振響，以揚靈効才於方嶽之下。故玆今日之所薦者，莫非嚮往思奮、承休順則之文，渢渢乎可誦可式者矣。是故精深之謂賾，鬯達之謂明，渾璞之謂醇，雋雅之謂則，參伍以變、錯綜而通之之謂文。淵乎備矣！豈非近被棫樸菁莪之化，遠孕山川物采之靈，毓精會元，以闡今日之郁郁者乎？昔者成周三年之比，合六鄉之士，考其德行道
translation_en:
…His vast beneficence and enriching bounty have spread abundantly throughout the realm for thirteen years. Now the scholars in broad-sleeved robes of the two provinces have all purified themselves and made their voices resound, displaying their spirit and offering their talents before the provincial authorities. Thus the writings recommended today all express aspiration and the resolve to strive, receiving imperial favor and following proper standards. Rich and resonant, they merit recitation and emulation.

Profundity is called subtlety; free and lucid expression is called clarity; uncarved simplicity is called purity; distinction and elegance are called exemplary form. Varying these through comparison and bringing them into coherence through interweaving is called literary accomplishment. How profound and complete it is! Surely this flourishing display today arises from the immediate transforming influence celebrated in “Luxuriant Oaks” (Yupu) and “Flourishing Southernwood” (Jing’e), and from the long-nurtured numinous potency of mountains, rivers, and the splendor of their products, fostering essential vitality and gathering primal energies.

Formerly, under the perfected Zhou order, at the triennial assessment, the scholars of the six districts were assembled and examined as to their moral conduct and the Way …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
藝者升之天府是以至德薦
士也今胡以文辭爲哉夫文
莫精於德行莫通於道藝君
子擬之後言議之後動脩辭
立誠而天下之理得矣是謂
天下之至文夫至文無聲至
德無文神而明之存乎其人
===
諸士其知所以自勵者詩曰
辭之輯矣民之洽矣辭之懌
矣民之莫矣諸士脩辭以呈
身而敷辭以安民其何事之
弗濟廼若曲學阿世媚辭售
妍怵聲勢而狥人視民如草
菅而莫之恤者是文之厲也
punctuated:
藝者，升之天府，是以至德薦士也。今胡以文辭爲哉？夫文莫精於德行，莫通於道藝。君子擬之後言，議之後動，脩辭立誠，而天下之理得矣，是謂天下之至文。夫至文無聲，至德無文，神而明之，存乎其人。
諸士其知所以自勵者！詩曰：「辭之輯矣，民之洽矣；辭之懌矣，民之莫矣。」諸士脩辭以呈身，而敷辭以安民，其何事之弗濟？廼若曲學阿世，媚辭售妍，怵聲勢而狥人，視民如草菅而莫之恤者，是文之厲也。
translation_en:
…arts, and advanced those who qualified to the Celestial Treasury. This was to recommend men on the strength of consummate virtue. Why, then, do we now use literary composition? No writing is more refined than moral conduct, nor more comprehensive than the Way and the arts. The gentleman considers before speaking and deliberates before acting; he refines his words and establishes his sincerity, and thereby apprehends the principles of all under Heaven. This is what is called the highest literary refinement under Heaven. Yet the highest literary refinement is soundless, and the highest virtue has no ornament. To comprehend these wondrously and illuminate them rests with the individual.
You scholars should know how to spur yourselves onward! The Book of Odes says: “When words are harmonious, the people are united; when words are pleasing, the people are settled.” If you scholars refine your words to present yourselves and set forth your words to bring peace to the people, what undertaking could fail? But those who distort learning to curry favor with the age, use ingratiating words to peddle their elegance, bow to others in fear of their prestige and power, and regard the people as mere grass and weeds without concern for them—these are the scourge of letters.

雲南都指揮使司經歷司經歷瞿良翰〔周臣，四川達州人，監生〕。雲南都指揮使司斷事司斷事郭選〔登瀛，山東膠州人，監生〕。雲南府晉寧州同知簡敬〔尚賓，江西新喻縣人，監生〕。雲南府昆陽州同知劉隆〔惟脩，江西安福縣人，監生〕。大理府趙州同知毛海〔景學，浙江鄞縣人，監生〕。雲南府易門縣知縣伍惟貞〔元吉，四川榮縣人，監生〕。楚雄府廣通縣知縣皮英〔峻業，江西新淦縣人，丙子貢士〕。大理衛經歷司經歷李純〔一之，直隸華亭縣人，監生〕。平夷衛經歷司經歷陳憲〔天章，四川雅州守禦千戶所籍，監生〕。雲南府經歷司經歷許宸〔覲夫，江西貴溪縣人，監生〕。雲南府昆明縣縣丞陳才〔德夫，四川犍為縣人，監生〕。
translation_en:

text:
