title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
子曰君子道者三我無能焉仁者不憂知
者不惑勇者不懼子貢曰夫子自道也
尊賢則不惑
友也者友其德也不可以有挾也
易
大哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也
豚魚吉信及豚魚也利涉大川乗木舟虛
===
也中孚以利貞乃應乎天也
極天下之賾者存乎卦鼓天下之動者存
乎辭化而裁之存乎變推而行之存乎
通神而明之存乎其人默而成之不言
而信存乎德行
天地之道貞觀者也
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝
以義制事以禮制心
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

子曰：「君子道者三，我無能焉：仁者不憂，知者不惑，勇者不懼。」子貢曰：「夫子自道也。」

尊賢則不惑。

友也者，友其德也，不可以有挾也。

易

大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。

豚魚吉，信及豚魚也。利涉大川，乗木舟虛也。中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。

極天下之賾者存乎卦，鼓天下之動者存乎辭，化而裁之存乎變，推而行之存乎通，神而明之存乎其人，默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。

天地之道，貞觀者也。

書

文命敷于四海，祗承于帝。

以義制事，以禮制心。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “There are three aspects to the way of the gentleman, none of which I am capable of: the benevolent are free from anxiety, the wise from perplexity, and the courageous from fear.” Zigong said: “The Master is describing himself.”

“Honor the worthy, and you will not be perplexed.”

“To befriend someone is to befriend his virtue; one must not rely on any advantage one possesses.”

Book of Changes (Yijing)

“Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure and unalloyed in its essence.”

“‘Good fortune with pigs and fish’ means that trustworthiness extends even to pigs and fish. ‘It is beneficial to cross the great river’ means riding in a wooden boat whose interior is hollow. Inner Sincerity, through beneficial steadfastness, accords with Heaven.”

“To fathom the intricacies of all under Heaven depends on the hexagrams; to stir all movement under Heaven depends on the statements. To transform and give things their appropriate form depends on change; to carry them forward and put them into practice depends on free passage. To comprehend them with spiritual insight depends on the right person. To accomplish silently and inspire trust without speaking depends on virtuous conduct.”

“The way of Heaven and Earth is displayed through steadfast constancy.”

Book of Documents (Shujing)

“His civilizing influence spread throughout the Four Seas, and he reverently served the sovereign.”

“Regulate affairs through righteousness; regulate the heart through ritual propriety.”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
王拜手稽首曰公不敢不敬天之休來相
宅其作周匹休公既定宅伻來來視予
卜休恒吉我二人共貞公其以予萬億
年敬天之休拜手稽首誨言
今爾罔不由慰日勤爾罔或戒不勤
詩
樹之榛栗椅桐梓漆爰伐琴瑟
湛湛露斯在彼杞棘顯允君子莫不令德
其桐其椅其實離離豈弟君子莫不令
===
儀
民之靡盈誰夙知而莫成
載穫濟濟有實其積萬億及秭
春秋
秋八月庚辰公及戎盟于唐〔隱公二年〕
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊〕
〔公十有三年〕秋七月辛巳豹及諸侯之
大夫盟于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕
冬晉人執虞公〔僖公五年〕
punctuated:
王拜手稽首曰：「公，不敢不敬天之休。來相宅，其作周匹休。公既定宅，伻來，來視予卜休恒吉。我二人共貞。公其以予萬億年敬天之休。拜手稽首，誨言。」
今爾罔不由慰日勤，爾罔或戒不勤。

詩
樹之榛栗、椅桐梓漆，爰伐琴瑟。
湛湛露斯，在彼杞棘。顯允君子，莫不令德。其桐其椅，其實離離。豈弟君子，莫不令儀。
民之靡盈，誰夙知而莫成？
載穫濟濟，有實其積，萬億及秭。

春秋
秋八月庚辰，公及戎盟于唐〔隱公二年〕。
春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏〔莊〕〔公十有三年〕。
秋七月辛巳，豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋〔襄公二十有七年〕。
冬，晉人執虞公〔僖公五年〕。
translation_en:
The king bowed with clasped hands and touched his head to the ground, saying: “Duke, I dare not fail to honor Heaven’s favor. You came to inspect the site for the capital, thereby securing a corresponding blessing for Zhou. Having determined the site, you sent a messenger to show me that the divination was favorable and enduringly auspicious. Let the two of us uphold what is right together. Duke, may you help me honor Heaven’s favor for countless years. I bow with clasped hands and touch my head to the ground in acknowledgment of your instructive words.”

Now let all of you follow these exhortations and be diligent each day; let none of you fail to guard against indolence.

Book of Odes

Plant hazel and chestnut, yi trees, tong trees, catalpa, and lacquer trees, to be felled for making qin and se zithers.

Heavy lies the dew upon those willows and thorn trees. The illustrious and trustworthy gentlemen all possess excellent virtue. Those tong trees and yi trees bear fruit in abundant clusters. The gracious and amiable gentlemen all possess excellent deportment.

People do not reach fulfillment: who knows early and achieves only late? [?]

They reap in great numbers; full indeed are their heaps of grain, numbering in myriads, hundreds of millions, and even trillions.

Spring and Autumn Annals

In autumn, in the eighth month, on the gengchen day, the duke made a covenant with the Rong at Tang. 〔Second year of Duke Yin.〕

In spring, the Marquis of Qi and representatives of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕

In autumn, in the seventh month, on the xinsi day, Bao and the grandees of the regional lords made a covenant at Song. 〔Twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang.〕

In winter, the men of Jin seized the Duke of Yu. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
城中城〔成公九年〕
禮記
博聞強識而讓敦善行而不怠謂之君子
命有司為民祈祀山川百源大雩帝用盛
樂乃命百縣雩祀百辟卿士有益於民
者以祈穀實
事君以自顯也
夫樂者先王之所以飾喜也軍旅鈇鉞者
先王之所以飾怒也故先王之喜怒皆
===
得其儕焉喜則天下和之怒則暴亂者
畏之先王之道禮樂可謂盛矣
第貳場
論
脩己以安百姓
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢文帝舉賢良方正能直言極諫者詔〔二年〕
擬唐以孫伏伽為治書侍御史誥〔武德元〕
punctuated:
城中城。〔成公九年〕

禮記
博聞強識而讓，敦善行而不怠，謂之君子。
命有司為民祈祀山川百源，大雩帝，用盛樂。乃命百縣雩祀百辟卿士有益於民者，以祈穀實。
事君以自顯也。
夫樂者，先王之所以飾喜也；軍旅鈇鉞者，先王之所以飾怒也。故先王之喜怒皆得其儕焉：喜則天下和之，怒則暴亂者畏之。先王之道，禮樂可謂盛矣。

第貳場
論
脩己以安百姓。

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢文帝舉賢良方正能直言極諫者詔。〔二年〕
擬唐以孫伏伽為治書侍御史誥。〔武德元〕
translation_en:
The inner city wall was built. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng〕

Record of Rites (Liji)
One who is widely learned and has a strong memory, yet remains modest, and who earnestly practices good conduct without flagging, is called a gentleman.
Order the responsible officials to offer prayers and sacrifices on behalf of the people to the mountains, rivers, and numerous springs, and to perform the great rain sacrifice to the Supreme God, employing grand music. Then order the hundred districts to perform rain sacrifices to former lords, ministers, and officers who benefited the people, praying for a full grain harvest.
Serving one’s ruler is a means of making oneself illustrious.
Music was the means by which the former kings gave fitting expression to joy; armies and executioners’ axes were the means by which they gave fitting expression to anger. Thus the joy and anger of the former kings each found their proper expression: when they rejoiced, all under Heaven joined in harmony with them; when they were angry, the violent and disorderly feared them. In the Way of the former kings, rites and music may be called fully developed indeed.

Second Session
Discourse
Cultivate oneself so as to bring peace to the common people.

Imperial Edict, Proclamation, and Memorial 〔One question from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Wen of the Han calling for the recommendation of worthy, upright men capable of speaking frankly and remonstrating fully. 〔Second year〕
Compose a Tang proclamation appointing Sun Fuga as Censor for Judicial Review. 〔First year of Wude …〕

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
〔年〕
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表〔元祐元〕
〔年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
荒蕪田地
服舍違式
優恤軍屬
聽訟廻避
===
第叁場
策五道
問帝王之治本諸學帝王之學本諸心堯
舜禹湯文武之治蕩蕩巍巍弗可尚已
一皆本之心學以見之事功者其曰人
心惟危道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中
者羣聖傳心致治之要法也降及嬴秦
無論焉漢高帝不事詩書然恢濶大度
事多暗合于古人唐太宗不及禮樂而
punctuated:
〔年〕
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表〔元祐元〕〔年〕。
判語〔五條〕：官吏給由；荒蕪田地；服舍違式；優恤軍屬；聽訟廻避。
第叁場
策五道
問：帝王之治本諸學，帝王之學本諸心。堯舜禹湯文武之治，蕩蕩巍巍，弗可尚已，一皆本之心學，以見之事功者。其曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」者，羣聖傳心致治之要法也。降及嬴秦，無論焉。漢高帝不事詩書，然恢濶大度，事多暗合于古人。唐太宗不及禮樂，而
translation_en:
…year).

Compose a memorial of thanks for the Song appointment of Cheng Yi as Expositor in Chongzheng Hall (first year of Yuanyou).

Legal judgments (five topics): issuing certificates of service to officials and clerks; uncultivated farmland; clothing and dwellings that violate prescribed regulations; preferential relief for military dependents; recusal in hearing lawsuits.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The government of emperors and kings is rooted in learning, and their learning is rooted in the mind. The government of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu was so vast and lofty that it could not be surpassed. In every case, it was rooted in the learning of the mind and manifested in practical achievements. The saying, “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning; be single-minded. Hold faithfully to the mean,” expresses the essential method by which the sages transmitted their understanding of the mind and brought about good government.

Coming down to the Qin under the Ying house, we need not discuss it. Emperor Gao of Han did not devote himself to the Odes and Documents, yet he was broad-minded and magnanimous, and his actions often accorded unawares with those of the ancients. Taizong of Tang fell short in ritual and music, yet…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
好賢納諫駸駸乎熈皡之風焉宋太祖
陽施陰構事亦譎矣然崇儒重道卒致
乾德開寶之治是三君者果天資之美
不學而能歟抑有得於心學之助歟我
太祖高皇帝丕顯之謨
太宗文皇帝丕承之烈直與二帝三王之治並
稱矣其在當時大廷便殿老臣宿儒相
與從容咨訪莫非精一執中之道觀心
有亭洪範有註論正心之章正而確揭
===
明德之典簡而明其法天運精育神復
命之道一皆心學之傳淵乎微矣然亦
可得而悉言歟我
皇上御極十有三年勵精圖治明物察倫仁孝
誠敬之道直接乎精一執中之傳其所
以脩之深宮而見之大廷以達之天下
者煥若日星則又與我
聖祖神宗其道固脗合而無間者也諸士子能
敬陳而三嘆之歟抑以觀仰
punctuated: 好賢納諫，駸駸乎熈皡之風焉。宋太祖陽施陰構，事亦譎矣，然崇儒重道，卒致乾德、開寶之治。是三君者，果天資之美，不學而能歟？抑有得於心學之助歟？我太祖高皇帝丕顯之謨、太宗文皇帝丕承之烈，直與二帝三王之治並稱矣。其在當時，大廷便殿，老臣宿儒，相與從容咨訪，莫非精一執中之道。觀心有亭，洪範有註，論正心之章正而確，揭明德之典簡而明。其法天運精、育神復命之道，一皆心學之傳，淵乎微矣！然亦可得而悉言歟？我皇上御極十有三年，勵精圖治，明物察倫，仁孝誠敬之道，直接乎精一執中之傳。其所以脩之深宮而見之大廷，以達之天下者，煥若日星，則又與我聖祖神宗，其道固脗合而無間者也。諸士子能敬陳而三嘆之歟？抑以觀仰
translation_en: …he cherished worthy men and accepted remonstrance, steadily approaching the spirit of radiant harmony. Emperor Taizu of the Song bestowed favors openly while plotting in secret; his actions, too, were devious. Yet he honored Confucian scholars and esteemed the Way, ultimately bringing about the good government of the Qiande and Kaibao eras. Did these three rulers truly possess such excellent natural endowments that they could accomplish this without learning? Or did they benefit from the assistance of learning of the mind? The illustrious plans of our Emperor Taizu Gao and the achievements of our Emperor Taizong Wen in grandly carrying on his legacy rank alongside the government of the Two Emperors and Three Kings. In their day, whether in the great court or the private audience halls, they consulted senior ministers and learned Confucian scholars at leisure: everything concerned the Way of refinement and single-mindedness and holding fast to the Mean. There was a pavilion for contemplating the mind and a commentary on the Great Plan. The chapter discussing rectification of the mind was sound and precise; the exposition setting forth luminous virtue was concise and clear. Their Way of emulating Heaven and circulating vital essence, nurturing the spirit and returning to the source of life, all belonged to the transmission of learning of the mind. How profound and subtle it was! Yet can it also be expounded in full? Our reigning emperor has occupied the throne for thirteen years, applying himself earnestly to good government, discerning things and examining human relationships. His Way of benevolence, filial devotion, sincerity, and reverence directly continues the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness and holding fast to the Mean. What he cultivates deep within the palace, manifests in the great court, and extends throughout the realm shines like the sun and stars. His Way is indeed wholly consonant with that of our sage progenitor and divine ancestor, without any divergence. Can you candidates respectfully set this forth and acclaim it repeatedly? This may also serve to contemplate and look up to …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖明心之學
問太平作樂所以和神人合上下六律調
而後五音正理固然也周禮謂樂六變
則天神皆降八變則地祇皆出九變則
人鬼可享其變法可得聞歟漢書以五
音配於五行而考其德月令以六律分
於五方而應其時或謂吕有上生而無
下生又謂納音不同於納甲其詳可得
言歟太蔟一也天以為徵地以為角姑
===
===
洗一也地以為徵天以為羽其義果何
用歟圜丘樂有圜鍾方澤樂有函鍾其
名何以異三鍾之變皆會于卯其意何
以同唐無徵音說者謂李嗣真求得於
弩營之中宋無商聲說者謂蔡元定惡
其有陵君之象然歟否歟鄭譯條從相
生為八十四調元稹宫調改革為八十
一調是歟非歟樂記所稱君臣民事物
咸寓於音亂則有殃樂元語所記四夷
punctuated:
聖明心之學。

問：太平作樂，所以和神人、合上下。六律調而後五音正，理固然也。《周禮》謂樂六變則天神皆降，八變則地祇皆出，九變則人鬼可享，其變法可得聞歟？《漢書》以五音配於五行而考其德，《月令》以六律分於五方而應其時。或謂吕有上生而無下生，又謂納音不同於納甲，其詳可得言歟？太蔟一也，天以為徵，地以為角；姑洗一也，地以為徵，天以為羽，其義果何用歟？圜丘樂有圜鍾，方澤樂有函鍾，其名何以異？三鍾之變皆會于卯，其意何以同？唐無徵音，說者謂李嗣真求得於弩營之中；宋無商聲，說者謂蔡元定惡其有陵君之象。然歟否歟？鄭譯條從相生為八十四調，元稹宫調改革為八十一調，是歟非歟？《樂記》所稱君臣民事物，咸寓於音，亂則有殃。《樂元語》所記四夷
translation_en:
…the learning of the mind of His Sagely Majesty.

Question: Music is instituted in times of peace to bring spirits and human beings into harmony and unite those above and below. Only after the six pitch standards are attuned are the five notes correct: this is indeed the natural principle. The Rites of Zhou states that after six musical transformations all the celestial spirits descend, after eight all the terrestrial spirits emerge, and after nine the spirits of the dead can receive offerings. May we hear how these transformations are performed? The History of the Han pairs the five notes with the Five Phases and examines their properties; the Monthly Ordinances distributes the six pitch standards among the five directions to accord with their seasons. Some say that the lü pitches are generated upward but never downward, and that the system of nayin, assigning notes, differs from that of najia, assigning the heavenly stems. Can you explain these matters in detail? Taicu is a single pitch, yet Heaven takes it as zhi and Earth as jue; guxian is a single pitch, yet Earth takes it as zhi and Heaven as yu. What purpose, indeed, do these relationships serve? The music of the Circular Mound includes huanzhong, while that of the Square Marsh includes hanzhong: why do their names differ? The transformations of the three zhong pitches all converge at mao, the fourth earthly branch: why do they share this significance?

The Tang lacked the zhi note, and commentators say that Li Sizhen found it in a crossbow camp. The Song lacked the shang note, and commentators say that Cai Yuanding disliked its symbolism of encroaching upon the ruler. Are these claims true or not? Zheng Yi arranged the successive generation of pitches into eighty-four modes; Yuan Zhen reformed the gong modes into eighty-one modes. Are these accounts correct or incorrect? The ruler, ministers, people, affairs, and things mentioned in the Record of Music are all embodied in the notes; when these are disordered, calamity follows. As for the peoples of the four outer regions recorded in the Primordial Sayings on Music (Yue yuanyu) …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
制樂曰䟽禁昧離皆先王所作以順天
時亦必有說矣願詳言之以見考古之
學
問漢人尚評晉人尚駁皆私議也今與諸
士秉公議以尚論古人可乎漢高帝懲
亡秦孤立之失大封同姓及異姓功臣
以分制疆宇周以固矣然未及數世而
功臣徹侯誅戮殆盡至哀平之世中外
俱弱不可支持議者以漢有呂新之禍
===
多歸咎於外戚不知所以致此者果外
戚歟抑別有故歟唐太宗承亡隋極亂
之後大振乾綱以成不世之功宏以遠
矣然未及數世而政權下移國祚日傾
逮僖昭之世冠舄倒置不可捄藥議者
以唐有安朱之禍多歸咎於藩鎮不知
所以致此者果藩鎮歟抑別有故歟宋
藝祖厭五季兵戈之亂釋兵權戒殺戮
以安天下之民厚而仁矣然未及中葉
punctuated:
制樂曰䟽、禁、昧、離，皆先王所作，以順天時，亦必有說矣。願詳言之，以見考古之學。

問：漢人尚評，晉人尚駁，皆私議也。今與諸士秉公議，以尚論古人，可乎？漢高帝懲亡秦孤立之失，大封同姓及異姓功臣，以分制疆宇，周以固矣。然未及數世，而功臣徹侯誅戮殆盡。至哀、平之世，中外俱弱，不可支持。議者以漢有呂、新之禍，多歸咎於外戚。不知所以致此者，果外戚歟？抑別有故歟？唐太宗承亡隋極亂之後，大振乾綱，以成不世之功，宏以遠矣。然未及數世，而政權下移，國祚日傾。逮僖、昭之世，冠舄倒置，不可捄藥。議者以唐有安、朱之禍，多歸咎於藩鎮。不知所以致此者，果藩鎮歟？抑別有故歟？宋藝祖厭五季兵戈之亂，釋兵權，戒殺戮，以安天下之民，厚而仁矣。然未及中葉
translation_en:
…established music called Shu, Jin, Mei, and Li [?], all created by the former kings to accord with the seasons of Heaven: surely there must also be an explanation for this. Please discuss these matters in detail, demonstrating your learning in the study of antiquity.

Question: Men of the Han prized appraisal, and men of the Jin prized disputation; these were all private judgments. May we now join you gentlemen in maintaining impartial judgment to discuss the men of antiquity?

Emperor Gao of the Han, taking warning from the fatal isolation of the fallen Qin, extensively enfeoffed members of his own surname and meritorious servants of other surnames, dividing control of the realm among them. His arrangements were comprehensive and secure. Yet within only a few generations, the meritorious servants who held the rank of marquis had almost all been executed. By the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping, both the central government and the outlying regions were weak, and the dynasty could no longer sustain itself. Those discussing the calamities brought upon the Han by the Lü clan and the Xin dynasty mostly lay the blame on imperial affinal relatives. But were imperial affinal relatives truly the cause, or was there some other reason?

Emperor Taizong of the Tang succeeded to the extreme disorder left by the fallen Sui. He vigorously asserted sovereign authority and accomplished achievements rarely equaled in any age. His work was grand and far-reaching. Yet within only a few generations, political power had shifted into subordinate hands, and the dynasty’s fortunes declined daily. By the reigns of Emperors Xizong and Zhaozong, caps and shoes had exchanged places—the hierarchy was inverted—and the situation was beyond remedy. Those discussing the calamities brought upon the Tang by An Lushan and Zhu Wen mostly lay the blame on regional military commands. But were regional military commands truly the cause, or was there some other reason?

The founding ancestor of the Song, weary of the warfare and disorder of the Five Dynasties, relinquished military authority [on the part of his commanders] and enjoined restraint in killing, bringing peace to the people of the realm. His policies were generous and humane. Yet before the dynasty had reached its middle period…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而徽欽北狩高宗南遷逮至理度之季
大勢已去而竟不可支矣議者以宋有
金元之禍多歸咎於夷狄不知所以致
此者果夷狄歟抑别有故歟我
聖祖繼天立極創業垂統其宏綱大要以貽謀
後世者至精至備真能超三軼五而萬
世可行矣故外戚無干政也藩鎮無專
制也夷狄無驕橫也恩威行而情法盡
烏有漢唐宋末流之弊哉然天下之事
===
變每生於意料之所弗及而防微杜漸
尤臣子事君之至情今諸士幸際
聖明正忠言讜論得以自陳之日也其漢唐宋
致釁之由與我
國家今日所以持盈保治以衍億萬年無疆
之休者願詳言之毋隱
問象數之學其來尚矣近世考曆者或推
測之未精而談數者多粗迹之是務故
不能無可質者夫歲差之說古有之矣
punctuated:
而徽欽北狩，高宗南遷，逮至理度之季，大勢已去，而竟不可支矣。議者以宋有金元之禍，多歸咎於夷狄，不知所以致此者，果夷狄歟？抑别有故歟？我聖祖繼天立極，創業垂統，其宏綱大要以貽謀後世者，至精至備，真能超三軼五，而萬世可行矣。故外戚無干政也，藩鎮無專制也，夷狄無驕橫也。恩威行而情法盡，烏有漢唐宋末流之弊哉？然天下之事變，每生於意料之所弗及，而防微杜漸，尤臣子事君之至情。今諸士幸際聖明，正忠言讜論得以自陳之日也。其漢唐宋致釁之由，與我國家今日所以持盈保治，以衍億萬年無疆之休者，願詳言之，毋隱。

問：象數之學，其來尚矣。近世考曆者，或推測之未精，而談數者，多粗迹之是務，故不能無可質者。夫歲差之說，古有之矣。
translation_en:
…yet Huizong and Qinzong went on their “northern hunt” [were taken captive], and Gaozong moved south. By the closing years of Lizong and Duzong, the dynasty’s position was already lost, and it ultimately could no longer sustain itself. Those who discuss the calamities inflicted on the Song by the Jin and Yuan mostly lay the blame on the non-Chinese peoples. Yet was it really these peoples who brought this about, or was there some other cause? Our Sagely Progenitor succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard, founded the dynasty, and handed down its rule. The broad principles and essentials by which he provided for later generations were supremely refined and complete. They truly surpassed the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors and could be put into practice for ten thousand generations. Thus imperial in-laws do not interfere in government, regional military commands do not exercise independent power, and non-Chinese peoples do not behave with arrogance and violence. Benevolence and authority prevail, and both human circumstances and the law receive their full due. How could the abuses of the declining Han, Tang, and Song arise?

Yet upheavals in the world often arise beyond the reach of anticipation. To guard against the slightest signs and forestall gradually developing dangers is, above all, the fullest expression of a subject’s devotion in serving his ruler. You gentlemen are now fortunate to live under a sagacious sovereign: this is precisely the time when you may personally present loyal counsel and forthright arguments. Please explain in detail, concealing nothing, the causes that brought disaster upon the Han, Tang, and Song, and the means by which our state today may preserve its flourishing condition and maintain good government, extending its boundless blessings for countless millions of years.

Question: The study of images and numbers has a long history. In recent times, those who investigate calendrical systems have sometimes lacked precision in their calculations, while those who discuss numbers have mostly concerned themselves with superficial manifestations. There are therefore matters that call for examination. The theory of annual precession has existed since antiquity.

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
顓帝曆者實統宗會元之法宋熙寧中
用之不驗乃改正月建寅爲建丑以日
短星昴爲日短星東壁而更定新曆然
則洛下閎所謂八百年差一筭者果相
合否乎唐大衍曆者得步歲候氣之詳
宋皇祐中行之不合乃改閏十二月爲
閏正月移立春晷景爲立冬而造奉元
曆然則向子信所記八十年差一度者
又相合否乎占候之失古亦有之矣或
===
謂下漏家常患冬月水澁夏月水利以
爲水性之常又疑冰澌所壅萬方理之
終不應法然則得其傳者必有所櫽矣
或謂一日之氣卽其短長播爲刻分至
交一氣則頓易刻襄黃道觚而不圓縱
有强爲數以步之者亦非秉理用筭然
則盡其妙者必有可考矣若歲運又有
主氣客氣之分天月亦有二道九道之
異十二辰而有天時人事之別二十八
punctuated: 顓帝曆者，實統宗會元之法。宋熙寧中用之不驗，乃改正月建寅爲建丑，以日短星昴爲日短星東壁，而更定新曆。然則洛下閎所謂八百年差一筭者，果相合否乎？唐大衍曆者，得步歲候氣之詳。宋皇祐中行之不合，乃改閏十二月爲閏正月，移立春晷景爲立冬，而造奉元曆。然則向子信所記八十年差一度者，又相合否乎？占候之失，古亦有之矣。或謂下漏家常患冬月水澁、夏月水利，以爲水性之常，又疑冰澌所壅，萬方理之，終不應法。然則得其傳者，必有所櫽矣。或謂一日之氣，卽其短長播爲刻分，至交一氣，則頓易刻襄，黃道觚而不圓，縱有强爲數以步之者，亦非秉理用筭。然則盡其妙者，必有可考矣。若歲運，又有主氣、客氣之分；天月亦有二道、九道之異；十二辰而有天時、人事之別；二十八
translation_en:
…The calendar of Emperor Zhuan is indeed a method for unifying the fundamental cycles and bringing their epochs into conjunction [?]. During the Xining reign period of the Song, its use failed to accord with observation. Accordingly, the first month was changed from correspondence with the earthly branch yin to correspondence with chou; “at the shortest day, the culminating asterism is Mao” was changed to “at the shortest day, the culminating asterism is Dongbi”; and a new calendar was established. Does this actually agree with Luoxia Hong’s statement that an error of one counting unit accumulates in eight hundred years?

The Tang Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li) provided detailed methods for calculating the year and determining the solar terms. During the Huangyou reign period of the Song, its application failed to agree with observation. Accordingly, an intercalary twelfth month was changed to an intercalary first month, the gnomon shadow for the Beginning of Spring was reassigned to the Beginning of Winter, and the Upholding the Origin Calendar (Fengyuan li) was compiled. Does this, in turn, agree with Xiang Zixin’s record of an error of one degree in eighty years?

Errors in celestial observation and prognostication also occurred in antiquity. Some say that those who operate water clocks constantly find that water flows sluggishly in winter and readily in summer. They regard this as water’s normal nature, yet also suspect obstruction by floating ice. Although they try every means to correct it, the result never conforms to the prescribed method. Those who have received the transmitted knowledge must therefore possess some means of adjustment [?].

Some say that the qi of each day is apportioned into time divisions and fractions according to that day’s length. Upon the transition to another solar term, the time divisions are abruptly changed [?], making the ecliptic angular rather than circular. Even if someone forces numerical values into a scheme to calculate it, this is still not calculation grounded in principle. There must therefore be something ascertainable in the methods of those who fully comprehend its subtleties.

As for the annual cycles, there is also a distinction between host qi and guest qi. For heaven and the moon [?], there is likewise a difference between two paths and nine paths. Within the twelve earthly branches, there is a distinction between celestial timing and human affairs; and among the twenty-eight…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
宿而有三十三度十七度半之殊其詳
可得聞歟天運之周有行黃道之裏者
有行黃道之外者有行黃道之上者有
行黃道之下者有循度者有失度者有
犯經星者有犯客星者其義果何謂歟
有推步日蝕而知其強弱之限有占測
雨候而得其晦暘之宜有增六十甲子
而成上壽之數有獻九卷新曆而更乾
元之制者其人之得失可悉言歟渾儀
===
渾象之制何以不同韓顯符舒易簡之
造孰為詳略馮相保章分職也至何時
而兼太史占候兼官也至何時而分若
有以祝融之功而推楚之治以虞舜之
德而占陳之存其有關於世道亦大矣
幸盡言之毋忽
問雲南乃古秦黔之地遠在邊徼控御惟
難自我
聖祖龍興混一區宇懷遠為近一以中國治之
punctuated:
宿而有三十三度、十七度半之殊，其詳可得聞歟？天運之周，有行黃道之裏者，有行黃道之外者，有行黃道之上者，有行黃道之下者，有循度者，有失度者，有犯經星者，有犯客星者，其義果何謂歟？有推步日蝕而知其強弱之限，有占測雨候而得其晦暘之宜，有增六十甲子而成上壽之數，有獻九卷新曆而更乾元之制者，其人之得失可悉言歟？渾儀、渾象之制何以不同？韓顯符、舒易簡之造孰為詳略？馮相、保章分職也，至何時而兼？太史、占候兼官也，至何時而分？若有以祝融之功而推楚之治，以虞舜之德而占陳之存，其有關於世道亦大矣。幸盡言之，毋忽。
問：雲南乃古秦黔之地，遠在邊徼，控御惟難。自我聖祖龍興，混一區宇，懷遠為近，一以中國治之。
translation_en:
…the lunar lodges differ in extent, some spanning thirty-three degrees and others seventeen and a half degrees. May we hear the details? In the circuit of celestial motion, some bodies travel inside the ecliptic, some outside it, some above it, and some below it. Some follow their prescribed courses, while others stray from them; some encroach upon fixed stars, and others upon guest stars. What precisely do these phenomena signify?
Some have calculated solar eclipses and determined the limits of their greater and lesser magnitudes [?]; some have predicted conditions for rain and ascertained the appropriate alternation of overcast and clear weather; some have added a sixty-year sexagenary cycle to arrive at the number constituting the highest longevity [?]; and some have presented a new calendar in nine juan to replace the Qianyuan system. Can you explain fully these men's successes and failures? How do the designs of the armillary sphere and the celestial globe differ? Of the instruments made by Han Xianfu and Shu Yijian, which was more detailed and which simpler? The duties of the fengxiang and baozhang officers—those responsible for calendrical observation and celestial prognostication—were separate: when were they combined? The Grand Astrologer's office and the office responsible for observation and prognostication were combined: when were they separated?
As for inferring the good government of Chu from the achievements of Zhurong, or predicting the survival of Chen from the virtue of Yu Shun, these matters have considerable bearing on the course of human affairs. Please discuss them fully, neglecting nothing.
Question: Yunnan is the territory of ancient Qin and Qian [?]. Situated far away on the frontier, it is particularly difficult to control and govern. Since our Sagely Progenitor rose like a dragon and united the realm, he has cherished distant peoples as though they were near and governed them uniformly according to the practices of the Central Kingdom…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
法至備矣奈何承平旣久玩愒日滋亦
有當思患而預防者何也夫狼子野心
賓貢愆度土酋之桀驁甚矣未聞有懾
而震之者豈不犯無武之戒生計蕭條
賦役繁重土軍之窮困極矣未聞有撫
而恤之者豈不懷寡助之憂土酋之桀
驁固也而多惑於漢人之敎誘姦偽百
出果何道以禁之乎土軍之窮困固也
而又加以漢軍之逃亡營伍日虛果何
===
道以實之乎關隘設險夷夏之大防也
而石門失守三營罷戍則中國反受制
於外夷屯田額徵兵食之大計也而重
價求售以軍作民則外夷多置莊於中
國軍衞之儲每歲用之不充而有司積
貯者多朽腐而不可食所謂國有五寒
者非歟流品之官多取於廢斥之輩而
以才能進者又齟齬而不可行所謂君
子有五耻者非歟古之入滇者有置郡
punctuated: 法至備矣。奈何承平旣久，玩愒日滋，亦有當思患而預防者，何也？夫狼子野心，賓貢愆度，土酋之桀驁甚矣，未聞有懾而震之者，豈不犯無武之戒？生計蕭條，賦役繁重，土軍之窮困極矣，未聞有撫而恤之者，豈不懷寡助之憂？土酋之桀驁固也，而多惑於漢人之敎誘，姦偽百出，果何道以禁之乎？土軍之窮困固也，而又加以漢軍之逃亡，營伍日虛，果何道以實之乎？關隘設險，夷夏之大防也，而石門失守，三營罷戍，則中國反受制於外夷。屯田額徵，兵食之大計也，而重價求售，以軍作民，則外夷多置莊於中國。軍衞之儲，每歲用之不充，而有司積貯者，多朽腐而不可食，所謂國有五寒者非歟？流品之官，多取於廢斥之輩，而以才能進者，又齟齬而不可行，所謂君子有五耻者非歟？古之入滇者，有置郡
translation_en:
…the regulations are most comprehensive. Yet now that peace has long prevailed, negligence and idleness increase daily. There are also matters that require us to anticipate trouble and take precautions. What are they? With the untamed disposition of wolf cubs, the native chieftains transgress the prescribed rules for attendance at court and tribute. Their defiance is extreme, yet we hear of no one who has overawed and intimidated them. Does this not incur the admonition against lacking military preparedness? Livelihoods languish, while taxes and labor services are onerous. The native troops suffer extreme poverty and distress, yet we hear of no one who has comforted and relieved them. Should this not cause concern that we have too little support? The native chieftains are indeed defiant, but they are often misled by the instruction and enticements of Han Chinese, with treachery and deceit emerging in countless forms. By what means can these truly be restrained? The native troops are indeed impoverished, but in addition, Han Chinese troops desert, leaving the ranks emptier by the day. By what means can they truly be replenished?

Fortifying strategic passes provides the great barrier between the non-Chinese peoples and the Chinese. Yet Shimen has fallen, and garrison service at the three camps has been discontinued, so that China instead finds itself subject to outside peoples. The prescribed levies on military agricultural colonies are a major provision for feeding the troops. Yet sales are sought at high prices, and military personnel are treated as civilians [?], so that outside peoples establish many estates within China. The stores of the military guards are insufficient for each year's needs, while much of what the responsible civil authorities have accumulated rots and becomes unfit to eat. Is this not what is meant by a state having ‘five chills’ [?]? Officials holding ranked posts are largely drawn from men who have been dismissed and rejected, while those advanced for their ability encounter obstruction and cannot put their abilities into practice. Is this not what is meant by the gentleman having ‘five shames’? Among those who entered Yunnan in antiquity, there were some who established commanderies…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
治於白崖不屯兵而諸夷竟服有勒石
碑於濫川旣旋師而諸夷復叛有征討
封離而請兵務求其姦黨有檢校南寧
而置郡乃任其豪帥其得失可盡言歟
管子曰化夷之道九變而後安之不知
今日亦可循行否也願明告我將以聞
于
當宁
punctuated: 治於白崖，不屯兵而諸夷竟服；有勒石碑於濫川，旣旋師而諸夷復叛；有征討封離，而請兵務求其姦黨；有檢校南寧，而置郡乃任其豪帥。其得失可盡言歟？管子曰：「化夷之道，九變而後安之。」不知今日亦可循行否也？願明告我，將以聞于當宁。
translation_en: …with the administrative seat at Baiya, where the various non-Chinese peoples ultimately submitted without troops being stationed there; others erected a stone inscription at Lanchuan, yet those peoples rebelled again once the army withdrew. Some campaigned against Fengli [?] and requested troops, intent on seeking out its treacherous faction; others supervised Nanning and established commanderies, appointing its powerful local chieftains to govern them. Can you fully explain the successes and failures of these measures? The Guanzi states: “The way to transform the non-Chinese peoples requires nine changes before bringing them peace.” I wonder whether this approach can also be followed today. Please explain clearly to me, so that I may report it to His Majesty.
