title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰君子道者三我無能焉仁者不憂知
者不惑勇者不懼子貢曰夫子自道也
陳扆
考試官教諭張批聖人子貢之意體認俱到
辭亦渾厚
考試官教授黄批識得聖賢氣象不徒工於
文者
===
聖人以君子之道而不居賢者以為辭之謙也
夫君子之道聖人之所優為也而猶不自居焉
賢者以為辭之謙真知足以知聖人者哉昔夫
子意謂學貴於大成理難於速契吾固不敢以
自居而亦安敢以自誣耶誠以君子以德則盛
矣以業則大矣而語其為道則有三焉顧我學
之不講也德之不脩也而反之于身皆無能焉
何則自其純於理而有仁之名仁者渾然無欲
斯不憂矣而我未免於憂也自其明於理而有
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「君子道者三，我無能焉：仁者不憂，知者不惑，勇者不懼。」子貢曰：「夫子自道也。」

陳扆

考試官教諭張批：聖人、子貢之意，體認俱到，辭亦渾厚。

考試官教授黄批：識得聖賢氣象，不徒工於文者。

聖人以君子之道而不居，賢者以為辭之謙也。夫君子之道，聖人之所優為也，而猶不自居焉。賢者以為辭之謙，真知足以知聖人者哉！昔夫子意謂：學貴於大成，理難於速契。吾固不敢以自居，而亦安敢以自誣耶？誠以君子以德則盛矣，以業則大矣，而語其為道，則有三焉。顧我學之不講也，德之不脩也，而反之于身，皆無能焉。何則？自其純於理而有仁之名，仁者渾然無欲，斯不憂矣，而我未免於憂也；自其明於理而有
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “There are three aspects to the way of the gentleman, of which I am capable of none: the benevolent are free from anxiety, the wise are free from confusion, and the courageous are free from fear.” Zigong said: “The Master is describing himself.”

Chen Yi 陳扆

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The intentions of both the sage and Zigong are fully grasped; the language, too, is substantial and rounded.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “He understands the bearing of sages and worthies; his skill is not merely literary.”

The sage declined to claim for himself the way of the gentleman; the worthy understood his words as an expression of modesty. Now, the way of the gentleman is something the sage can practice with ease, yet he still did not claim it for himself. The worthy understood this as modest speech: truly, his understanding sufficed to understand the sage!

Formerly, the Master’s meaning was this: In learning, what matters is comprehensive attainment; understanding principle cannot readily be achieved in haste. Though I certainly dare not claim such attainment for myself, how could I dare to misrepresent myself either? Indeed, the gentleman is abundant in virtue and great in accomplishment; as for his way, it has three aspects. Yet I consider that my learning has not been thoroughly pursued and my virtue has not been cultivated; when I examine myself, I find myself capable of none of them. Why is this? Through being wholly in accord with principle, one earns the name of benevolent. The benevolent person is entirely free from selfish desires and therefore free from anxiety; yet I am not free from anxiety. Through being clear in one’s understanding of principle, one earns…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
知之名知者洞然無蔽斯不惑矣而我未免於
惑也自其强此理而又有勇之名勇者毅然無
屈斯不懼矣而我未免於懼也是其有愧於君
子者多矣時子貢在侍乃作而言曰至道固不
易窺而盛德終於難掩夫子道集羣聖罔弗備
矣聖由天縱蔑以加矣故有稱夫子之仁者必
將曰仁之至也有稱夫子之知者必將曰知之
盡也有稱夫子之勇者又必將曰不賴勇而裕
如也今乃曰我無能焉是蓋聖不自聖之心形
===
而為謙已之至自不覺措之詞而遂有是過甚
焉耳矣而在夫子也則固有不得而辭也哉抑
立必俱立之心發而為誨人之切自不吝惜之
言而姑為是退托焉耳矣而在夫賜也亦遽肯
信以為然也哉吁夫子遜之子貢知之授受之
間兩無負矣抑夫子斯言多為子貢發蓋孔門
顏子而下穎悟莫若子貢但務方人容有矜已
驚遠而自治或疎故借之已以警之不然他日
與回孰愈之問莫我知也之歎何皆獨於子貢
punctuated: 知之名，知者洞然無蔽，斯不惑矣，而我未免於惑也。自其强此理而又有勇之名，勇者毅然無屈，斯不懼矣，而我未免於懼也。是其有愧於君子者多矣。時子貢在侍，乃作而言曰：「至道固不易窺，而盛德終於難掩。夫子道集羣聖，罔弗備矣；聖由天縱，蔑以加矣。故有稱夫子之仁者，必將曰仁之至也；有稱夫子之知者，必將曰知之盡也；有稱夫子之勇者，又必將曰不賴勇而裕如也。今乃曰我無能焉，是蓋聖不自聖之心，形而為謙已之至，自不覺措之詞，而遂有是過甚焉耳矣。而在夫子也，則固有不得而辭也哉！抑立必俱立之心，發而為誨人之切，自不吝惜之言，而姑為是退托焉耳矣。而在夫賜也，亦遽肯信以為然也哉！」吁！夫子遜之，子貢知之，授受之間，兩無負矣。抑夫子斯言，多為子貢發。蓋孔門顏子而下，穎悟莫若子貢，但務方人，容有矜已驚遠，而自治或疎，故借之已以警之。不然，他日與回孰愈之問、莫我知也之歎，何皆獨於子貢
translation_en:
…the name of wisdom. The wise are thoroughly clear-sighted and unobscured, and thus free from perplexity; yet I have not escaped perplexity. From steadfastness in this principle comes, further, the name of courage. The courageous are resolute and unyielding, and thus free from fear; yet I have not escaped fear. In many respects, then, I fall short of the gentleman.”
At that time Zigong was attending him. He rose and said: “The utmost Way is indeed difficult to fathom, yet abundant virtue is ultimately difficult to conceal. Master, your Way brings together that of all the sages, lacking nothing. Your sagehood is Heaven’s gift, and nothing can surpass it. Thus anyone praising your benevolence must call it benevolence at its highest; anyone praising your wisdom must call it wisdom in its fullest measure; and anyone praising your courage must say that, without relying on courage, you possess ease in abundance. Yet now you say, ‘I am capable of none of these.’ Surely this is the heart of a sage who does not regard himself as a sage, manifested in the utmost self-effacement: unwittingly putting it into words, you have merely carried your disclaimer this far. But can you, Master, truly disclaim these qualities? Or perhaps your wish that, in establishing yourself, you should establish others as well has issued in an earnest desire to instruct. Sparing no words, you have simply adopted this self-deprecating stance for the occasion. But would I, Ci, so readily accept it as true?”
Ah! The Master spoke modestly, and Zigong understood him. Between teacher and recipient, neither failed the other. Indeed, these words of the Master were largely uttered for Zigong’s sake. Among Confucius’s disciples, below Master Yan, none equaled Zigong in quickness of understanding. Yet he occupied himself with judging others; there may have been self-conceit and alarm at what lay far beyond him [?], while his work on himself was perhaps neglected. The Master therefore used himself as an example to admonish him. Otherwise, why were his question on another occasion, “Who is the better, you or Hui?” and his lament, “No one understands me,” both addressed specifically to Zigong…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
焉發之夷考其終至聞性與天道則於所謂仁
知勇三者思之過半矣此固見夫子之曲成而
亦以見子貢之速肖云
尊賢則不惑
朱文質
同考試官教諭尹批聖人動君微旨子能發之
考試官教諭張批精確
考試官教授黃批講不惑最精切
人君能重乎君子斯可以進於明矣夫君子之
===
有關於君德也大矣苟非尊重而得以親之其
何從以進吾之明也哉昔夫子對哀公以九經
尊賢之效意謂人君一心惟在所養君子養之
以善則知矣但人君處崇高之極而視夫韋布
之微固已難親而易疎而彼君子負道德之高
而審於去就之義則又難進而易退非有以尊
之孰得而致之乃若慕古王公之風內則盡敬
于凡所以樂善而忘勢者無所不用其極鑒今
諸侯之失外則盡禮于凡所以折節以下士者
punctuated:
焉發之？夷考其終，至聞性與天道，則於所謂仁知勇三者，思之過半矣。此固見夫子之曲成，而亦以見子貢之速肖云。

尊賢則不惑
朱文質
同考試官教諭尹批：「聖人動君微旨，子能發之。」
考試官教諭張批：「精確。」
考試官教授黃批：「講不惑最精切。」

人君能重乎君子，斯可以進於明矣。夫君子之有關於君德也大矣，苟非尊重而得以親之，其何從以進吾之明也哉？昔夫子對哀公以九經，尊賢之效，意謂人君一心，惟在所養。君子養之以善，則知矣。但人君處崇高之極，而視夫韋布之微，固已難親而易疎；而彼君子負道德之高，而審於去就之義，則又難進而易退。非有以尊之，孰得而致之？乃若慕古王公之風，內則盡敬，于凡所以樂善而忘勢者，無所不用其極；鑒今諸侯之失，外則盡禮，于凡所以折節以下士者，
translation_en:
…did he utter them? If we calmly examine how things ultimately developed, when Zigong came to hear about human nature and the Way of Heaven, he had already understood the greater part of what are called benevolence, wisdom, and courage. This certainly shows how the Master brought him to fulfillment through painstaking guidance; it also shows how swiftly Zigong came to resemble him.

“By Honoring the Worthy, One Is Free from Perplexity”
Zhu Wenzhi
Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor, comments: “You have brought out the subtle intent with which the sage sought to move the ruler.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Precise.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “The explanation of ‘free from perplexity’ is exceptionally incisive and apt.”

If a ruler can esteem gentlemen of virtue, he can advance toward clear understanding. Such gentlemen have a profound bearing on the ruler’s virtue. Unless he honors them and thereby gains their close association, how can he advance his own understanding? Formerly, when the Master answered Duke Ai by setting forth the nine guiding principles, his account of the effects of honoring the worthy meant that everything depends on how the ruler’s mind is nurtured. When gentlemen nurture it with goodness, it becomes wise.

Yet the ruler occupies the very pinnacle of exalted rank and looks upon the lowly station of those clad in plain cloth: it is already difficult for him to draw close to them and easy to keep them at a distance. Those gentlemen, meanwhile, possess lofty moral cultivation and carefully judge whether accepting office or withdrawing accords with righteousness; thus they are difficult to bring forward and quick to retire. Without some means of honoring them, who could succeed in attracting them?

If, then, he admires the ways of the kings and dukes of antiquity, inwardly he will show the utmost reverence, doing everything possible to delight in goodness and forget his own power and position. Taking warning from the failings of the feudal lords of the present day, outwardly he will fulfill every requirement of ritual courtesy, in all the ways by which he humbles himself to defer to men of learning …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
無所愛於其情悅矣而能養也養矣而能舉也
隆之以親師取友之恭而讒諂不得以間之結
之以言聽計從之契而貨色不得以沮之夫然
懿德之好自有以動其樂用之心而謙光之施
又有以爲受言之地將見納約之資動有所悟
沃心之助日罔自知義理得於薰陶之益而察
中庸于兩端遠而聖賢大學之道亦將躍然於
心目之間矣聞見充於講論之功而析萬殊於
一貫上而帝王心法之傳亦將了然於精神之
===
會矣其不惑者有如此以之脩身而身益脩以
之用人而人益辨尚何文武之政有不舉哉抑
此道惟古能盡之明哉良哉卓乎不可尚已魯
有孔子而不知所以尊之攝相三月定公似矣
齊人歸女樂季桓子受之惡在其爲貴德而奚
異乎其惑也然東周之望遽能忘情耶故因哀
公問政卽以九經啓之列尊賢於脩身之次而
及其效焉使知身爲治本賴賢以脩而知人非
自明不可意獨至矣惜乎哀之猶夫定也
punctuated: 無所愛於其情。悅矣而能養也，養矣而能舉也。隆之以親師取友之恭，而讒諂不得以間之；結之以言聽計從之契，而貨色不得以沮之。夫然，懿德之好自有以動其樂用之心，而謙光之施又有以爲受言之地。將見納約之資，動有所悟；沃心之助，日罔自知。義理得於薰陶之益，而察中庸于兩端，遠而聖賢大學之道，亦將躍然於心目之間矣；聞見充於講論之功，而析萬殊於一貫，上而帝王心法之傳，亦將了然於精神之會矣。其不惑者有如此，以之脩身而身益脩，以之用人而人益辨，尚何文武之政有不舉哉？抑此道惟古能盡之。明哉！良哉！卓乎不可尚已！魯有孔子，而不知所以尊之。攝相三月，定公似矣；齊人歸女樂，季桓子受之，惡在其爲貴德，而奚異乎其惑也？然東周之望，遽能忘情耶？故因哀公問政，卽以九經啓之，列尊賢於脩身之次，而及其效焉，使知身爲治本，賴賢以脩，而知人非自明不可。意獨至矣！惜乎哀之猶夫定也！
translation_en:
…withholding nothing of his sincere feelings. Taking delight in worthy men, he can nurture them; nurturing them, he can raise them to office. He honors them with the reverence shown in drawing close to teachers and choosing friends, so that slanderers and flatterers cannot come between them. He binds them to himself through a bond of heeding their words and following their counsel, so that wealth and sensual pleasures cannot thwart them. Thus his love of fine virtue naturally stirs their willingness to serve, while his manifest humility provides a basis for receiving their advice. It will then be seen that counsel conveyed simply and directly brings insight at every turn, and that the aid of advice nourishing his mind works daily without his awareness. Through the benefits of sustained moral influence, he grasps righteousness and principle and discerns the constant mean between the two extremes. Extending his understanding into the distant past, even the sages’ and worthies’ Way of Great Learning will come vividly before his mind’s eye. Through discussion and exposition, his knowledge grows, and he distinguishes the myriad particulars within the single unifying principle. Reaching upward, even the transmission of the emperors’ and kings’ teachings of the mind will become clear within his spiritual understanding.

Such is his freedom from perplexity. Applying this to self-cultivation, he becomes ever more cultivated; applying it to employing others, he distinguishes their qualities ever more clearly. What aspect of the government of Kings Wen and Wu could then remain unimplemented? Yet only in antiquity was this Way fully realized. How discerning! How worthy! So outstanding that none could surpass it!

Lu had Confucius, yet did not know how to honor him. When Confucius served as acting chief minister for three months, Duke Ding seemed to approach this ideal. But when the men of Qi sent female entertainers and Ji Huanzi accepted them, where was their esteem for virtue? How did this differ from remaining perplexed? Yet could Confucius readily relinquish his cherished hope of establishing a Zhou in the east? Thus, when Duke Ai asked about government, he instructed him through the nine guiding principles, placing honoring the worthy immediately after self-cultivation and explaining its effects. He sought to make the duke understand that his own person was the foundation of government and that its cultivation depended upon worthy men, while discerning others required that he himself first attain clarity. His intention was supremely earnest! Alas that Duke Ai was just like Duke Ding!

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
友也者友其德也不可以有挾也
楊懷哲
考試官敎諭張批發出孟子論友語意還淳
黜浮之文可以式矣
考試官敎授黄批辭理明當是可與論友者
大賢論友資於人者重而有於已者輕也夫所
資於友者重其德也使有所挾焉則豈取友之
道哉孟子告萬章之意如此今夫朋友乃生人
之大倫爲天下之達道故獨學者來寡聞之譏
===
而麗澤者取相資之益雖論諸學而定交實同
其氣以爲求也是友之云者將拍肩執袂以爲
容悅而已邪抑朋攀類引以相結納而已邪是
故直也諒也多聞也仁足以成人之美而義足
以責人之善彼之所有者德也吾惟因言以觀
其行所足畏也從而友之朝夕相磨于以藉其
薰陶之力因迹以考其心所可益也從而友之
肝膽相示于以仰其切磋之功德業之勸過失
之規胥焉賴之蓋將相觀以爲善而淬礪焉以
punctuated:
友也者，友其德也，不可以有挾也。
楊懷哲
考試官敎諭張批：發出孟子論友語意，還淳黜浮之文，可以式矣。
考試官敎授黄批：辭理明當，是可與論友者。
大賢論友，資於人者重，而有於已者輕也。夫所資於友者，重其德也；使有所挾焉，則豈取友之道哉？孟子告萬章之意如此。今夫朋友，乃生人之大倫，爲天下之達道，故獨學者來寡聞之譏，而麗澤者取相資之益。雖論諸學，而定交實同其氣以爲求也。是友之云者，將拍肩執袂以爲容悅而已邪？抑朋攀類引以相結納而已邪？是故直也，諒也，多聞也，仁足以成人之美，而義足以責人之善。彼之所有者，德也。吾惟因言以觀其行，所足畏也，從而友之，朝夕相磨，于以藉其薰陶之力；因迹以考其心，所可益也，從而友之，肝膽相示，于以仰其切磋之功。德業之勸，過失之規，胥焉賴之，蓋將相觀以爲善，而淬礪焉以
translation_en:
“Friendship means befriending a person's virtue; one must not presume upon any advantage.”

Yang Huaizhe

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “This brings out the meaning of Mencius's words on friendship. An essay that restores simplicity and rejects superficiality: it may serve as a model.”

Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “The language and reasoning are clear and apt. Here is someone with whom one may discuss friendship.”

When the great worthy discusses friendship, he gives weight to what one draws from others and little weight to what one possesses oneself. What one seeks in friends is their virtue, which one esteems. If one presumes upon some advantage, how could this be the proper way to choose friends? Such is the meaning of Mencius's words to Wan Zhang. Now friendship is one of the great human relationships, a universally followed Way throughout the world. Thus those who study alone incur the criticism of being poorly informed, whereas those who, like adjoining lakes, nourish one another gain the benefit of mutual assistance. Although this is said of learning, in forming friendships too, people indeed seek those of kindred disposition. Does friendship, then, mean merely clapping someone on the shoulder and grasping his sleeve to ingratiate oneself? Or merely cultivating associates and drawing in one's own kind to build connections?

Thus friends should be upright, trustworthy, and widely learned. Their benevolence should suffice to bring others' good qualities to fulfillment, and their righteousness to demand goodness of others. What they possess is virtue. Through a person's words I observe his conduct; finding in him something worthy of reverence, I befriend him. We refine one another morning and evening, and thereby I draw upon his formative influence. Through his deeds I examine his heart; finding something from which I can benefit, I befriend him. We lay our hearts bare to one another, and thereby I rely upon the achievement of mutual refinement. For encouragement in virtue and worthy undertakings, and admonition concerning faults and errors, I depend upon such friends in all these things. The purpose is to observe one another so as to become good, and to temper and sharpen ourselves in order to…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
自新也信誓之期平生之託乆焉要之蓋將因
人以成已而道義焉以相終也友非所以友其
德乎若夫長也貴也兄弟也勢足以傾於一時
而力足以兼乎天下我之所有者此也以此而
恃諸已歟適足以爲長傲遂非之資耳於性分
乎何加以此而施諸人歟徒足以爲席寵怙侈
之地耳於輕重乎何有德色者距人千里之外
不惟失乎人而因以失乎已也驕氣者自矜一
已之長非惟喪乎名而且喪乎業也友而可以
===
有挾乎是知德之與勢輕重殊科在君子權之
而已於此而不失其倫斯之爲能友也夫嘗聞
之古之敎者七年論學取友謂之小成自天子
以至於庶人一也追而考之堯舜以下若晉平
若費惠若獻子猶有聞者自此而友道日廢在
上者以莫予違爲賢在下者以巧附爲能無復
知所謂貴貴尊賢之義輔仁之風嗚呼微矣世
道之不古彝倫之攸斁又何怪焉故詩存伐木
谷風之刺易示致一斯孚之占有以也夫
punctuated:
自新也。信誓之期，平生之託，乆焉要之，蓋將因人以成已，而道義焉以相終也。友非所以友其德乎？若夫長也，貴也，兄弟也，勢足以傾於一時，而力足以兼乎天下，我之所有者此也。以此而恃諸已歟？適足以爲長傲遂非之資耳，於性分乎何加？以此而施諸人歟？徒足以爲席寵怙侈之地耳，於輕重乎何有？德色者，距人千里之外，不惟失乎人，而因以失乎已也。驕氣者，自矜一已之長，非惟喪乎名，而且喪乎業也。友而可以有挾乎？是知德之與勢，輕重殊科，在君子權之而已。於此而不失其倫，斯之爲能友也。
夫嘗聞之，古之敎者，七年論學取友，謂之小成，自天子以至於庶人一也。追而考之，堯舜以下，若晉平，若費惠，若獻子，猶有聞者。自此而友道日廢，在上者以莫予違爲賢，在下者以巧附爲能，無復知所謂貴貴尊賢之義、輔仁之風。嗚呼，微矣！世道之不古，彝倫之攸斁，又何怪焉？故《詩》存《伐木》《谷風》之刺，《易》示「致一斯孚」之占，有以也夫！
translation_en:
…to renew oneself. Through pledges sincerely sworn and the entrusting of one’s entire life, friends bind themselves to one another for the long term: their purpose is to perfect themselves through others and to remain united in the Way and righteousness to the end. Is not friendship a matter of befriending another’s virtue? As for seniority, high rank, and brothers—one’s influence may overawe one’s contemporaries, and one’s power may encompass all under Heaven: these are the things one possesses. Should one rely on them oneself? They merely furnish the means to foster arrogance and persist in wrongdoing; what do they add to one’s inherent moral nature? Should one bring them to bear upon others? They merely provide a basis for presuming upon favor and indulging in extravagance; what bearing do they have on one’s true worth? An air of moral superiority keeps others a thousand li away: one not only loses others but thereby loses oneself. An arrogant disposition boasts of one’s own strengths: one not only ruins one’s reputation but also ruins one’s achievements. Can one enter friendship presuming upon such advantages? Thus we know that virtue and power differ in their relative worth; it rests with the gentleman to weigh them. To preserve the proper relationships in this matter is what it means to be capable of friendship.
Now, I have heard that in ancient education, after seven years students discussed their learning and chose their friends; this was called the ‘lesser attainment.’ From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, the principle was the same. Looking back over the past, from Yao and Shun onward, we still hear of such men as Duke Ping of Jin, Duke Hui of Fei, and Xianzi. Thereafter, the way of friendship fell increasingly into neglect. Those above regarded ‘Let no one oppose me’ as the mark of worthiness; those below regarded skill in ingratiating themselves as ability. No longer did they understand the meaning of honoring the highly ranked and respecting the worthy, or the practice of helping one another cultivate benevolence. Alas, how feeble that practice has become! Why, then, should we wonder that the ways of the world fall short of antiquity and that the constant human relationships have deteriorated? Thus the Book of Odes preserves the admonitions of ‘Felling Trees’ and ‘Valley Wind,’ and the Book of Changes presents the prognostication, ‘Achieve unity, and then there will be trust.’ There is indeed a reason for this!

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
易
豚魚吉信及豚魚也利涉大川乘木舟虛
也中孚以利貞乃應乎天也
朱文質
同考試官教諭尹批孚貞之理辭足以發
考試官教諭張批確而正
考試官教授黄批雅健
彖傳釋中孚之辭孚貞之義舉之矣蓋孚且貞
天之道也則其感物而濟險也庸舍此而他求
===
乎夫子彖傳若曰中孚之卦有曰豚魚吉者厥
義維何蓋豚魚者罔覺者也感而通者信之浹
也立人之道信而已矣信則精誠神應妙必動
之機而物莫能外體信達順本無心之感而物
罔弗從是信足以及乎豚魚矣豚魚且然維人
維靈有弗感矣乎中孚之吉有如此者何言乎
利涉大川也蓋卦焉全體外實中虛擬象乎舟
虛而乘巽之木以行乎兌澤唯虛也實德中涵
故能涉天下之險而無虞唯巽也誠順積中故
punctuated:
易

豚魚吉，信及豚魚也。利涉大川，乘木舟虛也。中孚以利貞，乃應乎天也。

朱文質

同考試官教諭尹批：孚貞之理，辭足以發。
考試官教諭張批：確而正。
考試官教授黄批：雅健。

彖傳釋中孚之辭，孚貞之義舉之矣。蓋孚且貞，天之道也。則其感物而濟險也，庸舍此而他求乎？夫子彖傳若曰：中孚之卦有曰「豚魚吉」者，厥義維何？蓋豚魚者，罔覺者也；感而通者，信之浹也。立人之道，信而已矣。信則精誠神應，妙必動之機，而物莫能外；體信達順，本無心之感，而物罔弗從。是信足以及乎豚魚矣。豚魚且然，維人維靈，有弗感矣乎？中孚之吉，有如此者。何言乎「利涉大川」也？蓋卦焉全體，外實中虛，擬象乎舟虛，而乘巽之木，以行乎兌澤。唯虛也，實德中涵，故能涉天下之險而無虞；唯巽也，誠順積中，故
translation_en:
Book of Changes

“Good fortune with pigs and fish”: trustworthiness reaches even pigs and fish. “It is beneficial to cross the great river”: one rides in a wooden boat whose interior is empty. In Inner Sincerity, “it is beneficial to be steadfast and correct”: thus one accords with Heaven.

Zhu Wenzhi

Comment by Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor: “The language adequately expounds the principles of sincerity and steadfast correctness.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Sound and correct.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “Elegant and vigorous.”

In explaining the wording of Inner Sincerity, the Commentary on the Judgments brings out the meaning of sincerity and steadfast correctness. For to be sincere and steadfastly correct is the Way of Heaven. In moving other beings and overcoming dangers, then, how could one abandon this and seek elsewhere? The Master's Commentary on the Judgments seems to say: The hexagram Inner Sincerity contains the words “good fortune with pigs and fish.” What do they mean? Pigs and fish are creatures without understanding; that they are moved and respond is because trustworthiness permeates them. The Way by which human beings establish themselves is simply trustworthiness. With trustworthiness, perfect sincerity elicits a spiritual response, wondrously working through the impulse that must move others, so that nothing can remain outside its influence. Embodying trustworthiness and attaining harmony, one acts through an influence that is fundamentally without deliberate intent, and nothing fails to follow. Thus trustworthiness is sufficient to reach even pigs and fish. If even pigs and fish respond in this way, could human beings, endowed with spiritual intelligence, fail to be moved? Such is the good fortune of Inner Sincerity.

Why does it say, “It is beneficial to cross the great river”? The hexagram as a whole is solid on the outside and empty within, resembling a boat with an empty interior; riding upon the wood of Xun, it travels over the waters of Dui. Precisely because it is empty, substantial virtue is contained within, and thus it can traverse the dangers of the world without anxiety. Precisely because it is yielding, sincerity and compliance accumulate within, and thus …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
能拯天下之難而有濟是孚足以濟乎大川矣
大川且然履道坦坦有弗順矣乎中孚之利有
如此者夫至信可以感物矣涉險矣而尤利於
貞者何耶蓋維天之命於穆不已者一孚貞焉
耳今焉有孚顒若而貞固以守乎天理我與天
一而已矣至誠無息而中正以觀乎天下天卽
我而已矣先天焉而天莫之違也後天焉而奉
厥天時也豈不有以應乎天哉天且弗違而況
於人乎況於豚魚乎況於大川乎然則中孚而
===
本於正也不亦宜哉彖傳之旨深矣大抵天下
之道二誠與偽正與邪而已矣故信非正則諒
諒者道之蔽也正非誠則忒忒者道之慝也其
何以感物神化而冒天下之道哉故文王於中
孚拳拳以孚貞之義開示萬世扶焉抑焉宰造
化之力著心易之本焉者也於戲非夫子之聖
之至其孰能與於此
極天下之賾者存乎卦鼓天下之動者存
乎辭化而裁之存乎變推而行之存乎
punctuated:
能拯天下之難而有濟，是孚足以濟乎大川矣。大川且然，履道坦坦，有弗順矣乎？中孚之利有如此者。夫至信可以感物矣，涉險矣，而尤利於貞者，何耶？蓋維天之命，於穆不已者，一孚貞焉耳。今焉有孚顒若，而貞固以守乎天理，我與天一而已矣；至誠無息，而中正以觀乎天下，天卽我而已矣。先天焉，而天莫之違也；後天焉，而奉厥天時也。豈不有以應乎天哉？天且弗違，而況於人乎？況於豚魚乎？況於大川乎？然則中孚而本於正也，不亦宜哉？彖傳之旨深矣！大抵天下之道二：誠與偽，正與邪而已矣。故信非正則諒，諒者道之蔽也；正非誠則忒，忒者道之慝也。其何以感物神化而冒天下之道哉？故文王於中孚，拳拳以孚貞之義開示萬世，扶焉抑焉，宰造化之力，著心易之本焉者也。於戲！非夫子之聖之至，其孰能與於此？

極天下之賾者存乎卦，鼓天下之動者存乎辭，化而裁之存乎變，推而行之存乎
translation_en:
…one can rescue all under Heaven from calamity and bring relief. Thus trustworthiness suffices to cross a great river. If this holds even for a great river, could anything fail to go smoothly when one treads a broad and level path? Such are the benefits of Inner Truth (Zhongfu). Utmost trustworthiness can move other beings and carry one through danger; why, then, is it especially beneficial to remain steadfast in correctness? The mandate of Heaven, profound and unceasing, is nothing more than this unity of trustworthiness and correctness. When one possesses trustworthiness, maintains reverence, and firmly preserves heavenly principle, oneself and Heaven are simply one. When perfect sincerity never ceases and one surveys all under Heaven with centrality and correctness, Heaven is simply oneself. If one acts before Heaven, Heaven does not oppose one; if one acts after Heaven, one follows Heaven’s seasons. Does this not provide the means to accord with Heaven? If even Heaven does not oppose one, how much less would human beings, pigs and fish, or a great river? Is it not fitting, then, that Inner Truth should be rooted in correctness? Profound indeed is the purport of the Commentary on the Judgments!

Broadly speaking, the ways of the world fall into two alternatives: sincerity and falsity, correctness and deviation. Thus trustworthiness without correctness becomes petty fidelity, which obscures the Way; correctness without sincerity becomes aberration, which corrupts the Way. How could these move other beings, transform them wondrously, and encompass the Way of all under Heaven? Thus, in Inner Truth, King Wen earnestly disclosed the meaning of trustworthiness and steadfast correctness to all generations. Upholding the one and restraining the other, he exercised the power to govern creation and transformation and made manifest the foundation of the Changes within the heart. Ah! Without the supreme sageliness of the Master, who could attain such understanding?

What plumbs the deepest intricacies of all under Heaven resides in the hexagrams; what stirs all movement under Heaven resides in the statements. Transforming and fittingly shaping things resides in change; extending them and putting them into practice resides in…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
通神而明之存乎其人默而成之不言
而信存乎德行
田時中
同考試官教諭尹批純正細密深於易者
考試官教諭張批切當
考試官教授黄批析理明措詞整
大傳論易備天下之用必言用之所以妙於天
下焉蓋卦爻變通天下之能事畢矣待其人而
後行也不有在於德行也哉且天下之賾易理
===
之散見也究極於雜陳之中而廣大悉備之無
遺則存乎卦卦立而賾無不探矣天下之動易
理之發用也鼓動於利用之際而殊塗百慮之
皆順則存乎辭辭告而動無不效矣陰陽動靜
有自然之化也而裁之存乎變蓋進退極而陰
陽易位動靜分而剛柔趨時易窮則變化裁不
在兹乎陰陽變易有可行之道也而推之存乎
通蓋變以趨時而當動之理寓易以從道而攸
往之幾形易變則通推行不在是乎然是變通
punctuated:
通，神而明之存乎其人，默而成之，不言而信，存乎德行。
田時中。
同考試官教諭尹批：純正細密，深於易者。
考試官教諭張批：切當。
考試官教授黄批：析理明，措詞整。
大傳論易備天下之用，必言用之所以妙於天下焉。蓋卦爻變通，天下之能事畢矣，待其人而後行也，不有在於德行也哉？且天下之賾，易理之散見也。究極於雜陳之中，而廣大悉備之無遺，則存乎卦；卦立而賾無不探矣。天下之動，易理之發用也。鼓動於利用之際，而殊塗百慮之皆順，則存乎辭；辭告而動無不效矣。陰陽動靜，有自然之化也，而裁之存乎變。蓋進退極而陰陽易位，動靜分而剛柔趨時，易窮則變，化裁不在兹乎？陰陽變易，有可行之道也，而推之存乎通。蓋變以趨時，而當動之理寓；易以從道，而攸往之幾形。易變則通，推行不在是乎？然是變通
translation_en:
…free passage. Making it spiritually efficacious and illuminating it depends on the right person; silently bringing it to completion and securing trust without words depend on virtuous conduct.

Tian Shizhong.

Associate Examiner Yin, Instructor, comments: “Pure and correct, meticulous and closely reasoned: the work of someone deeply versed in the Changes.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Apt and fitting.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “Clear in its analysis of principles and orderly in its wording.”

When the Great Commentary discusses how the Changes provides for every use under Heaven, it must explain what makes its application wondrous throughout the world. For the hexagrams and lines, transformation and free passage, encompass all that can be accomplished under Heaven. Yet they await the right person before they can be put into practice. Does this not depend on virtuous conduct?

Now, the intricacies of all under Heaven are the scattered manifestations of the principles of the Changes. To fathom them amid their manifold array and encompass their vast extent completely, leaving nothing out, depends on the hexagrams. Once the hexagrams are established, no intricacy remains unexplored. The movements of all under Heaven are the principles of the Changes coming into operation. To set them in motion at the point of beneficial application, bringing diverse paths and a hundred deliberations alike into accord, depends on the statements. Once the statements give their guidance, no movement fails to achieve its effect.

Yin and yang, movement and stillness, undergo spontaneous transformation; giving this its proper measure depends on change. For when advance and retreat reach their limits, yin and yang exchange positions; as movement and stillness differentiate, the firm and yielding respond to the time. When the Changes reaches an impasse, it changes: does not transforming and giving proper measure lie here?

Within the changes of yin and yang there is a way that can be put into practice; carrying it forward depends on free passage. For through transformation one responds to the time, and therein resides the principle governing appropriate action; through change one follows the Way, and the incipient signs of where to proceed take form. When the Changes changes, free passage follows: does not carrying forward and putting into practice lie here? Yet these transformations and free passage…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
也精義入神而周知乎變化之道知來藏往而
大明其終始之幾是必齋戒是存而人之至者
焉能與於此苟非其人道不虛行矣然其神明
也無瀆再三而至理渾成於已無騰口說而微
幾妙契於心是必窮神知化而德之盛者焉能
與於此苟不至德至道不疑矣是則大用備於
易而妙用係於人所以聖人用易而必神明其
德也夫大抵有言畫之易也卦爻也無言心之
易也德行也聖人洗心退藏於密心易具矣百
===
姓日用而不知易安得而不作也乎故有言之
易甚非聖人之得已者而乃以德行望之人無
非欲同歸於無言之域也歟不此之務而徒卦
爻焉是卜抑亦不占而已
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝
陳扆
考試官教諭張 批命意脩辭宛然虞廷氣象
考試官教授黄 批說出大禹祗承意純雅可錄
punctuated:
也，精義入神而周知乎變化之道，知來藏往而大明其終始之幾，是必齋戒是存，而人之至者焉能與於此。苟非其人，道不虛行矣。然其神明也，無瀆再三而至理渾成於已，無騰口說而微幾妙契於心，是必窮神知化，而德之盛者焉能與於此。苟不至德，至道不疑矣。是則大用備於易，而妙用係於人，所以聖人用易而必神明其德也夫！大抵有言，畫之易也，卦爻也；無言，心之易也，德行也。聖人洗心，退藏於密，心易具矣。百姓日用而不知，易安得而不作也乎？故有言之易，甚非聖人之得已者，而乃以德行望之人，無非欲同歸於無言之域也歟！不此之務而徒卦爻焉，是卜抑亦不占而已。
書
文命敷于四海，祗承于帝。
陳扆
考試官教諭張批：命意脩辭，宛然虞廷氣象。
考試官教授黄批：說出大禹祗承意，純雅可錄。
translation_en:
…As for this transformation and continuity: by refining meaning and penetrating the numinous, one comprehensively understands the way of change; by knowing what is to come and storing up what has passed, one clearly apprehends the subtle incipiencies of endings and beginnings. This requires maintaining purification and reverent restraint; only a person of the highest attainment can participate in it. Without the right person, the Way does not operate of itself. As for its numinous illumination: without profaning it by repeated inquiries, ultimate principle becomes fully integrated within oneself; without airing verbal explanations, its subtle workings are wondrously apprehended in the heart. This requires fathoming the numinous and understanding transformation; only one whose virtue flourishes can participate in it. Without consummate virtue, the ultimate Way is not doubted [?]. Thus the Changes contains the full scope of its great operations, but their wondrous application depends upon the person. That is why the sage, in employing the Changes, must bring numinous illumination to his virtue!

Broadly speaking, the Changes expressed in words is the Changes of drawn figures—the hexagrams and their lines. The wordless Changes is the Changes of the heart—virtue and conduct. The sage cleanses his heart and withdraws into hidden secrecy; the Changes of the heart is complete within him. Yet ordinary people use it daily without knowing it: how, then, could the Changes have remained unwritten? Thus the verbal Changes was something the sage could scarcely avoid producing. His expectation that people cultivate virtue and conduct was surely intended only to bring them all back together into the realm beyond words! If one neglects this task and attends merely to hexagrams and lines, this is divination—or merely a failure to divine [?].

Book of Documents

“His civilizing influence spread throughout the Four Seas, and he reverently served the Emperor.”

Chen Yi 陳扆

Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The conception and phrasing vividly evoke the atmosphere of the court of Yu [Shun].”

Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “It brings out the meaning of Great Yu’s reverent service. Pure and elegant, it merits inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
已成天下之大化猶獻天下之大猷史臣賛聖
人然也甚矣聖人之不自滿假也大化旣成於
天下而猶獻其猷於帝焉圖治之心何至哉史
臣紀大禹之謨而首之以此蓋謂昔禹之佐舜
也天下之大患旣平致治之大功已定由是祗
台德先著而為聲教之布流行洋溢有不疾而
速之機也方懋厥德發而為教化之施浸漬浹
洽有不行而至之妙也漸於東海被於西海無
遠弗届燦然禮樂衣冠之會矣暨於南海及於
===
北海舉世丕冒煥然聲名文物之區矣是蓋職
盡于錫圭之餘化行于功成之日而禹之心不
但已也誠以好問如舜而望治之心無窮禹於
是而敬應之彼此有協恭之美樂善如舜求道
之心罔極禹於是而將順之明良孚一德之休
下而民德之觀感係焉則君臣之艱不可以不
愼也而經世之大要是陳豈曰治已隆矣責難
其少置耶上而天道之昭鑒存焉則善惡之辯
不可以不嚴也而保邦之鴻謨是獻豈曰君已
punctuated: 已成天下之大化，猶獻天下之大猷，史臣賛聖人然也。甚矣，聖人之不自滿假也！大化旣成於天下，而猶獻其猷於帝焉，圖治之心何至哉！史臣紀大禹之謨，而首之以此，蓋謂昔禹之佐舜也，天下之大患旣平，致治之大功已定。由是祗台德先，著而為聲教之布，流行洋溢，有不疾而速之機也；方懋厥德，發而為教化之施，浸漬浹洽，有不行而至之妙也。漸於東海，被於西海，無遠弗届，燦然禮樂衣冠之會矣；暨於南海，及於北海，舉世丕冒，煥然聲名文物之區矣。是蓋職盡于錫圭之餘，化行于功成之日，而禹之心不但已也。誠以好問如舜，而望治之心無窮，禹於是而敬應之，彼此有協恭之美；樂善如舜，求道之心罔極，禹於是而將順之，明良孚一德之休。下而民德之觀感係焉，則君臣之艱不可以不愼也，而經世之大要是陳，豈曰治已隆矣，責難其少置耶？上而天道之昭鑒存焉，則善惡之辯不可以不嚴也，而保邦之鴻謨是獻，豈曰君已
translation_en:
Having already accomplished the great moral transformation of all under Heaven, he still presented grand counsels for governing all under Heaven: thus did the court historian praise the sage. How utterly the sage refused to become complacent or self-satisfied! Though the great transformation had already been accomplished throughout the realm, he still presented his counsels to the emperor. How profound was his devotion to good government! The court historian recorded the Counsels of the Great Yu and placed this statement at their beginning. His meaning was that, when Yu assisted Shun, the great calamity afflicting the realm had already been quelled, and the great achievement of establishing good government had been secured. Thus, reverently giving precedence to his own virtue [?], he made it manifest through the dissemination of moral instruction, which spread and overflowed everywhere, possessing the power to advance swiftly without haste. Striving to strengthen his virtue, he expressed it through the exercise of transforming instruction, which permeated and saturated everything, possessing the wondrous capacity to arrive without traveling. It reached the Eastern Sea and extended to the Western Sea, leaving no place untouched, however remote: a splendid gathering of ritual, music, and people in ceremonial dress. It reached the Southern Sea and extended to the Northern Sea, abundantly covering the whole world: a radiant domain of illustrious reputation and cultural refinement.

Thus, after receiving the jade tablet, he had fully discharged his duties; with his work accomplished, his transforming influence prevailed. Yet Yu’s heart did not rest content with this alone. For Shun so delighted in asking questions that his desire for good government knew no bounds. Yu therefore responded to him reverently, and the two displayed the excellence of harmonious respect. Shun so delighted in goodness that his desire to seek the Way knew no limit. Yu therefore supported and furthered his intentions, and the enlightened ruler and worthy minister realized the excellence of being united in virtue.

Below, the people’s moral character depended on what they observed and how they were moved by it. The difficulties of serving as ruler and minister therefore demanded careful attention, and Yu set forth the essentials of ordering the world. Could he have said that government had already attained greatness, and that urging difficult duties upon the ruler might therefore be set aside for a while? Above, the luminous scrutiny of Heaven’s Way remained. The distinction between good and evil therefore demanded strict attention, and Yu presented grand counsels for preserving the state. Could he have said that the ruler had already…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
聖矣陳善姑少緩耶是則化成既見澤民之仁
謨陳又見致君之義古之大臣當大任而遠慮
也如此夫抑論治化之盛未有加于有虞之世
也而君臣上下方且勉力不怠毎皇皇然惟恐
難成之功易隳而謀猷之陳交相儆戒君不自
聖臣不自滿相與都俞吁咈于一堂之上惟日
不足此其治所以卓乎不可及也後世論絕德
者曰禹之功皐陶之謨自今觀之禹豈徒功而
已哉
===
王拜手稽首曰公不敢不敬天之休來相
宅其作周匹休公既定宅伻來來視予
卜休恒吉我二人共貞公其以予萬億
年敬天之休拜手稽首誨言
施繼遠
考試官教諭張批形容尊異周公處親切
考試官教授黃批成王叙謝之情此作盡之
賢王敬禮大臣必叙其建都之美而謝其卜都
之辭也蓋建都稽卜事未有重于此者賢王叙
punctuated:
聖矣，陳善姑少緩耶？是則化成，既見澤民之仁；謨陳，又見致君之義。古之大臣當大任而遠慮也如此夫！抑論治化之盛，未有加于有虞之世也，而君臣上下方且勉力不怠，毎皇皇然，惟恐難成之功易隳，而謀猷之陳，交相儆戒。君不自聖，臣不自滿，相與都俞吁咈于一堂之上，惟日不足。此其治所以卓乎不可及也。後世論絕德者曰：「禹之功，皐陶之謨。」自今觀之，禹豈徒功而已哉！

王拜手稽首曰：「公不敢不敬天之休，來相宅，其作周匹休。公既定宅，伻來，來視予卜休，恒吉。我二人共貞，公其以予萬億年敬天之休。」拜手稽首，誨言。

施繼遠

考試官教諭張批：形容尊異周公處親切。
考試官教授黃批：成王叙謝之情，此作盡之。

賢王敬禮大臣，必叙其建都之美，而謝其卜都之辭也。蓋建都稽卜，事未有重于此者。賢王叙
translation_en:
…already a sage, might the presentation of good counsel be relaxed a little? Thus, the completion of the transforming work revealed his benevolence in bringing benefits to the people; the presentation of his counsels further revealed his righteousness in bringing his ruler to perfection. Such was the foresight with which the great ministers of antiquity bore their great responsibilities!

Now, in the flourishing of government and moral transformation, no age surpassed that of Youyu [Shun]. Yet ruler and ministers, high and low, continued to exert themselves tirelessly. Ever anxious, they feared only that achievements difficult to accomplish might readily be undone; in presenting their plans and counsels, they admonished and cautioned one another. The ruler did not regard himself as a sage, nor were his ministers self-satisfied. Together in a single hall, they voiced approval and dissent, finding the days insufficient for their work. This was why their government stood so far beyond the reach of later ages. Those in later generations who discussed surpassing virtue spoke of “Yu’s achievements and Gao Yao’s counsels.” Viewed now, could Yu’s contribution have consisted of achievements alone?

The king bowed with hands clasped and knocked his head to the ground, saying: “You, Duke, dared not fail to revere Heaven’s favor. You came to inspect the site for the capital, that it might bring Zhou corresponding blessings. Once you had determined the site, you sent a messenger, who came to show me the favorable divination: enduring good fortune. Let us two jointly uphold what is right. May you enable me, for myriad upon myriad years, to revere Heaven’s favor.” He bowed with hands clasped and knocked his head to the ground, acknowledging the words of instruction.

Shi Jiyuan

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: The passages describing the exceptional honor accorded to the Duke of Zhou are apt and vivid.
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: This composition fully conveys King Cheng’s feelings as he recounts the Duke’s services and expresses his gratitude.

When a worthy king honors a great minister with due ceremony, he must recount the excellence of that minister’s work in establishing the capital and give thanks for his words concerning the divination of its site. For no undertaking is weightier than establishing a capital and consulting divination. The worthy king recounts…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
而謝之安得不致其敬哉成王授使者以復周
公而拜手稽首蓋尊異元勳而重其禮也乃曰
宅中圖大天休渥矣公弗敢以慢心乗之故繼
太保而大相東土仰稽天心俯察地理配周命
于無窮乎逮夫元龜協吉基圖定矣公不敢以
已意裁之故遣使而昭示予二人休祥朕兆無疆
惟吉我二人其共當乎是公之宅洛也規模壮
偉允矣萬邦之方蓋欲我穆穆皇皇以宜王萬
億年敬天之休也用意何至哉氣象恢宏誠哉
===
惟民所止蓋欲我子子孫孫永保民萬億載荷
天之寵也為謀何遠哉是蓋撝謙于將意之餘
而優崇于感德之際故又拜手稽首以為告卜
之辭使固獻之矣然含蓄無涯至教隱然于言
外庸敢忘乎陳卜之言予固受之矣然該括深
微而至意宛然于面命敢不謝乎吁始盡禮而
叙之詳終致謝而敬之至君臣之相與何其盛
哉大抵宅洛者先王之意周公成王成之雖則
取天地之中實為式化殷民之地故遷洛之後
punctuated: 而謝之，安得不致其敬哉？成王授使者以復周公，而拜手稽首，蓋尊異元勳而重其禮也。乃曰：「宅中圖大，天休渥矣。公弗敢以慢心乗之，故繼太保而大相東土，仰稽天心，俯察地理，配周命于無窮乎！逮夫元龜協吉，基圖定矣，公不敢以已意裁之，故遣使而昭示予二人，休祥朕兆，無疆惟吉，我二人其共當乎！是公之宅洛也，規模壮偉，允矣萬邦之方，蓋欲我穆穆皇皇以宜王，萬億年敬天之休也，用意何至哉！氣象恢宏，誠哉惟民所止，蓋欲我子子孫孫永保民，萬億載荷天之寵也，為謀何遠哉！」是蓋撝謙于將意之餘，而優崇于感德之際，故又拜手稽首，以為：「告卜之辭，使固獻之矣，然含蓄無涯，至教隱然于言外，庸敢忘乎？陳卜之言，予固受之矣，然該括深微，而至意宛然于面命，敢不謝乎？」吁！始盡禮而叙之詳，終致謝而敬之至，君臣之相與何其盛哉！大抵宅洛者，先王之意，周公、成王成之。雖則取天地之中，實為式化殷民之地，故遷洛之後，
translation_en:
…and thanked him: how could he fail to show the utmost reverence? King Cheng entrusted the envoy with a reply to the Duke of Zhou, bowing with hands joined and touching his forehead to the ground. In this way he accorded exceptional honor to a founding minister of outstanding merit and gave full weight to the ceremonial courtesies.

He then said: “In establishing the capital at the center and planning great undertakings, Heaven’s favor has been abundant. You, my lord, dared not meet it with an indolent heart. Thus, following the Grand Guardian, you thoroughly surveyed the eastern lands, looking upward to investigate Heaven’s intentions and downward to examine the configuration of the land, that Zhou might remain worthy of its mandate forever! When the great tortoise yielded auspicious signs and the plan for establishing the capital was settled, you dared not decide according to your own wishes. You therefore sent an envoy to make the matter clearly known to us two. These felicitous signs and portents promise boundless good fortune: should we two not bear its charge together? Your establishment of the capital at Luo is magnificent in scale, truly a model for the myriad states. Surely you intend that I should be solemn and resplendent, worthy to reign, reverently receiving Heaven’s favor for countless millions of years. How consummate your purpose! Its scope is expansive, truly a place where the people may settle. Surely you intend that my descendants, generation after generation, should protect the people forever and bear Heaven’s favor for countless millions of years. How far-reaching your plans!”

Here, after conveying his feelings, he further displayed humility; in gratitude for the duke’s virtue, he accorded him exceptional honor. Thus he again bowed with hands joined and touched his forehead to the ground, reflecting: “The envoy has indeed presented the words reporting the divination. Yet their implications are inexhaustible, and the highest instruction lies hidden beyond the words. How could I dare forget them? I have indeed received the account of the divination. Yet it embraces profound subtleties, and its deepest purpose is as vividly present as if I were being instructed face to face. How could I fail to give thanks?”

Ah! At the outset he observed every courtesy and recounted the matter in detail; at the close he expressed thanks and showed the utmost reverence. How splendid was this relationship between ruler and minister! Establishing the capital at Luo was, in essence, the intention of the former king; the Duke of Zhou and King Cheng brought it to completion. Although they chose the center of Heaven and Earth, it was in fact to serve as a place for transforming the people of Yin through exemplary instruction. Thus, after the move to Luo…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
成王退居宗周而留公治洛蓋成王不欲舍祖
宗之舊而託周公以承保之責卒之殷民化訓
而王業靈長八百年精神命脉未有不基于此
詩□
湛湛露斯在彼杞棘顯允君子莫不令德其
桐其椅其實離離豈弟君子莫不令儀
李登
同考試官教諭李批君禮臣恭宛然在目
同考試官教諭趙批成周明良氣象模寫殆盡
===
考試官教諭張批明白正大
考試官教授黃批典雅精當
王者於諸侯兩興其與燕之善也夫恃恩易忽
於禮也諸侯與燕而德儀交盡焉其來天子之
予也亦宜矣此天子燕諸侯之詩其意蓋謂慈
惠者君之恩敬慎者臣之禮今日之燕何如耶
因興之曰天道以普物爲心也湛湛露斯則在
彼杞棘而優渥之惟均矣况我顯允之君子秉
離之明體孚之貞皆磐石我宗社者也登筵于
punctuated:
成王退居宗周，而留公治洛。蓋成王不欲舍祖宗之舊，而託周公以承保之責。卒之殷民化訓，而王業靈長，八百年精神命脉，未有不基于此。
詩□
「湛湛露斯，在彼杞棘。顯允君子，莫不令德。其桐其椅，其實離離。豈弟君子，莫不令儀。」
李登
同考試官教諭李批：君禮臣恭，宛然在目。
同考試官教諭趙批：成周明良氣象，模寫殆盡。
考試官教諭張批：明白正大。
考試官教授黃批：典雅精當。
王者於諸侯，兩興其與燕之善也。夫恃恩易忽於禮也，諸侯與燕而德儀交盡焉，其來天子之予也，亦宜矣。此天子燕諸侯之詩，其意蓋謂慈惠者君之恩，敬慎者臣之禮。今日之燕何如耶？因興之曰：天道以普物爲心也，湛湛露斯，則在彼杞棘，而優渥之惟均矣。况我顯允之君子，秉離之明，體孚之貞，皆磐石我宗社者也。登筵于
translation_en:
…King Cheng withdrew to reside at Zongzhou, leaving the Duke of Zhou to govern Luo. King Cheng was unwilling to abandon the ancestral seat, and entrusted the Duke of Zhou with responsibility for sustaining and safeguarding the realm. In the end, the people of Yin were transformed through instruction, and the royal enterprise long endured. The vitality and lifeblood of its eight hundred years were all grounded in this.
Book of Odes [illegible character]
“Copious is the dew,
Upon those wolfberry bushes and thorn trees.
Illustrious and trustworthy are the gentlemen;
None lacks excellent virtue.
Those tong trees and those yi trees,
Their fruits hang in clusters.
Those gracious and amiable gentlemen;
None lacks excellent deportment.”
Li Deng
Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The ruler’s ritual propriety and the ministers’ reverence stand vividly before our eyes.”
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “The atmosphere of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers in the Zhou dynasty is depicted almost to perfection.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Clear, upright, and dignified.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “Classically elegant, precise, and apt.”
The king uses two evocative comparisons to praise the excellence of the feudal lords’ conduct at his banquet. Now, reliance on favor can easily lead to neglect of ritual propriety. Yet when the feudal lords attend the banquet, they fully display both virtue and deportment; it is fitting, therefore, that they should win the Son of Heaven’s approval. This is an ode about the Son of Heaven’s banquet for the feudal lords. Its meaning is that kindness and beneficence constitute the ruler’s favor, while reverence and caution constitute his ministers’ ritual propriety. What, then, is today’s banquet like?
Thus it introduces an evocative comparison: the Way of Heaven takes the universal nurturing of things as its purpose. The copious dew rests upon those wolfberry bushes and thorn trees, bestowing its abundant moisture equally upon them. How much more, then, upon our illustrious and trustworthy gentlemen, who possess the brightness of Li and embody the steadfastness of sincerity, and who all serve as firm foundations for our ancestral temple and altars of state! Taking their places at the banquet here…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
斯孰有不令德者乎齊聖之心克持於旣醉之
餘温恭之念愈嚴於交錯之後夜飮之厭厭一
初筵之秩秩矣何伐德之足慮耶又興之曰地
道以生物爲功也其桐其椅則其實離離而蕃
衍之皆盛矣况我豈弟之君子暢豫之樂協巽
之順皆龍光我邦家者也依几于斯孰有不令
儀者乎情雖洽也而禮益脩不吳不敖也飮雖
久也而容益愼不戢不難也在宗之雍雍一至
止之肅肅矣何愆儀之足慮耶吁燕在君也而
===
善是燕者臣也周王於諸侯而歌之以此其亦
美不忘規者歟大抵先王制爲燕享非徒爲游
豫之舉所以合上下之歡而通其情者也故惟
開納之誠可以啓忠告之益而有道之君子亦
必待禮貌恭敬而后得其委心也古之聖帝明
王其盛德大業未有不成於此者卽諸湛露之
歌其義備矣此上下之所以交而爲泰也此周
德之所以爲盛也讀是詩者可以觀矣
民之靡盈誰夙知而莫成
punctuated:
斯，孰有不令德者乎？齊聖之心克持於旣醉之餘，温恭之念愈嚴於交錯之後。夜飮之厭厭，一初筵之秩秩矣，何伐德之足慮耶？又興之曰：地道以生物爲功也，其桐其椅，則其實離離，而蕃衍之皆盛矣。况我豈弟之君子，暢豫之樂，協巽之順，皆龍光我邦家者也。依几于斯，孰有不令儀者乎？情雖洽也，而禮益脩，不吳不敖也；飮雖久也，而容益愼，不戢不難也。在宗之雍雍，一至止之肅肅矣，何愆儀之足慮耶？吁！燕在君也，而善是燕者臣也。周王於諸侯而歌之以此，其亦美不忘規者歟？大抵先王制爲燕享，非徒爲游豫之舉，所以合上下之歡而通其情者也。故惟開納之誠，可以啓忠告之益，而有道之君子，亦必待禮貌恭敬而后得其委心也。古之聖帝明王，其盛德大業，未有不成於此者。卽諸《湛露》之歌，其義備矣。此上下之所以交而爲泰也，此周德之所以爲盛也。讀是詩者可以觀矣。

民之靡盈，誰夙知而莫成？
translation_en:
…here, who among them does not possess excellent virtue? Their wise and sagacious minds remain composed even after intoxication; their concern for gentleness and reverence becomes still more exacting after the drinking vessels have passed back and forth. The tranquil pleasure of drinking at night matches the orderly conduct at the banquet’s beginning. What need is there to fear injury to their virtue?

Again, the poem introduces its meaning through an evocative image: the Way of Earth takes the generation of living things as its achievement. Those tong and yi trees bear abundant fruit, flourishing alike in their growth and propagation. How much more is this true of our gracious gentlemen! With their joyful ease and harmonious compliance, they all bring great glory to our state. Leaning on their armrests here, who among them does not display excellent deportment? Though their feelings grow intimate, their observance of ritual becomes still more cultivated: they are neither clamorous nor arrogant. Though they drink long, their bearing becomes still more circumspect, requiring neither restraint nor rebuke [?]. Their harmony within the ancestral temple matches their solemnity on arrival. What need is there to fear a lapse in deportment?

Ah! The ruler provides the banquet, but his ministers make it a good banquet. When the king of Zhou sang this to the feudal lords, was he not praising them without forgetting admonition? Generally speaking, the former kings instituted banquets and feasts not merely for recreation, but to unite the joy of superiors and subordinates and allow their feelings to pass freely between them. Thus only sincerity in welcoming and accepting counsel can elicit the benefit of loyal advice. Gentlemen who possess the Way, too, must be treated with courtesy and respect before their wholehearted devotion can be secured. Among the sage emperors and enlightened kings of antiquity, none attained abundant virtue and great accomplishments without this. The meaning is fully expressed in the song Abundant Dew (Zhan lu). This is how superiors and subordinates interact to bring about peaceful prosperity; this is how the virtue of Zhou became so flourishing. Those who read this poem can perceive it.

“Among the people, none is complete; who gains knowledge early and attains accomplishment late?” [?]

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
史筆
同考試官教諭李批溫厚和平真善說詩者
同考試官教諭趙批寫出武公求教之心可錄
考試官教諭張批明暢
考試官教授黃批純正
人能虛心以受教斯易於有成矣夫虛德之歸
也虛斯明明斯成矣欲成厥德而可以自滿乎
衛武公作抑詩使人日誦於其側以自警至此
若曰爾德之不成知之晚也爾知之不早滿之
===
招也爾欲成德無亦滿之是去乎人誠知夫天
下之義理無窮而一人之知識有限也卑以自
牧每懷夫望道未見之心慮以下人恒切夫檢
身不及之念有焉而若無也實焉而若虛也孳
孳好善之誠自忘夫崇高之分敢訑訑以驕人
耶明而守之以愚也勇而守之以怯也拳拳好
問之切不遺于芻蕘之言肯沾沾以自足耶夫
民之靡盈如此是其資性之謙冲足為受善之
地而意氣之感召孰不興願教之心吾知教戒
punctuated:
史筆

同考試官教諭李批：溫厚和平，真善說詩者。
同考試官教諭趙批：寫出武公求教之心，可錄。
考試官教諭張批：明暢。
考試官教授黃批：純正。

人能虛心以受教，斯易於有成矣。夫虛，德之歸也；虛斯明，明斯成矣。欲成厥德，而可以自滿乎？衛武公作《抑》詩，使人日誦於其側以自警。至此若曰：「爾德之不成，知之晚也；爾知之不早，滿之招也。爾欲成德，無亦滿之是去乎？」人誠知夫天下之義理無窮，而一人之知識有限也，卑以自牧，每懷夫望道未見之心；慮以下人，恒切夫檢身不及之念。有焉而若無也，實焉而若虛也，孳孳好善之誠，自忘夫崇高之分，敢訑訑以驕人耶？明而守之以愚也，勇而守之以怯也，拳拳好問之切，不遺于芻蕘之言，肯沾沾以自足耶？夫民之靡盈如此，是其資性之謙冲，足為受善之地，而意氣之感召，孰不興願教之心？吾知教戒
translation_en:
Shi Bi

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Gentle, generous, balanced, and harmonious: truly someone skilled at expounding the Odes.”
Associate Examiner Zhao, Instructor, comments: “Expresses Duke Wu’s desire to receive instruction; worthy of selection.”
Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “Clear and fluent.”
Examiner Huang, Professor, comments: “Pure and orthodox.”

If a person can empty his mind of conceit and receive instruction, he will readily attain accomplishment. Humility is where virtue finds its home. Humility brings understanding, and understanding brings accomplishment. Can one wish to perfect one’s virtue yet remain complacent? Duke Wu of Wei composed the ode “Admonition” (Yi) and had someone recite it beside him daily to warn himself. At this point, it is as though he says: “Your failure to perfect your virtue comes from understanding too late; your failure to understand early comes from complacency. If you wish to perfect your virtue, should you not cast off complacency?”

If a person truly understands that the principles of rightness throughout the world are inexhaustible, while one individual’s knowledge is limited, he will cultivate himself through humility, always feeling that he gazes toward the Way but has not yet seen it. He will thoughtfully place himself below others [?], constantly intent upon examining himself as though he still fell short. Possessing ability, he will seem to possess none; being full, he will seem empty. In his tireless sincerity in loving goodness, he will forget his exalted station: would he dare arrogantly to look down upon others? Though discerning, he will preserve that discernment through seeming foolishness; though courageous, he will preserve that courage through seeming timidity. In his earnest eagerness to ask questions, he will overlook not even the words of grass cutters and wood gatherers: would he consent to smug self-satisfaction?

When a person is thus free of conceit, the modesty of his natural disposition provides fertile ground for receiving goodness. Moved by his spirit and bearing, who would not feel a desire to teach him? I know that instruction and admonition …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之下聰明為之日啓一身之微而衆善咸萃固
將先人而有知也領悟之餘問學以之日新一
心之虚而衆理咸歸固已先人而有覺也知焉
既早則知至至之忽不自知其優入於聖賢之
域而學之所成蓋有如金錫圭璧者矣夫豈待
抱子而尚未有成乎知終終之忽不自覺其先
登乎義理之岸而德之所就蓋無不淑慎臧嘉
者矣夫豈待既耄而尚未有成乎由是觀之謙
斯受益而有光滿則招損而無成玆固聖愚之
===
所由分而成敗之所以異也爾小子其亦知所
從事也哉考之易曰君子以虚受人書曰謙受
益滿招損君子進德脩業實以謙虚為要但人
君處崇高富貴之中驕泰易生而受教尤難武
公乃惓惓以靡盈自儆真上契易書之旨而得
大禹不自滿假之心此其所以踐履篤實而終
成睿聖之德也嗚呼賢哉
春秋
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏莊
punctuated:
之下，聰明為之日啓，一身之微而衆善咸萃，固將先人而有知也。領悟之餘，問學以之日新，一心之虚而衆理咸歸，固已先人而有覺也。知焉既早，則知至至之，忽不自知其優入於聖賢之域，而學之所成蓋有如金錫圭璧者矣。夫豈待抱子而尚未有成乎？知終終之，忽不自覺其先登乎義理之岸，而德之所就蓋無不淑慎臧嘉者矣。夫豈待既耄而尚未有成乎？由是觀之，謙斯受益而有光，滿則招損而無成。玆固聖愚之所由分，而成敗之所以異也。爾小子其亦知所從事也哉！考之，《易》曰：「君子以虚受人。」《書》曰：「謙受益，滿招損。」君子進德脩業，實以謙虚為要。但人君處崇高富貴之中，驕泰易生，而受教尤難。武公乃惓惓以靡盈自儆，真上契《易》《書》之旨，而得大禹不自滿假之心。此其所以踐履篤實，而終成睿聖之德也。嗚呼，賢哉！

春秋

春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。莊
translation_en:
…under such instruction and admonition, his understanding grows clearer each day. Though he is but one insignificant person, all virtues gather in him; surely he will attain knowledge before others. Through what he comprehends, his inquiry and learning are renewed daily. Because his mind is receptive, all principles converge within it; surely he has already attained awakening before others. Having gained knowledge early, he knows the point he must reach and reaches it. Before he realizes it, he has entered with ease into the realm of sages and worthies, and his accomplishments in learning are like gold and tin, jade tablets and jade discs. How could he wait until he has a child in his arms and still have accomplished nothing? He knows how to bring matters to completion and completes them. Before he realizes it, he has reached the shore of moral principle ahead of others, and his attainments in virtue are wholly good, circumspect, worthy, and admirable. How could he wait until he is already aged and still have accomplished nothing? Viewed in this light, humility brings benefit and lustre, while self-satisfaction invites loss and leaves one without accomplishment. This indeed is what separates sages from fools and accounts for the difference between success and failure. You young men should surely know, then, where to direct your efforts!

Examining the classics, we find that the Book of Changes says: “The gentleman receives others with an open mind.” The Book of Documents says: “Humility receives benefit; self-satisfaction invites loss.” For the gentleman, humility is truly essential to advancing in virtue and cultivating his undertakings. Yet a ruler lives amid exalted rank, wealth, and honour, where arrogance and complacency easily arise and accepting instruction is especially difficult. Duke Wu earnestly warned himself against self-satisfaction. He truly accorded with the purport of the Book of Changes and the Book of Documents and grasped the spirit of the Great Yu, who was never complacently satisfied with himself. This is why his practice was earnest and genuine, and why he ultimately attained the virtue of sagely wisdom. Ah, how worthy he was!

Spring and Autumn Annals

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
公十有三年秋七月辛巳豹及諸侯之
大夫盟于宋襄公二十有七年
楊懷哲
考試官敎諭張批得聖人經世之志
考試官敎授黄批嚴整可式
春秋於會盟也有罪其啓霸之跡有罪其召夷
之横夫王降而霸霸降而夷皆天下之大故也
聖人至是不能不憂其始焉昔齊桓公假平亂
之名偕四國爲圖霸之計夫是以有北杏之會
===
考之文王始爲西伯受商王之命也矧赫赫宗
周典章之舊猶存桓也未聞受命顧可遽主會
盟之政耶當時或有執此詞者王道尚無恙也
惟夫四國戴之自是天下諸侯皆俛首東向而
宗齊又烏知夫王也夫桓霸旣開其端末流不
可復制迨桓之没一霸於宋襄再霸於晉文秦
穆楚莊相繼而起竟成五霸之名皆此會爲之
作俑也周道之微聖人憂焉欲誅始亂正王法
人四國以見之也故曰五霸者三王之罪人也
punctuated:
公十有三年。秋七月辛巳，豹及諸侯之大夫盟于宋。襄公二十有七年。
楊懷哲。
考試官敎諭張批：得聖人經世之志。
考試官敎授黄批：嚴整可式。
春秋於會盟也，有罪其啓霸之跡，有罪其召夷之横。夫王降而霸，霸降而夷，皆天下之大故也。聖人至是，不能不憂其始焉。昔齊桓公假平亂之名，偕四國爲圖霸之計，夫是以有北杏之會。考之文王始爲西伯，受商王之命也。矧赫赫宗周，典章之舊猶存，桓也未聞受命，顧可遽主會盟之政耶？當時或有執此詞者，王道尚無恙也。惟夫四國戴之，自是天下諸侯皆俛首東向而宗齊，又烏知夫王也？夫桓霸旣開其端，末流不可復制。迨桓之没，一霸於宋襄，再霸於晉文，秦穆、楚莊相繼而起，竟成五霸之名，皆此會爲之作俑也。周道之微，聖人憂焉，欲誅始亂，正王法，人四國以見之也。故曰：「五霸者，三王之罪人也。」
translation_en:
…the thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang. “In autumn, in the seventh month, on the xinsi day, Bao and the grandees of the various states made a covenant at Song.” The twenty-seventh year of Duke Xiang.

Yang Huaizhe.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Grasps the Sage’s purpose in ordering the world.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Prefectural School Instructor: “Rigorous and well ordered; worthy of serving as a model.”

In its treatment of meetings and covenants, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes condemns the acts that inaugurated hegemony, and sometimes condemns the arrogance that brought in the non-Chinese peoples. For the decline from kingship to hegemony, and from hegemony to domination by non-Chinese peoples, were both momentous upheavals in the world. At these points, the Sage could not but be concerned about their beginnings. Formerly, Duke Huan of Qi, under the pretext of pacifying disorder, joined with four states to devise a plan for attaining hegemony. Thus came about the meeting at Beixing.

Consider King Wen: when he first became the Earl of the West, he received his commission from the king of Shang. Moreover, the inherited institutions and statutes of the illustrious Zhou royal house still survived. Yet Duke Huan was not known to have received a royal commission. How, then, could he abruptly take charge of meetings and covenants? Had anyone at that time upheld this argument, the Way of kingship might still have remained intact. But the four states supported him, and thereafter all the lords of the realm bowed their heads, turned eastward, and acknowledged Qi as their leader. What recognition did they any longer have of the king?

Once Duke Huan’s hegemony had set this process in motion, its subsequent course could no longer be controlled. After Huan’s death, hegemony passed first to Duke Xiang of Song, then to Duke Wen of Jin; Duke Mu of Qin and King Zhuang of Chu arose in succession, ultimately completing the roster known as the Five Hegemons. It was this meeting that set the precedent for them all. The Sage grieved over the decline of the Zhou Way. Wishing to condemn those who first brought disorder and to uphold royal law, he expressed this by designating the representatives of the four states simply as “men.” Thus it is said: “The Five Hegemons were offenders against the Three Kings.”

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
若合左師倡弭兵之說楚屈建主交見之議夫
是以有于宋之盟稽之宣王命將南征守周公
之訓也矧堂堂晉伯安攘之烈猶存楚也義當
膺懲顧敢交見晉楚之從耶當時苟有仗此議
者霸圖尚不墜也惟夫趙武從之自是中國諸
侯皆傾心南向而朝楚又烏知夫霸也夫大勢
旣張於前燎原莫之能禦迄靈之世一逞於會
申再逞於伐吳執徐滅賴無與抗違遂貽八年
之禍皆此盟為之造端也中國之衰聖人憂焉
===
欲誅大惡正人倫再言宋以見之也故曰今之
諸侯五霸之罪人也吁會也繫王霸消長之機
盟也關夷夏盛衰之由聖人作經至是其傷之
也至矣嘗觀上古稱號其名有三變皇矣而帝
帝矣而王應乎時也况春秋之頽運乎王迹熄
不得不變而為霸霸道微不得不變而為夷勢
使然也雖然可憂也亦可幸也如齊桓召陵之
師霸也楚莊辰陵之盟夷也而孔子皆與之又
曰微管仲吾其被髮左衽矣夷狄之有君不如
punctuated:
若合左師倡弭兵之說，楚屈建主交見之議，夫是以有于宋之盟。稽之宣王命將南征，守周公之訓也。矧堂堂晉伯，安攘之烈猶存，楚也義當膺懲，顧敢交見晉楚之從耶？當時苟有仗此議者，霸圖尚不墜也。惟夫趙武從之，自是中國諸侯皆傾心南向而朝楚，又烏知夫霸也？夫大勢旣張於前，燎原莫之能禦。迄靈之世，一逞於會申，再逞於伐吳，執徐滅賴，無與抗違，遂貽八年之禍，皆此盟為之造端也。中國之衰，聖人憂焉，欲誅大惡、正人倫，再言宋以見之也。故曰：「今之諸侯，五霸之罪人也。」

吁！會也，繫王霸消長之機；盟也，關夷夏盛衰之由。聖人作經，至是其傷之也至矣！嘗觀上古稱號，其名有三變：皇矣而帝，帝矣而王，應乎時也。况春秋之頽運乎？王迹熄，不得不變而為霸；霸道微，不得不變而為夷，勢使然也。雖然，可憂也，亦可幸也。如齊桓召陵之師，霸也；楚莊辰陵之盟，夷也，而孔子皆與之。又曰：「微管仲，吾其被髮左衽矣。」「夷狄之有君，不如
translation_en:
As for the Minister of the Left [the opening wording 若合 is doubtful], he advocated putting an end to warfare, while Qu Jian of Chu championed reciprocal court visits. Thus the covenant at Song came about. Consider how King Xuan ordered his generals to campaign southward: he was observing the instructions of the Duke of Zhou. How much more should the illustrious hegemon of Jin have done so, when the achievements of securing the Chinese states and repelling outsiders still endured! Chu ought in justice to have been punished. How could anyone dare instead to arrange reciprocal court visits by the states following Jin and Chu? Had anyone then upheld this argument, the enterprise of hegemony would not yet have collapsed. But Zhao Wu accepted the proposal. Thereafter, the lords of the central states all turned their hearts southward and paid court to Chu. What regard did they still have for the hegemon? Once this great momentum had developed, it was like a prairie fire that none could withstand. By the reign of King Ling, Chu asserted its will first at the assembly at Shen and again in attacking Wu; it seized the ruler of Xu and destroyed Lai, with none able to resist or defy it. This ultimately brought the calamity of the eighth year: its beginnings lay entirely in this covenant. The Sage grieved over the decline of the central states. Wishing to condemn great evil and rectify human relationships, he mentioned Song twice to make this judgment manifest. Thus it is said: “The feudal lords of today are offenders against the Five Hegemons.”

Alas! The assembly bore upon the turning point in the waxing and waning of kingship and hegemony; the covenant concerned the causes of the rise and decline of the non-Chinese peoples and the Xia. When the Sage composed the Classic, his grief at this point was profound indeed! I have observed that the titles of rulers in high antiquity underwent three changes: from august sovereigns to emperors, and from emperors to kings, in response to their times. How much more was this so amid the declining fortunes of the Spring and Autumn period! When the traces of true kingship disappeared, it necessarily gave way to hegemony; when the way of hegemony declined, it necessarily gave way to rule by non-Chinese peoples. Circumstances made it so. Nevertheless, although there was cause for concern, there was also cause for relief. Duke Huan of Qi’s expedition to Shaoling was an act of a hegemon; King Zhuang of Chu’s covenant at Chenling was an act of a non-Chinese ruler. Yet Confucius approved of both. He also said: “Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and fasten our robes on the left.” And: “The Yi and Di peoples’ having rulers is not as good as …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
諸夏之亡也亦幸之也爲其尚有補於周道也
城中城成公九年
呂鳳來
考試官教諭張批聖人重禮之意正如此
考試官教授黄批義精辭暢
春秋譏望國因其守國之微而昧於謹禮焉夫
城非春秋所貴也又不知謹禮以爲國故書以
致譏且魯成君國謂四境之守不足恃也乃有
中城之城切於宫庭朝市若亦得於保國者君
===
子則曰百雉之城七里之郭扞蔽也君人之事
設險之大端也故易曰王公設險以守其國辨
尊卑分貴賤明等威異物采令政也君人之紀
體險之大用也故易曰君子以辯上下定民志
是有國不可以無城有城不可以無禮何成也
惟見其城城不聞其謹禮耶若曰城以衞民其
效速也禮以防民其事緩矣抑不知經世安民
視道之得失一失其道國無常經禮之喪也固
無以範圍人心而杜絶陵替强者踰其節弱者
punctuated:
諸夏之亡也。」亦幸之也，爲其尚有補於周道也。

城中城。成公九年。
呂鳳來。
考試官教諭張批：聖人重禮之意，正如此。
考試官教授黄批：義精辭暢。

春秋譏望國，因其守國之微而昧於謹禮焉。夫城非春秋所貴也，又不知謹禮以爲國，故書以致譏。且魯成君國，謂四境之守不足恃也，乃有中城之城，切於宫庭朝市，若亦得於保國者。君子則曰：百雉之城，七里之郭，扞蔽也，君人之事，設險之大端也。故易曰：「王公設險，以守其國。」辨尊卑，分貴賤，明等威，異物采，令政也，君人之紀，體險之大用也。故易曰：「君子以辯上下，定民志。」是有國不可以無城，有城不可以無禮。何成也，惟見其城城，不聞其謹禮耶？若曰：城以衞民，其效速也；禮以防民，其事緩矣。抑不知經世安民，視道之得失。一失其道，國無常經。禮之喪也，固無以範圍人心而杜絶陵替，强者踰其節，弱者
translation_en:
…the states of the Xia without one.” This too was a cause for relief, because they still contributed something to the Way of Zhou.

“They fortified the inner city.” Ninth year of Duke Cheng.
By Lü Fenglai.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Precisely this is the sage’s intention in placing such weight on ritual propriety.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “The meaning is refined and the language fluent.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals censures the eminent state [?], because its means of defending the state were inadequate and it failed to understand the need for scrupulous observance of ritual propriety. Fortifications are not what the Spring and Autumn Annals prizes. Since the ruler also did not understand how to govern the state through careful observance of ritual, the event was recorded to convey censure. When Duke Cheng ruled Lu, he considered the defenses along its four borders insufficient to rely upon, and so fortified the inner city, close to the palace courts, the court of government, and the markets. This might seem to have contributed to preserving the state.

The gentleman, however, says: walls a hundred zhi in extent and an outer wall seven li in circuit provide protection. They are the business of a ruler and the principal means of establishing defensive barriers. Thus the Book of Changes says: “Kings and dukes establish defensive barriers to safeguard their states.” Distinguishing the honored from the lowly, separating the noble from the humble, making clear the dignity proper to each rank, and differentiating ceremonial objects and colors constitute good government. These are the governing principles of a ruler and the great practical application of embodying defensive barriers. Thus the Book of Changes says: “The gentleman distinguishes those above from those below and settles the people’s purposes.” Hence a state cannot be without walls, and a walled state cannot be without ritual propriety. Why, then, in the case of Duke Cheng, do we see only his building walls and hear nothing of his careful observance of ritual?

It is as though he said: “Walls protect the people, and their effects are swift; ritual restrains the people, but its work is slow.” Yet he did not understand that ordering the world and securing the people depend upon whether the Way is attained or lost. Once the Way is lost, the state has no enduring norms. When ritual is lost, there is indeed no means of keeping people’s hearts within bounds or preventing the encroachment of inferiors upon superiors. The strong exceed their proper limits, while the weak…

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
殺其分上下亂矣雖有城猶空國也國空則人
孰與守城果不足恃也易教人以設險寓謹禮
之意焉苟得其道國有常法禮之興也自有以
綱維衆志而限隔名分智者信其道愚者守其
度上下安矣雖無城猶善國也國善則人孰與
敵禮固所當謹也易教人以辨分即體險之謂
焉由是觀之非城無以為保障生民之具非禮
無以為固結民心之本緩急輕重明矣今乃急
於目前而遺經國之遠圖切于近小而畧安民
===
===
之大計其為儆守也益微其所以自治者益疎
謂之不知類者公其有焉說者謂凡城之誌皆
譏得春秋之旨矣抑春秋非無稽而然也左河
濟右泰華桀之險不可及左孟門右太行紂之
險莫能當矣然南巢一舉孟津一會又何有於
險耶即此可以驗中城焉嗚呼房闥不謹宣伯
諧行君臣交辱沙隨之事公亦幾不能免其身
而况於國乎其不能謹禮之明驗也春秋於此
非有所見而然歟
punctuated:
殺其分，上下亂矣。雖有城，猶空國也。國空，則人孰與守？城果不足恃也。《易》教人以設險，寓謹禮之意焉。苟得其道，國有常法，禮之興也，自有以綱維衆志而限隔名分。智者信其道，愚者守其度，上下安矣。雖無城，猶善國也。國善，則人孰與敵？禮固所當謹也。《易》教人以辨分，即體險之謂焉。由是觀之，非城無以為保障生民之具，非禮無以為固結民心之本，緩急輕重明矣。今乃急於目前，而遺經國之遠圖；切于近小，而畧安民之大計。其為儆守也益微，其所以自治者益疎。謂之不知類者，公其有焉。說者謂凡城之誌皆譏，得《春秋》之旨矣。
抑《春秋》非無稽而然也。左河濟，右泰華，桀之險不可及；左孟門，右太行，紂之險莫能當矣。然南巢一舉，孟津一會，又何有於險耶？即此可以驗中城焉。嗚呼！房闥不謹，宣伯諧行，君臣交辱。沙隨之事，公亦幾不能免其身，而况於國乎？其不能謹禮之明驗也。《春秋》於此，非有所見而然歟？
translation_en:
…the weak have their allotted standing diminished, and order between superiors and inferiors falls into confusion. Though there are city walls, the state is as good as empty. If the state is empty, with whom can one defend it? Walls indeed cannot be relied upon. When the Book of Changes teaches people to establish defensive barriers, it embeds within this the intention that they should carefully observe ritual propriety. If the proper Way is attained, the state has enduring standards. When ritual propriety flourishes, it provides the means to hold the people's purposes together and maintain the boundaries between designated ranks. The wise carry forward its Way, and the foolish observe its rules; superiors and inferiors alike are secure. Even without walls, the state remains well ordered. If the state is well ordered, who can contend against its people? Ritual propriety must therefore be carefully observed. When the Book of Changes teaches people to distinguish ranks, this is precisely what it means to embody the principle of defensive barriers. Viewed in this light, without walls there is no means of protecting the people, and without ritual propriety there is no foundation for binding their hearts together. The relative urgency and importance of these measures are clear. Yet now the immediate concern is treated as urgent, while the long-term design for governing the state is neglected; small, nearby matters are pressed, while the great plan for securing the people's peace is disregarded. Vigilance and defense become ever less effective, and the means of putting one's own government in order grow ever more deficient. If this is called a failure to understand how things belong together, the duke surely exemplifies it. Commentators say that every record of building city walls conveys criticism: they have grasped the purport of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
Yet the Spring and Autumn Annals does not take this position without evidence. With the He and Ji rivers on his left and Mounts Tai and Hua on his right, Jie possessed defensive barriers that none could match. With Mengmen on his left and the Taihang Mountains on his right, Zhou possessed defensive barriers that none could withstand. Yet with a single military action at Nanchao and a single assembly at Mengjin, what became of those barriers? This provides a test of the fortification of Zhongcheng. Alas! Propriety within the inner chambers was not carefully observed, and Xuanbo joined in illicit conduct [?], bringing disgrace upon ruler and minister alike. In the affair at Shasui, the duke himself nearly failed to escape unscathed—how much less could he secure the state? This is clear evidence of his failure to observe ritual propriety carefully. Was it not because the Spring and Autumn Annals perceived something here that it recorded the matter as it did?

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
禮記
事君以自顯也
謝寵
同考試官教諭文批說事顯字透徹
考試官教諭張批精切
考試官教授黃批明贍
記者論人臣道盡于事上身成于獲上蓋臣之
事君固道之所當盡耳而成身之榮抑豈有所
要而然哉禮運言君之分非所以事於人則所
===
===
以事人者其惟百姓乎彼臣以君爲元首故策
名委質左右就有方之養以承弼乎一人民以
后爲腹心故用下敬上夙夜效匪躬之節以服
勤於王室凡力所能爲無弗爲之有官守脩其
職有言責盡其忠務欲處其位而履其事也凡
分所當致無弗致之內以安中國外以攘夷狄
固敢受若直而怠若事也百姓事君如此豈徒
益於國而無利於已哉吾知匪事乎君則窮之
所養終於韜晦無以表見當時不行其義則幼
punctuated:
禮記

事君以自顯也

謝寵

同考試官教諭文批：說事顯字透徹。
考試官教諭張批：精切。
考試官教授黃批：明贍。

記者論人臣道盡于事上，身成于獲上。蓋臣之事君，固道之所當盡耳，而成身之榮，抑豈有所要而然哉？禮運言君之分，非所以事於人，則所以事人者，其惟百姓乎？彼臣以君爲元首，故策名委質，左右就有方之養，以承弼乎一人；民以后爲腹心，故用下敬上，夙夜效匪躬之節，以服勤於王室。凡力所能爲，無弗爲之：有官守，脩其職；有言責，盡其忠；務欲處其位而履其事也。凡分所當致，無弗致之：內以安中國，外以攘夷狄，固敢受若直而怠若事也？百姓事君如此，豈徒益於國而無利於已哉？吾知匪事乎君，則窮之所養終於韜晦，無以表見當時；不行其義，則幼
translation_en:
Book of Rites

“In serving the ruler, one brings distinction to oneself.”

Xie Chong

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: “The explanation of ‘serving’ and ‘distinction’ is penetrating.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “Precise and apposite.”
Comment by Examiner Huang, Professor: “Clear and ample.”

The compiler of the Record explains that a minister fulfills the Way through serving his superior and achieves personal fulfillment through gaining his superior’s favor. A minister’s service to his ruler is surely no more than the fulfillment of what the Way requires. Could the honor of personal fulfillment arise from seeking something in return? The “Evolution of Rites” chapter describes the ruler’s allotted role as one that does not entail serving others. Then those whose role is to serve others must be the common people, must they not?

Ministers regard the ruler as their head; thus they enter their names into service and pledge their allegiance, attending at his sides and receiving duly ordered support [?], to assist the One Man. The people regard their sovereign as their heart and vitals; thus, from their subordinate position, they honor their superior, displaying selfless devotion morning and night and laboring diligently for the royal house. Whatever lies within their power, they do: those charged with an office discharge its duties; those responsible for remonstrance give their utmost loyalty. Their aim is to fulfill the work belonging to the position they occupy. Whatever their allotted duty requires, they render in full: within, they bring peace to the Central States; beyond, they repel the Yi and Di. Would they indeed dare to accept their pay while neglecting their duties?

When the common people serve their ruler in this way, could it benefit only the state and bring no advantage to themselves? I know that, without serving the ruler, what they cultivated in obscurity would remain concealed, with no means of making it manifest to their contemporaries; if they did not put their righteousness into practice, then what they had in youth …

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之所學甘於懷藏何以明揚朝著今也奮庸熙
載而側陋之微獲覲天子之光脩其職者以才
顯盡其忠者以諫顯矣受爵策勳而閭閻之賤
得為萬夫之望安中國者以文顯攘夷狄者以
武顯矣身豈有不榮哉夫謀其國不遺其身如
此然則事君者雖所以成君乃所以自成也歟
大抵天下之勢莫患於禮教之不達而名分之
不定上下之分既定則自有相成之機夫豈强
勉而然耶故此曰則君以自治也養君以自安
===
也事君以自顯也中庸曰尊賢則不惑敬大臣
則不眩體羣臣則士之報禮重若此者君何以
負於臣臣何以負於君哉是故上下交而德業
成矣後之為君臣者可不鑒諸
夫樂者先王之所以飾喜也軍旅鈇鉞者
先王之所以飾怒也故先王之喜怒皆
得其儕焉喜則天下和之怒則暴亂者
畏之先王之道禮樂可謂盛矣
王廷佐
punctuated:
之所學，甘於懷藏，何以明揚朝著？今也奮庸熙載，而側陋之微獲覲天子之光，脩其職者以才顯，盡其忠者以諫顯矣。受爵策勳，而閭閻之賤得為萬夫之望，安中國者以文顯，攘夷狄者以武顯矣。身豈有不榮哉？夫謀其國，不遺其身如此。然則事君者，雖所以成君，乃所以自成也歟？大抵天下之勢，莫患於禮教之不達，而名分之不定。上下之分既定，則自有相成之機，夫豈强勉而然耶？故此曰：「則君以自治也，養君以自安也，事君以自顯也。」《中庸》曰：「尊賢則不惑，敬大臣則不眩，體羣臣則士之報禮重。」若此者，君何以負於臣，臣何以負於君哉？是故上下交而德業成矣。後之為君臣者，可不鑒諸？

夫樂者，先王之所以飾喜也；軍旅鈇鉞者，先王之所以飾怒也。故先王之喜怒，皆得其儕焉。喜則天下和之，怒則暴亂者畏之。先王之道，禮樂可謂盛矣。

王廷佐
translation_en:
…what they learned in youth would remain willingly concealed within them; how could they gain recognition and distinction at court? Now, exerting their abilities and bringing their tasks to fruition, even those of humble and obscure station may behold the radiance of the Son of Heaven. Those who discharge their duties become distinguished for their talents; those who give their utmost loyalty become distinguished for their remonstrances. Receiving ranks and having their merits recorded, even lowly men from common neighborhoods become those to whom multitudes look up. Those who bring peace to the central realm become distinguished for their civil achievements; those who repel the Yi and Di become distinguished for their martial achievements. How could they themselves fail to gain honor? Such is the way that, in planning for their state, they do not leave themselves out. Thus, although serving the ruler is a means of bringing the ruler to fulfillment, is it not also a means of fulfilling oneself? In the affairs of the world, the greatest concerns are that ritual teaching should fail to reach people and that the distinctions of status and duty should remain unsettled. Once the distinctions between superior and inferior are established, the means by which they fulfill one another naturally arise. How could this depend upon forced effort? Thus the text here says: “Taking the ruler as one’s model is a means of governing oneself; sustaining the ruler is a means of securing oneself; serving the ruler is a means of distinguishing oneself.” The Doctrine of the Mean says: “By honoring the worthy, one avoids perplexity; by respecting the great ministers, one avoids confusion; by treating the assembled officials with sympathetic consideration, one receives an ample return of propriety from the gentlemen.” If this is so, how could the ruler fail his ministers, or the ministers fail their ruler? Thus, when superior and inferior are in mutual accord, virtue and achievement are brought to fulfillment. Can those who become rulers and ministers in later ages fail to take this as their mirror?

Music was the means by which the former kings gave fitting expression to joy; armies and execution axes were the means by which the former kings gave fitting expression to anger. Thus the joy and anger of the former kings each found their proper objects. When they rejoiced, all under Heaven joined in harmony with them; when they were angry, the violent and rebellious feared them. In the Way of the former kings, ritual and music may indeed be called magnificent.

Wang Tingzuo.

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭文批予亦想見禮樂之盛
考試官教諭張批莊重
考試官教授黃批雅暢
聖王以禮樂而著情之公必原其效而賛其大
也甚矣禮樂之道之大也然則聖王所以公其
情而感人心者舍此其何以哉樂記君子意謂
有無私之德者而後可以成無爲之化不觀諸
先王之世乎是故雅頌干戚樂之謂也先王善
端造於自然和順積於罔間不能不喜動於中
===
矣於是被諸聲容以顯其忻喜歡愛之懷軍旅
鈇鉞禮之謂也先王事有弗如吾意化有未愜
于衷不得不怒發於外矣於是詰爾戎兵以昭
其神武不殺之德夫樂以飾喜是以道制欲好
非私好樂以天下也禮以飾怒是以理奉天惡
非私惡憂以天下也喜焉既中其節則以順感
順聞之者父子和親君臣和敬五刑不必用矣
怒焉既當其類則以序召序見之者暴民不作
諸侯賓服兵革不必試矣由是觀之先王之道

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
法制固非一端不過末節耳而其大者則在至
禮不讓而天下自治禮不極其隆乎禁令雖非
一事徒爲文具耳而其要者則在至樂無聲而
天下自和樂不極其盛乎是知始也以禮樂而
治吾之情終也以禮樂而化人之心自非聖王
建中和之極安能臻此無爲之治耶嗟夫禮樂
之在天下固不可一日無特在舉而措之何如
耳故嘗論三代而上治出於一而禮樂達於天
下三代而降治出於二而禮樂爲虛文彼謂天
===
下未定不宜以興禮樂者惡足以知之雖然隱
於人心者歷古今未始亡其必有待於至德乎
先儒曰王道純則禮樂興良有以夫
第貳場
論
脩己以安百姓
陳扆
考試官教諭張批發敏學無餘蘊想見聖人
當時告子路之心

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授黃批意格不凡文詞雅鬯錄之
君子能使天下相安於大順之化其敬德之功
至矣天下之人雖異而此敬之德則同夫惟其
本同也使加於民者不若身之所藏則吾心已
失之乖戾而大本不立矣大本不立吾知推之
天下將必扞格而不通烏能使之弗我悖哉倡
之而愈悖是塞天下之望其治始病治之病君
子自爲之也豈民之罪乎固雖君子有病天下
之心而肯終俾一夫之不獲眞有以病天下之
===
治耶知天下之病在塞之也塞之則不可以不
通通之則不可以不順然所以順之者亦惟立
極以爲之先耳夫立極豈有出於一敬之外哉
蓋敬則脩己者此也及物者亦此也聖德神化
人與我自然誠一無間純而又乂而融會貫通
莫不各得其所而皆囿於範圍之內矣夫是之
謂大同夫是之謂安嗚呼大同之道豈易言哉
必若古之蕩蕩如也熈熈如也皞皞如也而後
可謂之安然地如此其遠勢易隔也俗如此其

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
殊情易否也動如此其衆分易暌也以是不可
齊之勢乘之以不可挽之情間之以不可比之
分苟無道以聯屬之吾恐動之而莫則言之而
莫信雖日令月申家喻戸曉庭除之間尚不能
行於妻子況州里乎況羣黎百姓乎何者天下
之治本於道天下之道原於心天下之心統於
敬敬者存心之要也心者握道之樞也道者運
治之機也故己者民之則敬者德之聚包内外
徹上下兼遠近貫始終未見有異之者在易之
===
壯曰雷在天上大壯君子以非禮勿履坤曰直
方大不習無不利夫動容中禮則高極於天敬
直于方則大極於地孰謂敬之用不廣乎用之
廣者體之同也體同則本通也本通則本從也
以其本通本從者而使之通而使之從猶引水
以流濕引火以就燥有不沛然熾然者乎若使
獨謀其身則是聲色貨利之私而已雖曰將從
其所好也但恐劫奪之敎施而與吾爲敵者紛
紛耳矣豈能乆而安哉此君子所以不敢自異

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
以孤立於上者正欲觀民以觀我無人無己由
克復以造至仁推致曲以至動變耳是故姦聲
亂色不留聰明淫樂慝禮不接心術惰慢邪僻
之氣不設於身體不覩不聞莫見莫顯參前倚
衡所其無逸而四德在我罔不實七情在我罔
不公五倫在我罔不全凡躬行於上者皆由順
正以行其義由是而靜虛動直心平氣和其所
施爲無不各當允爲人極之主譬之天地至誠
無息而萬物各正性命矣惟聖同天亦豈强有
===
作爲哉自家而及其國自國而及其天下於是
有偏爲爾德者矣於是有無敢作好作惡者矣
於是有允升大猷者矣於是有不言而喻不行
而至莫知誰之所爲者矣强弱智愚老幼疾病
鰥寡孤獨極天地之所覆載親賢樂利各足其
欲薰爲太和之世矣彼謂勢之易隔者不至是
而協乎情之易否者不至是而泰乎分之易睽
者不至是而合乎歡忻交通雖四靈出萬物育
天地位皆由此而致之矣此之謂體信達順此

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
之謂篤恭而天下平此之謂身正而天下歸易
曰天下之動貞夫一書曰敬脩其可願禮曰毋
不敬其致一也嗚呼夫子一言足以盡天下之
道如此而子路猶少之豈知君子合一之學至
微而至彰至約而至博哉彼潔己而忘人責人
而恕己是隘與私者之所爲也而謂君子之道
如是乎徵之於古堯之欽明而黎民於變舜之
恭己而四方風動禹之祗台而地平天成湯之
懋敬而兆民允殖文之緝熈而西土冒怙武之
===
敬義而四海永清其脩己同也其安百姓亦同
也雖然沙石不能使之生寒谷不能使之煖在
天地固所不免而聖人之心曷嘗足乎噫此堯
舜之所以病也夫堯舜之病非病其脩己也病
其勢之所不能者耳旣曰勢之所不能豈能終
病乎堯舜也哉使堯舜而可病則天地亦將病
之矣是故君子惟有自反而巳
表
擬宋以程頤爲崇政殿說書謝表〔元祐元〕

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄

年
朱文質

允宜
考試官教諭張批麗而則規而婉佳士佳士

title: 嘉靖十三年雲貴鄉試錄
text:
履泰承元
大道神凝
至文天啓謂萬幾之始道在求賢故蒞政之
初人惟用舊嘉禾連茹青苗之病蔕咸除
威鳳鳴陽白髮之老臣尚在
聖學重
經筵之講
清朝精輔導之官乾德右文舊章可紀寶元
昭治故事如新昔建官以惟賢豈容輕授
今居乘而辭負終懼輿評竊念臣頤河洛
衡茆山泉野服安貧姱節初受學于濂溪
崇正黜浮嘗上書于

仕前承校書之
